543273|2026-06.headline: KMEW Q1 FY27 revenue rose 138% YoY to INR115.41 crore and PAT to INR62.75 crore, driven by one-off-heavy dredging execution.
543273|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR115.41 crore (+138% YoY), EBITDA INR73.41 crore (+258% YoY, ~64% margin) and PAT INR62.75 crore (+466% YoY, ~54% margin). Management attributed the quarter to dredging execution at JNPA (capital rock dredging, completed) and Pondicherry Port (maintenance dredging). Management said revenue and profitability are project-driven and vary by quarter. FY27 growth guidance was raised to "northwards of 60%" from an earlier 30-40%. The company also secured a INR62.40 crore IWAI hybrid ferry contract and raised INR150 crore via preferential issue plus a INR100 crore block deal.

Q4 FY26 + Q1 FY27 combined average PAT margin (as cited by CEO)

financial_highlights.value: More than INR1,300 crore: dredging ~INR240 crore, charter & hire ~INR850 crore, shipbuilding ~INR240 crore

segments.name: Dredging
segments.commentary: Core segment and main revenue driver this quarter from JNPA capital rock dredging (River Pearl 47, completed) and Pondicherry maintenance dredging (River Pearl 18). Dredging order book ~INR240 crore; management expects ~INR200 crore to execute in FY27.

segments.name: Charter & hire
segments.commentary: Recurring revenue from tugs, mooring, pilot, patrol, survey vessels under multiyear port contracts; order book ~INR850 crore across 15 contracts. Management says it is 3-5% of revenue currently.

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Order book ~INR240 crore across 4 contracts, including IWAI contract for 10 hybrid electric 20-seat ferries (INR62.40 crore, ~10 months, built at Saphale yard). Currently ~9% of revenue; 42 third-party vessels and 5 captive vessels under construction.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now guided to northwards of 60% YoY, up from earlier 30-40%.
Dredging revenue for FY27 expected to exceed FY26 levels; management expects INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging order book to execute this year.
Target revenue of INR1,000 crore in FY29; management described it as the next milestone.
Shipbuilding expected to scale significantly from Q4 FY27 after Phase 1 of Saphale yard (14 vessels per year at Phase 1, 18 at full build-out); Phase 1 operational by end of FY27.
Operating (EBITDA) margins guided at 35-40% across segments; management said dredging margins will expand with volumes and it does not expect ~48-63% margins to persist.
FY29 revenue mix target: dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, charter ~5%.
capex_capacity: Capex of close to INR1,000 crore over roughly the next 1.5 years: ~INR250 crore for Green Tugs and green vessels, ~INR450 crore for dredging, balance for shipyard and shipbuilding.
Adding larger TSHDs, CSDs, backhoe dredgers and water injection dredgers; new dredgers of 5,000-7,000 cubic metre capacity cited for deep-sea (Samudra Manthan) work.
Saphale shipyard: Phase 1 to Phase 3 build-out to ~18 vessels per annum; Phase 1 alone 14 vessels.
Portfolio under construction: 10 accommodation boats, 10 work boats, 4 CSD vessels, 2 60-ton bollard pull Green Tugs, 10 hybrid electric passenger ferries.
demand_pricing: Management said dredging faces very little to no competition; it is selective, requiring entry barriers to be met, and targets EBITDA margins of 35-40%.

Bid pipeline results expected in 30-45 days; dredging bids to be executed over 3 years. Maintenance dredging additions of INR100-120 crore in FY27, rising to more than INR250 crore from next year; capital dredging additions ~INR70 crore in FY27 and ~INR150 crore next year.
Historical bid hit rate above 50% over the last 11 years; management said it cannot assume this will continue.
Management attributed peer DCI's margin trend to older equipment needing refurbishment, while KMEW's fleet is more efficiently utilised.
Green Tug contracts are with Visakhapatnam and V.O. Chidambaranar ports, 15-year fixed charter regardless of utilisation; EBITDA margin cited at 75% for Green Tug.
Export shipbuilding inquiries from Europe for ~3,000 DWT vessels under evaluation; payment terms still being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 growth guidance including the INR60 crore revenue shift from last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier guidance was 30-40% YoY; management now sees potential northwards of 60% for FY27 on order book momentum.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ~INR1,300 crore order book executes in FY27 and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging book is expected in FY27. Management said margins will expand, not contract, though not at the 63% operating margin seen in Q1, which it described as not guidance (35-40% stays the guide).

qa_highlights.question: Why are KMEW's dredging margins rising while DCI's are falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCI has older equipment needing refurbishment, while KMEW is better sweating its assets for efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Subcontracting expense trend?
qa_highlights.answer: FY23-24 subcontracting was high because of a JV structure where KMEW was lead partner. Now projects are executed individually; FY26 subcontracting expected at 5-6% of turnover, mainly shipbuilding and ancillary boats.

qa_highlights.question: Dredging vs shipbuilding mix in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dredging 45-50%, shipbuilding 40-45%, chartering ~5%. Shipbuilding pre-subsidy margins 15-20%, post-subsidy expected to go beyond 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Is shipbuilding captive or third party, and how is working capital funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 5 captive vessels (3 tugs, 2 boats) and ~42 third-party vessels. Working capital funded from stage payments (every 10-50% milestone), with no further loans needed; shipbuilding subsidy of 15-20% comes on delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Is dredging a moat given privatisation of ports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disagreed, citing perpetual government demand, DCI's 50-year role and tender structure (domestic below INR250 crore, international above).

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margins (~64% EBITDA, ~54% PAT) are driven by one-off-heavy JNPA capital rock dredging and Pondicherry maintenance dredging; management says results are project-driven and vary by quarter, so track whether Q2 FY27 margins normalise toward the 35-40% EBITDA guide.

FY27 growth guidance raised to northwards of 60% depends on ~INR200 crore of the INR240 crore dredging order book executing this year and on bid pipeline conversion; bid results were said to arrive in 30-45 days, and management said it cannot assume the historical >50% hit rate continues.

Shipbuilding ramp depends on Saphale yard Phase 1 (14 vessels per year) being operational by end FY27 and on shipbuilding scaling from Q4 FY27; the INR62.40 crore IWAI ferry contract runs about 10 months.

Capex of close to INR1,000 crore over about 1.5 years, funded after the INR150 crore preferential issue and INR100 crore block deal; monitor capex pace and cash generation against the INR1,000 crore FY29 revenue target.

Competitive moat questioned: management says dredging faces little to no competition, but a shareholder argued privatisation of ports could allow private dredging; also export shipbuilding inquiries from Europe (~3,000 DWT) have payment terms still under negotiation.
key_quotes: So, our EBITDA margins, we have been guiding at 35% to 40%.
It will not be the same as 63% operating margin. It is not the guidance, we've always guided between 35% to 40%.
We believe the order book is streaming up well, and there is a potential in northwards of 60% for the current year now.
Dredging business is a perpetual business.

It was noticeably cautious on the Q1 margin level, calling it project-driven and not guidance, and it was evasive on specifics such as the Green Tug IRR (referred to the IR team) and the timing of export orders.

543275|2026-03.headline: Anupam FY26 consolidated revenue rose 65% to INR2,384 crores, with Q4 PAT of INR56 crores versus INR63 crores a year earlier.
543275|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the highest revenue year for Anupam, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR2,384 crores (up 65% YoY) and EBITDA including other income of INR543 crores (23% margin). Q4 consolidated total income rose 26% YoY to INR639 crores, but EBITDA fell to INR141 crores from INR150 crores and PAT fell to INR56 crores from INR63 crores; Q4 includes Tanfac and only 1 month and 2 days of Jayhawk. Management announced a definitive agreement to acquire a 43.3% to 48.2% stake in Bliss GVS Pharma plus an open offer for up to 26%, and said the last leg of capex (INR315 crores) is complete with no major capex planned. Operating cash flow reached INR334 crores on working capital release.

guidance_outlook: Standalone revenue growth of 20% to 30% CAGR over the next 3 to 5 years is the target, after 60% to 70% growth in FY26.
Blended EBITDA margins expected to stay near FY26 levels (about 24% standalone, per Q&A); management sees upward bias from pharma and polymer but declined to guide until products ramp up.
Standalone tax rate expected to be around 25% going forward.
Working capital expected to keep improving in FY27; pro forma consolidated working capital about 215 to 220 days, and about 240 to 250 days excluding Jayhawk.

Bliss GVS synergies expected to show in CDMO projects within 6 to 12 months, with more by 18 months. Deal expected to be EPS accretive from day 1; closing timeline 2 to 3 months, subject to SEBI approval and open offer.
Pro forma group revenue above INR4,000 crores and consolidated EBITDA about INR834 crores (Anupam INR1,676 crores, Tanfac INR711 crores, Jayhawk about INR722 crores, Bliss INR927 crores).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of INR315 crores completed the last leg of the capex programme; all plants are now commercialised.
No major capex is planned as current capacity covers near-term growth. Standalone maintenance capex guided at INR50 to 75 crores (including efficiency programmes).
Standalone gross block of about INR2,500 to 2,600 crores; management sees potential to support about INR3,500 crores of revenue from this block.
Bliss GVS currently runs at about 30% utilisation on revenue of about INR1,000 crores; management targets 60% to 70%.
Separate Halol capex of about INR250 crores for a CDMO project from a large multinational pharma customer; management expects asset turnover of 4x to 5x and gave no detailed timeline.
demand_pricing: Order book is about INR14,000 crores. Management estimates INR1,700 to 1,800 crores of annual incremental revenue from the pipeline on a 6 to 7 year average basis, partly agro and partly polymer.
Pharma growth is expected from Indian organic demand on a standalone basis; Jayhawk and Bliss synergies are additional.
Jayhawk shares some common customers with Anupam, and there are complementary customers; Bliss has overlap on the CDMO side.
Anupam has no African exposure; Bliss has meaningful Africa exposure, per management's comments.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the Bliss GVS acquisition and whether current management will continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management continues. Bliss runs at about 30% utilisation and could reach 60% to 70%. The deal adds a full pharma platform from KSM to finished dosage. Tanfac will remain a separate entity.

qa_highlights.question: Pro forma revenue, merger or delisting plans, synergies, funding and EPS impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Pro forma group revenue above INR4,000 crores and EBITDA about INR834 crores. No merger or delisting planned. Funding is about INR300 crores of NCDs in a wholly owned subsidiary, with the balance as non-controlling, non-voting quasi-equity. Deal to be EPS accretive from day 1.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone growth trajectory and business mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone grew over 60% to 70% this year. Management targets 20% to 30% CAGR over 3 to 5 years, led by pharma and polymer with agro also growing.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels and interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated gross debt about INR1,500 crores, net about INR1,100 crores; over two-thirds is working capital loans. Adding INR300 crores gives net debt of about INR1,400 to 1,500 crores against EBITDA above INR650 crores on the stated basis. Interest cost not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block capacity, maintenance capex and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross block can support about INR3,500 crores of revenue. Maintenance capex INR50 to 75 crores. Blended margins guided to stay near FY26 levels, with upward bias from pharma and polymer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Bliss promoter sell and what is the structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited succession planning by the senior promoter, who wants cash for his family. The promoter chose Anupam over other offers. Stake range 43.3% to 48.2% lets the seller keep about 5%.

risks_watch: Q4 EBITDA and PAT declined YoY despite higher revenue; Q4 includes only 1 month and 2 days of Jayhawk.
Debt rising to about INR1,400 to 1,500 crores net on a pro forma basis with the INR300 crores NCD; interest cost not disclosed.

Standalone tax rate guided down to about 25%, which supports PAT.

543275|2026-06.headline: Anupam Rasayan Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR655 crore (TI +36% YoY), EBITDA INR175 crore at 26% margin, PAT up only 6% to INR51 crore.
543275|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 36% YoY to INR667.5 crore, with EBITDA up 35% to INR174.9 crore and margin steady at about 26%. PAT grew 6% to INR51.2 crore as higher depreciation (partly Jayhawk's older depreciation policy) and interest absorbed the EBITDA gain. Management said the major capex cycle is complete and Jayhawk contributed roughly 20-22% of revenue at a 19-20% EBITDA margin. The Bliss GVS Pharma open offer closed on August 10, with completion expected by the first half of September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the API plant acquisition flagged in the last call?
qa_highlights.answer: Still exploratory with nothing to share. Management will work with Bliss management on any acquisitions once Bliss completes.

qa_highlights.question: Bliss completion timeline and pending approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: SEBI approval received and open offer closed on August 10. Procedural steps remain; completion expected by the first half of September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Jayhawk contribution and margin this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20-22% of revenue (around INR145 crore), with EBITDA margin of 19-20% (around INR30 crore) and PAT of about INR9 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone EBITDA margin 24-26%; consolidated 22-24%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Anupam fund Jayhawk capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No requirement is foreseen; Jayhawk is well capitalised and unlevered, with only limited repurposing or replacement capex.

qa_highlights.question: How is Bliss funded?
qa_highlights.answer: A fully owned subsidiary will take about INR300 crore of debt, with the balance funded through an equity-linked instrument that Anupam can buy out at any time. Management said Bliss has over INR200 crore of cash flow and no debt, so no large external capital is needed for later API acquisitions.

segments.name: Candere

guidance_outlook: Plan to open 150 showrooms in FY27 across Kalyan, Candere and the new regional brand; Candere share about 50-55 of these.
Aim to make India non-GML debt zero in FY27, possibly by H1 FY27, but management declined to guide firmly on timing.

Non-GML repayment of INR300 crores expected to save about INR30 crores in interest in FY27, at roughly 9-10%; about INR20 crores of one-off advance tax interest in FY26 adds to the reduction (around INR50 crores total).
Dividend recommended at about INR257 crores, roughly 20% of FY26 net profit, per the announced policy.
Management does not want to guide SSSG above 10% for the next 3-5 years, though recent SSSG has been 20-30%.

Gross margin expected to face YoY pressure from platinum/silver tailwinds that will not repeat; management cited about INR20 crores of silver benefit, with operating leverage and interest savings as offsets.
April 2026 started well despite a high base; Adhik Maas may shift some wedding demand between quarters, though management said revenue is not lost.
capex_capacity: Opened 129 showrooms across Kalyan and Candere in FY26, including the first Kalyan showroom in the UK.

Middle East: 2 new showrooms opened and 5-6 renovated into bigger formats; conversion of 4 FOCO stores to COCO worth about INR200-250 crores of inventory.
Q4 showroom count rose gross by 28 but net by about 4, with management saying only one small Madurai showroom closed and the rest were relocations.
Third regional brand launch in a South state delayed until post-election situation settles.
demand_pricing: Management said SSSG for the South was lower than for non-South in Q4; non-South acceleration continued from Q3.
Akshaya Tritiya sales grew strongly; coin sales were lower than estimated this year, unlike Dhanteras when they exceeded estimates.

Management said customers buy to a rupee budget, so volumes fall as gold prices rise; gold rose about 60-70% over the past year. Consumers were pushed to studded jewellery and lower karat (22K to 18K, 18K to 14K).
Management said gold supply is not a concern, with regular bank inventory and imports via GIFT City's India International Bullion Exchange.
Gold metal loan (GML) in India is capped by bank sanctions; Middle East GML is uncapped and rises with gold prices.
Management said inventory rises by only INR30-40 for every INR100 rise in gold price, to protect ROCE.

qa_highlights.question: Why did South SSSG diverge so sharply from non-South in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said South was lower, partly because its base is higher, and non-South acceleration continued from Q3 and was more pronounced in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-GML debt be fully repaid by H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to be non-GML debt free in FY27 and could do it by H1, but declined to guide on timing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise sequentially, and what is the underlying run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher processing charges and interest on advance tax explain the rise; about INR20 crores is one-off. Non-GML repayment should cut about INR30 crores in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 Adhik Maas period a risk to sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some sales may move between quarters, with possible slower days, but some purchases were preponed; April started well.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin came from silver and platinum, and what is the FY27 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the silver/platinum benefit was about INR20 crores and will not repeat, but operating leverage and interest savings can help. PBT margin for India should stay near 5.5-5.6%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East FOCO-to-COCO conversion's potential cash release?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only 4 showrooms were converted, worth about INR200-250 crores of inventory, and declined to budget any further conversion or cash release.

risks_watch: Gross margin sustainability after platinum and silver gains and the FOCO mix shift; Q4 gross margin reverted to about a 100 bps YoY decline in India, per an analyst.
Q1 FY27 wedding timing around Adhik Maas and tough H2 comparisons on a high base.
Middle East franchise conversion and the Arab investor deal, which is not yet materialised.

543278|2026-06.headline: Kalyan Jewellers Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38% to INR10,008 crore and PAT to INR349 crore, helped by a one-off customs duty gain.
543278|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue (net of bullion) grew 38% YoY to INR10,008 crore, with EBITDA of INR633 crore (vs INR508 crore) and PAT of INR349 crore (vs INR264 crore). India revenue rose to INR8,503 crore and Middle East to about INR1,320 crore, while Candere turned PAT positive at INR2.1 crore. Management attributed part of profit to a one-time customs duty gain of about INR40-41 crore that was passed to customers via old gold exchange offers, and flagged a 0.2-0.3% PBT margin dilution from exchange. Management said the PBT margin for the full year should hold at or above FY26 levels on a conservative basis.

segments.name: India (Kalyan)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8,503 crore (+38% YoY) and EBITDA INR500 crore (+15%); PAT INR321 crore (+25%). Management said non-South markets now contribute 50-60% of revenue.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,320 crore (+29%), EBITDA INR90 crore (vs INR73 crore), profit INR25 crore (vs INR22 crore).

segments.name: Candere (e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR141 crore (vs INR66 crore, roughly double); profit INR2.1 crore vs loss of INR10 crore. Management targets around 50 new Candere stores in FY27 and said Candere stays PAT positive for the year.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 PBT margin expected to be at least in line with FY26 on a conservative basis; exchange dilution of 0.2-0.3% to be offset by cash-for-gold, which is margin accretive.
Customs duty related gain expected at about INR60 crore in Q2 FY27, with some further benefit possible in the running quarter, though management said part may be shared with consumers.
Store expansion target unchanged: 84 Kalyan showrooms and about 50 Candere stores in FY27; H2 is typically heavier than H1. Management cites 70-80 showrooms a year overall.

Non-GML debt to be fully repaid by end-September 2026; second tranche of real estate collaterals to be released thereafter. Management said the company would be debt-free on a non-GML basis in a couple of months.
Recycled gold share to be maintained at 55-60% of revenue going forward.
Real estate sale: agreements signed for two land parcels for about INR102 crore; sale expected to close and proceeds received before end of Q1 FY27 (June quarter).
capex_capacity: Expansion is mainly franchise-led (FOCO model, where the franchisee funds capex and inventory and Kalyan runs the store for a margin share); franchisee ROCE cited at about 14%.
Kalyan ROCE rose to about 20% from the late teens; management expects further improvement from capital-light expansion.

New regional brand Akshaya Thanga Maligai (ATM) for Tamil Nadu: first showroom in Chennai on 21 August 2026, with four more showrooms planned in the following months, including other cities; expansion also to be predominantly FOCO.
Q1 FY27 saw 12 FOCO store openings, per the analyst's question; management confirmed no change to annual targets.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as robust except for about one month of Adhik Maas, when wedding demand slowed in parts of the country. Management said July demand was strong and continuing like Q1, but declined to quantify the trend.
Gold prices corrected about 15-20% over 2-3 months; management said customers buy by budget, so volumes rise when prices fall.
Recycled gold ('Shine with India' campaign) rose to over 46% of revenue in Q1, with June above 55%, as oil-driven forex pressure pushed the company to reduce imported gold.
Cash-for-gold (new product) grew from single-digit share in Q1 to double-digit share as of the call; management said peers are also adopting it.

Exchange transactions are priced at the board rate; cash purchases of old gold are at a discount to spot, which management said is margin accretive. Bullion sales in Q1 were used to fund cash needs of vendors, mainly studded vendors on invoice basis.
Employee cost rose about 54% YoY standalone; management said this is more than the usual annual increment and worth about 0.2-0.3% of revenue, offset by operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any bonus issue planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no bonus share plans as of now.

qa_highlights.question: Ex the one-off gain of INR410 crore, standalone PBT growth was only about 14%, so what drove the margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PBT margin ex-bullion was about 5.1% vs 5.5-5.6% earlier. The gain was partly passed to consumers via exchange offers (INR30-40 crore), exchange dilutes margin by 0.2-0.3%, and platinum/silver one-offs of about 0.2% were absent.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 0.2-0.3% exchange-related dilution persist for the next two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no for full year: cash-for-gold should offset exchange dilution, and it expects FY27 PBT margin at least in line with FY26 on a conservative basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gold price fall boosting volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers come with a budget, so lower gold prices mechanically raise volumes; wedding demand cannot pause more than 2-3 weeks, and discretionary demand may pause about 1-1.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much customs duty benefit is expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60 crore in Q2, with some benefit possible in the running quarter but part to be shared with consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Candere?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Candere has been PAT positive since 2H FY26, will stay positive in FY27, and will add about 50 stores with focus on inventory throughput in existing stores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost increase one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not one-time; it is above the usual annual increment, occurs once every few years, and operating leverage should absorb it.

risks_watch: Margin: exchange-led volumes dilute PBT margin by 0.2-0.3%; the full-year margin target depends on cash-for-gold scaling up.
One-off customs duty gains (about INR41 crore in Q1, about INR60 crore expected in Q2) may not recur and partly go to consumers.
Gold price volatility (15-20% correction) may pause discretionary demand and push customers to change grammage/price points.
Employee cost up about 54% YoY standalone; watch whether operating leverage offsets it.
Execution of non-GML debt repayment by September 2026 and the real estate sale proceeds.
Management declined to comment on governance questions raised in the press about related-party transactions; an open overhang for investors.
ATM's ramp-up and whether the regional format can scale beyond the first five stores.
543278|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth and demand, citing strong July trading and a 38% revenue rise. Somewhat evasive on quantifying the July trend, the Adhik Maas impact and governance questions, and reliant on cash-for-gold to offset margin dilution, which is not yet proven.
key_quotes: Q1 performance has been very satisfactory given the overall context.
The quarter has started off very well despite the volatility in gold prices.
Candere has been PAT positive for the first quarter and should continue for this financial year.
For the full year, I don't think there will be an impact. Even on a conservative basis, I think we'll be able to maintain the PBT margins of the previous year.

543279|2026-03.headline: Suryoday SFB FY26 PAT rose to ₹152 crores from ₹115 crores; management targets FY27 PAT above ₹300 crores, with credit cost guided at 70-80 bps.
543279|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of disciplined execution and gradual stabilisation after elevated microfinance credit costs. Q4 showed improvement: inclusive finance slippages fell to about ₹74 crores from ₹116 crores in Q3 (the call also cited ₹106 crores on a total-bank basis), and monthly disbursements returned to about ₹500 crores. FY26 net total income rose 10.2% to ₹1,458 crores and PAT to ₹152 crores, with GNPA at 6.5% (₹864 crores) and CRAR at 20.5%. Management guided to 30%+ growth, a 1.2% ROA for Q1 FY27 rising to 1.6% by Q4, and a cost-to-income ratio of 67-68%.

financial_highlights.value: ₹542 crores, of which ₹508 crores receivable from CGFMU

financial_highlights.metric: Mortgage book incl. micro home loans (Mar'26)

segments.name: Inclusive finance (microfinance)
segments.commentary: Shifting from JLG to individual Vikas loans, now 75% of the inclusive finance portfolio and growing about 40-45% YoY. Current-book collection efficiency is about 99.7%; slippages were about ₹74 crores in Q4 versus ₹116 crores in Q3.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Portfolio ₹1,819 crores, up 36% YoY. Stress is concentrated in an Odisha pocket; management says ex-Odisha metrics are about 2x better than market CV stress.

segments.name: Mortgages and micro home loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage book ₹3,013 crores, up 38% YoY. Stress in older mortgage and MHL portfolios in Karnataka was about 4% of the portfolio, with a few high-ticket LAP cases (₹3 crores+) in SARFAESI resolution.

segments.name: Digital products (credit on UPI, secured cards, digital MSME loans)
segments.commentary: Credit on UPI outstanding about ₹200 crores with 97-98% of dues paid; 90+ DPD about 1.5%. Of 10 lakh prequalified customers, about 5.5 lakh sanctioned and about 3 lakh utilised.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 ROA guided at about 1.2%, rising to 1.6% by Q4 FY27; Q4 FY26 ROA was 1.1%.
FY27 PAT target above ₹300 crores (about 2x FY26), per management's presentation.
FY27 credit cost of about 1%, per CFO earlier in the call; later revised to 70-80 bps for the coming year (FY27) in response to a follow-up question.
Cost-to-income ratio of 67-68% for FY27, with a stated goal of staying below 70%.
Quarterly slippages targeted at ₹75-90 crores; GNPA guided to about 3% for FY27 with CGFMU claims and write-offs as the main drivers.
NIM to be range-bound at 8-9%, with an uptick possible as the paying book grows; current NIM about 50 bps suppressed. Growth targeted at 20-30% of asset size.
capex_capacity: CGFMU claims: about ₹510 crores claimable, of which about ₹450 crores (up to ₹475 crores) is expected in FY27; the first cohort claim is targeted for Q1 or Q2, with the FY25 cohort the largest.
CGFMU cover premium expected at about ₹100-110 crores for FY27 (about ₹23 crores per quarter currently).
Fundraise: Tier 2 is the likely first step, possibly within FY27. An equity raise is more contingent, given the stock trades below book (P/B under 1) and the need to protect incumbent shareholders.
Branch expansion is kept rationalised and low-cost; corporate headcount is held flat, with hiring concentrated in frontline roles.
demand_pricing: Digital deposits are about 50% of net incremental deposit flows, with average ticket about ₹1.25 lakh and at least two deposits per customer on average.
Cost of funds has hardened; elevated Q4 rates have not come down as in prior years. The bank uses a mix of deposits and refinancing lines to manage funding.
Management sees unmet demand as large, especially where smaller MFIs have exited; the top 10-15 MFIs hold about 19% market share.
Individual-loan ticket sizes are being raised selectively; tenor is moving toward 3 years for high-ticket loans, with a portion above ₹1 lakh under review.

qa_highlights.question: Given the stronger Q4 performance, is the 1.2% Q1 ROA target realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said yes: the paying book is higher entering Q1, impaired book should exit on CGFMU claims, and Q1 typically has the most PSLC sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state slippage level and retail-asset (RA) slippage guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said RA slippage could settle near 1.25% over the next two halves as CV Odisha stress and high-ticket mortgage cases are resolved. Bank-wide slippages are targeted at ₹75-90 crores a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the CGFMU claim will be filed, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹510 crores is claimable, with ₹450 crores expected in FY27 and the timing (Q1 or Q2) still open. None filed in April; May is unlikely.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bank raising capital, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank is raising capital to sustain 30%+ growth, with CRAR around 20% as the internal comfort level. Tier 2 is most likely first, and an equity raise is subject to shareholder considerations.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIMs expand as the paying book grows?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided NIM to 8-9% and agreed NIM is suppressed by about 50 bps, with an uptick expected as non-paying assets convert to paying.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost should be expected for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided FY27 credit cost to 70-80 bps. Management also said downside risk from the Middle East war and diesel prices would be watched, with CV impact only if diesel rises above 10-15%.

543279|2026-06.headline: Suryoday SFB Q1 FY27: GNPA 6.5%, NNPA 1.2% after INR387 crore CGFMU claim; ROA about 1.6% helped by INR46 crore PSL income.

Bank-level slippages fell to INR92 crore from INR106 crore QoQ, and MFI slippages fell to INR53 crore from INR73 crore. Other income was lifted by about INR90 crore of PSL/other income plus INR46 crore of PSL certificate sales (INR1,600 crore sold), which management said will not recur at this scale in Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance: credit cost 0.8–1.0%, ROE 13–14% range, ROA of about 1.6% by Q4, and cost-to-income of 67–70%.

segments.commentary: PAR rose to 11.5% from 10.1% QoQ, attributed to fuel prices and load availability. About 75–80% of the book is used CVs. Management expects normalisation from Q2/Q3 after monsoon.

segments.name: Mortgages and secured retail
segments.commentary: Secured retail growing 30–35% YoY. Mortgages present in under 25% of branches, targeted at 40–45% by year-end. Some mortgage slippages are being resolved through legal process.

segments.name: Digital (CLOU/UPI credit line, digital deposits, digital MSME)
segments.commentary: Digital deposits INR2,222 crore with average daily accretion of INR6 crore. UPI credit customers crossed 9 lakh; CLOU convenience fee income INR18 crore against about INR13 crore related cost. Digital MSME disbursements INR59 crore.

ROA guided at about 1.6% in Q4 FY27 with no change to the start-of-year guidance; management said Q2 PSL income will be lower.
Steady-state ROE 13–14%, with a target of 0.5–1% YoY improvement over the next couple of years.
PSL income guided at INR10–15 crore in each of Q2 and Q3, and INR15–20 crore in Q4.

demand_pricing: Management said the MFI cycle has turned, but it is staying cautious on growth and will not treat the recovery as a reason to grow aggressively.

IBPC funding reopened at roughly 5% after the MFI book improved.
Deposit costs: SA cost of funds 5.5% (from 5.7%); FD cost about 8.1%. FD rates have not eased.
VL (individual loan) yield about 25–25.25%; secured assets yield about 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of about INR147 crore looks high. What is the steady-state run-rate for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income included about INR90 crore of PSL income plus INR46 crore from selling INR1,600 crore of PSL certificates. Q2 and Q3 PSL income is expected at INR10–15 crore each, and Q4 at INR15–20 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1.6% ROA reach 1.8–1.9% by Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 included about INR40 crore of PSL income, and the next two quarters will not have similar PSL opportunities, so the 1.6% ROA is not a base for linear increase.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to yield on non-NPA advances (17.2% to 16.1%)?

qa_highlights.question: Why did slippages stay elevated and what is the resolution path?

543279|2026-09.headline: Suryoday Q2 FY27: gross advances up 34.6% YoY to INR14,972 crores; gross NPA fell to 2.9% from 6.5% after INR596 crores write-offs and OTS.

543280|2026-03.headline: Nazara FY26 EBITDA rose 66% to INR 255 crore, with Q4 EBITDA margin at 19.5%, helped by a one-time INR 31 crore Rusk Media gain.

Q4 revenue was INR 398 crore and EBITDA INR 78 crore (19.5% margin). Gaming rose to 90% of EBITDA in FY26 from 56% in FY25. Bluetile and BestPlay acquisition was completed in the quarter but will be consolidated only from Q1 FY27, pending Spanish FDI approval expected in 3-4 weeks. Management guided to growth in revenue and EBITDA for FY27 without numerical guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NODWIN fundraising and IPO plan, and will Nazara monetise its stake?

543280|2026-06.headline: Nazara Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 429 crore and EBITDA INR 46 crore, with a PAT loss of INR 82 crore; Bluetile/BestPlay acquisition restructured to $303 million all-cash.
543280|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR 429 crore and EBITDA INR 46 crore, with a PAT loss of INR 82 crore driven by associate losses (about INR 62 crore share of loss) and impairment, mainly on the Moonshine remnant value. Excluding NODWIN's deconsolidation, comparable revenue grew about 9% YoY. Gaming revenue rose 14% YoY to INR 275 crore at a 19.5% EBITDA margin, with heavier user acquisition spend compressing margins at Bluetile, Kiddopia and Curve. Management restructured the Bluetile and BestPlay deal to a fixed $303 million all-cash price, with $89 million at closing and $214 million by 1 April 2027, and named Bluetile founder Raymond Stauffer as Nazara CEO from 1 September 2026.

543280|2026-09.headline: Nazara Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 803 crore (up 53% YoY) and EBITDA rose 93% to INR 120 crore, helped by Bluetile and BestPlay consolidation from 1 August 2026.
543280|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter including Bluetile and BestPlay, consolidated from 1 August 2026, and Nazara reported record revenue of INR 803 crore with EBITDA margin up 311 bps to 14.9%. Gaming is now 82% of revenue and effectively all EBITDA before corporate costs. Organic gaming growth was modest at 11% revenue and 17% EBITDA, with the acquired mobile businesses doing most of the lifting. Management, under a new CEO, CFO and Executive Director, framed the next year around platform centres of excellence, AI adoption and gaming focus, and declined to give numerical growth targets. Non-core assets (NODWIN, AdTech, Absolute Sports and others) are to be monetised opportunistically.

543283|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated SSSG rose to 14.4% (Q3: 8.2%) with dine-in volumes up ~43%, and management targets 9-10% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin in FY27.
543283|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest operating quarter in recent history, with consolidated revenue of INR360 crores (+23.1% YoY) and every segment and channel growing at double-digit rates. Growth was entirely volume-led with no price increase in Q4, while gross margin fell about 300 bps YoY to 65.5% due to segment mix, value campaigns in weaker dayparts and Middle East input inflation. Management says gross margin bottomed in February 2026 and recovered about 100 bps in March and April. Net debt was about INR100-102 crores, and FY27 guidance includes 40 new restaurants, around INR140 crores of capex and a 9-10% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin.

financial_highlights.change: ~850 bps better than FY25 negative trend
vs ~68.5% in Q4 FY25 (~300 bps lower)

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin (Q4 FY26)
Mature portfolio restaurant operating margin (Q4 FY26)
Back-end cost as % of revenue (Q4 FY26)

segments.name: Barbeque Nation India
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG 16.7% (Q3: 8.3%) and dine-in volume +47% YoY; more than 60% of dine-in transactions now via own digital channels (Q3: 53%). Lower per-cover spend than other segments diluted average realisation.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation International
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +27.5% YoY, SSSG 5.5%, dine-in volume ~+27%; pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin ~24.4%. Added 4 restaurants in FY26 (most ever); 3 under construction in Middle East and Southeast Asia. Two of ~8 restaurants (Bahrain, Dubai) impacted by West Asia crisis.

segments.name: Premium CDR (Salt and Toscano)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +23.3% YoY, SSSG 7%, dine-in volume ~+27%. Network grew from 30 to 42 restaurants in FY26; mature store pre-Ind AS ROM 18.4% in Q4 and 20.1% for FY26, while new-store cohort margins compressed in newer markets (Mumbai, Delhi).

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin target of 9-10%, with a path to double-digit margins thereafter; management clarified this is a full-year figure, not an exit rate.

FY27 SSSG internal aim: mid-single-digit to double-digit on a normalised base; management says it internally aims to cross double-digit full-year SSSG, and blended premium CDR plus International SSSG at early double-digit.
H1 FY27 SSSG expected to hold at Q4 levels, with possible slight improvement in Q1; management said Q1 and Q2 momentum is continuing.

Gross margin recovery of 100-150 bps in FY27 over Q4 levels, targeting a 67-68% medium-term band; mature ROM expected to rise from ~16% (H2 FY26 basis) to 17-18%; new-store drag 1.5-1.8%; consolidated ROM 15.5-16.5%.
Back-end cost to fall from 7.1% to ~6.5% of revenue in FY27 and ~6% over the longer term.
Plan to open 40 new restaurants in FY27 (network 300+ by end FY27) and reach 400-425 restaurants by FY30; 11 restaurants under construction to open in Q1-Q2 FY27.

FY27 capex of ~INR140 crores (30 India restaurants at ~INR2.5 crores, 5 International at ~INR6 crores, 5 premium CDR at ~INR3 crores, ~INR20 crores maintenance); expansion to be funded mainly from internal accruals, with net debt expected to stay flat.
Management said FY27 full-year revenue growth of 22-25% is reasonable if SSSG is double-digit and store expansion is 12-13% (answered 'on a full year basis, yes').
capex_capacity: FY26: 35 new restaurants added (14 in Q4), taking network to 262; 32 net additions versus 14 net in the prior two years combined.
FY27 plan: 40 new restaurants (~15% expansion), with 11 under construction and further advanced commercial discussions; FY28 target of 100-125 restaurants over three years (40-45 per year).
Capex plan FY27 ~INR140 crores, of which ~INR120 crores for new stores; International 5 stores at ~INR6 crores each; India 30 stores at ~INR2.5 crores; premium CDR 5 stores at ~INR3 crores.

Management says the 4-session-per-day model allows 3-4 table turns; a 100-seat restaurant can do ~300 covers/day, and peak restaurants do INR12-13 crores (India) and INR11-12 crores (Salt and Toscano).
demand_pricing: Approximately 90% of dine-in volume comes from captive channels (app, website, in-house reservation centre, walk-ins); monthly active users on app and website crossed 1.2 million, up 51% YoY.

Growth was volume-led: Q4 had no price increase. Management says it can recover INR15-20 net realisation per cover through base pricing, group offers and beverage mix, and is pulling back marginally on some campaign offers to full price.

Company-level AOV fell ~14-15% YoY due to mix (higher Barbeque India covers, weaker dayparts); management expects this to persist for two more quarters, then settle at levels similar to the last two quarters.
Delivery revenue grew ~32% YoY, led entirely by transaction growth.
Management is not pursuing discount-led growth that compromises unit economics; no new brand categories or acquisitions planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit SSSG for FY27 achievable given the cautious tone on H2 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects early double-digit SSSG comfortably and that the internal aim is to cross double-digit full-year SSSG, while declining to give formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 9-10% margin target be achieved from the current base, and is the 100-150 bps gross margin recovery net of inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 67-68% gross margin range is after inflation; gross margin gap to FY25 peak of 68.5% is now ~3 pp and expected to narrow to ~1-1.5 pp. Gross margin rose in March and April despite LPG price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 new-store drag on margins persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 new-store drag was 180 bps (vs 120 bps in Q4 FY25) as Q4 was the heaviest opening quarter; management expects drag to narrow as the cohort matures over 12-24 months, stabilising at 1.5-1.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did premium CDR margins fall sharply from Q3 to Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to new restaurants (4 opened in Q4), seasonality (December peak in Q3), one-time setup and liquor costs, and newer markets (Mumbai, Delhi) that take time to build up; mature cohort margins are fine.

qa_highlights.question: How will store expansion avoid the closures seen in FY23?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some Tier 2/3 stores were closed in FY23 but its current operating model works in those markets; FY27 plan of 40 stores is ~15% of the base and comparable to the 35 added in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for International given Middle East disruption and currency effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Two of ~8 restaurants (Bahrain, Dubai) are impacted; both improved month-on-month in April and May. No new Middle East sites reviewed in the last three months; focus is on Southeast Asia.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's per-restaurant revenue and peak capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peak-day capacity is not a constraint: a 4-session day at 100 seats gives 400 covers, about INR9 crores a month at INR750 per cover, and the company will open nearby stores 5-7 km apart when demand grows.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery (100-150 bps) depends on procurement, scale and selective realisation, against input inflation (LPG, utilities, Middle East) and continued value campaigns in weaker dayparts.
Tougher comparison base in H2 FY27 after strong Q3 and Q4 FY26 SSSG (8.2% and 14.4%); management says the planning factors this in.
New-store cohort drag (180 bps in Q4 FY26) and premium CDR margin compression in new markets (Mumbai, Delhi) could delay the mature ROM path.
Middle East (Bahrain, Dubai) and currency headwinds on International; management says it is not signing new sites there for now.
Store-expansion execution (40 stores in FY27, 100-125 over three years) given closures in FY23 Tier 2/3 markets; back-end cost must fall from 7.1% to 6.5% of revenue.
Monitor Q1 FY27 SSSG and gross margin trend, and any change to internal targets flagged for the Q1 results.
key_quotes: Q4 FY'26 has been the strongest operating quarter in our recent history.
I would believe that we would be able to comfortably deliver an early double-digit same-store sales growth. It is just that I'm on the side of caution to give guidance.
We are not chasing discount-led growth that comprises unit economics.
Our internal aim is to take pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin to 9% to 10% in FY'27 with a path towards double-digit margins going forward.
543283|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand momentum and the volume-led recovery, citing two consecutive quarters of strong SSSG and every segment growing double-digit. Cautious on forward guidance: management declined to give formal FY27 SSSG guidance, offering "early double-digit" only as a comfortable expectation and an internal aim, and stressed that the H2 comparison base will be tougher.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin is guided to recover 100-150 bps over Q4 65.5% (medium-term 67-68%), back-end cost falls from 7.1% to ~6.5%, and mature ROM rises to 17-18%, though new-store drag of 1.5-1.8% offsets part of it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: FY26 added 35 restaurants (network 262) and FY27 plan is 40 new stores (~15% of base), with 11 already under construction to open in Q1-Q2 FY27 and ~INR140 crore capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Dine-in volume grew ~43% in Q4 with SSSG at 14.4% and 40 new stores in FY27 (~15% of base), with H1 SSSG guided to hold at Q4 levels.

rows.when: FY28 (100-125 restaurants over three years, 40-45 per year)
rows.why: Capex of ~INR140 crore is already guided for FY27 and a FY28 target of 40-45 stores a year is stated, though no utilisation is cited and management says peak capacity is not a constraint.

rows.why: Gross margin is 65.5% in Q4 (down ~300 bps YoY), back-end cost is 7.1% of revenue against a 6.5% FY27 target, Middle East input inflation persists, and H2 FY27 faces a tougher comparison after SSSG of 8.2% and 14.4%.

rows.label: Mature restaurant ROM expansion to 17-18%

rows.why: Q4 had no price increase and AOV fell ~14-15% YoY on mix; management says it can recover INR15-20 per cover via base pricing, group offers and beverage mix, and expects AOV pressure for two more quarters.

rows.why: Net debt is ~INR100-102 crore at end Q4 FY26 and expansion is to be funded mainly from internal accruals against ~INR140 crore capex, with net debt guided to stay flat.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume-led demand, double-digit SSSG and store expansion, but declined formal FY27 SSSG guidance and flagged a tougher H2 comparison base; analysts pushed on whether double-digit SSSG and the 9-10% margin target are achievable given the cautious H2 tone.

543283|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43.4% YoY to INR426 crores, with same-store sales growth of 28.7% and pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin of 8.1%.
543283|2026-06.overview: United Foodbrands (Barbeque Nation) reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR426 crores, up 43.4% YoY, with consolidated SSSG of 28.7% on top of 14.4% in Q4 FY26. Growth was volume-led (dine-in transactions up 63.5%) with no price increase taken. Pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.1% from about 5.5% in Q4 and roughly 350 bps higher YoY, helped by a 130 bps sequential gross margin recovery in Barbeque Nation India. International gross margin fell on Middle East-linked food inflation, and net debt rose marginally to INR106 crores.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation India
segments.commentary: Same-store sales growth 33.5%, revenue growth 43.4%, dine-in transactions up 68.6%; gross margin up ~130 bps QoQ. Captive digital ecosystem drives 65% of dine-in transactions (from ~61% in Q4); MAUs ~1.4 million, up ~60% YoY.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation International
segments.commentary: Revenue growth 46.6%, SSSG 8.5%, dine-in volume growth 45.2%, gross profit up 40.3%. Restaurant operating margin 18.7%, but gross margin down ~3 pp on Middle East-linked inflation; added 1 UAE restaurant.

segments.name: Premium casual dining (Premium CDR)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth ~36%, SSSG 13.6%, dine-in volume growth ~40%. Mature restaurants deliver restaurant operating margin of upwards of 20%; added 1 and closed 1 restaurant, network unchanged. Q4 FY26 cohort expected to lift segment margin.

guidance_outlook: SSSG expected to moderate through FY27 as comparables tighten, with Q3 and Q4 FY27 lapping the strongest quarter of FY26; management called this a base effect, not weaker demand.

Margin levers for FY27: gross margin recovery in India, mature portfolio ROM expansion, new-store cohort maturation and back-end cost leverage; management did not give a pre-Ind AS double-digit EBITDA margin timeline.
Target of 300 restaurants by FY27 (about 40 additions this year vs ~35 last year); 15 restaurants under construction to operationalise in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex guided at ~INR140 crores (INR120 crores for new outlets, INR20 crores maintenance and ancillary), per the prior guidance reiterated on the call.
Management sees Barbeque Nation India capable of ~600 restaurants at current scale, up from an earlier view of 400-450, given the Big Buffet format in Tier 2/3 markets.
Momentum said to be continuing into July; revenue crossed INR400 crores for the first time, and the quarter ended at about INR425 crores.
capex_capacity: Restaurant count closed Q1 FY27 at 266 after 5 additions; target of 300 by FY27 maintained.
15 restaurants under construction, expected to open in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
Barbeque Nation India store format reduced to ~3,500 sq ft from 4,500 sq ft; newer format's revenue per restaurant said to be among the highest.
Expansion funded largely from internal accruals; borrowings to be kept at prudent levels.
demand_pricing: Growth described as entirely volume-led; no price increase taken in Q1 despite inflation. Average per-cover spend declined due to value initiatives from Q2 FY26 and has now stabilised at Q4 FY26 levels.
Average revenue per mature restaurant is around INR7 crores; management has not given a target for the next step.
Repeat business is ~45-47% of the base, with the new-vs-repeat mix shifting slightly toward new guests. Average bill is ~4.3 pax, and repeat tracking relies on one mobile number per bill.

Delivery growth of 62% was supported by value SKUs across Barbeque Nation, BBQ and Dum Safar brands and by higher marketing spend. Delivery share of mix rose ~2 pp YoY and carries commission and packaging costs of about 30%.
Management described the mature cost base as 'normalised' after recent hires in culinary, marketing and digital; each INR1 per-cover improvement adds about INR1.5 crores of annual cost impact.

financial_highlights.change: ~350 bps YoY; up from ~5.5% in Q4 FY26

qa_highlights.question: How much more market does Big Buffet open up in Tier 3/4 markets, versus two years ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Big Buffet has about 6 quarters of data in Tier 2/3 markets, with some sites as small as 3 lakh population. It sees Barbeque Nation India able to reach about 600 restaurants at current scale, versus an earlier view of 400-450.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the SSSG improvement, by brand?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-led volume strategy began in Barbeque Nation India, then extended to International and premium CDR. Marketing spend rose about 1 pp of revenue, and digital conversion investments were added. Average revenue per mature restaurant is about INR7 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is mature-portfolio ROM (16.2%) below the ~20% implied by flow-through math?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the ~400 bps shortfall to about 2 pp lower gross margin, about 1 pp higher marketing, about 60 bps from delivery mix (delivery costs about 30%), and about 140-150 bps of energy, manpower and other inflation. It said it would not cap margins at 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the back-end cost base still rising and what is the per-cover sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost base is now normalised after hires in culinary, marketing, digital and tech; the April increments were the only incremental impact. Each INR1 per-cover improvement adds about INR1.5 crores of annual cost.

qa_highlights.question: What drives delivery growth, and what is its profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Delivery grew 62% on value SKUs across Barbeque Nation, BBQ and Dum Safar, plus higher marketing. Management said delivery is non-captive, depends on aggregators, and is accretive only if it adds absolute margin; it did not disclose delivery profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q2 guidance levels of high single digit to early double digit SSSG still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a full-year SSSG number, pointing instead to volume growth and a new operating scale. It said the momentum continued into July and revenue crossed INR400 crores for the first time, with the quarter at about INR425 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international gross margin impact and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: International gross margin fell about 3 pp on Middle East-linked inflation, with some commodity prices up 30-40%. Management expects it to taper sequentially but said some structural reversal may not occur.

risks_watch: SSSG moderation through FY27: Q3 and Q4 FY27 lap the strongest FY26 quarters, and management guided that reported growth will normalise.
Gross margin pressure from mix (BBQ India growing faster than the lower-GM segments) and from Middle East-linked commodity inflation in International, with some commodity prices up 30-40%.
Service and food quality: April manpower disruption, some guest reviews on service and AC, and a recent food-blogger video on chicken quality, which management disputed without lab detail.
Delivery economics: about 30% commission and packaging costs, delivery share up about 2 pp YoY, and no disclosed delivery margin.
Store expansion execution: 40 openings planned for FY27 against 35 last year, with 15 under construction, and a new 3,500 sq ft format; watch whether 266 to 300 is met.
No double-digit pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin timeline given; watch the margin levers on gross margin, mature ROM and new-store cohort maturation.
key_quotes: Our growth continues to be entirely volume led. We have not taken any price increase during Q1, and our average per coverage spend continues to reflect changes in business segment mix, daypart and session mix and value-led initiatives that we started from Q2 FY26.
This is more mathematics than our comment on demand.
I think the current levels of around 66% -67% range is a good operating band and we would expect to move directionally from here over time.
And as long as the absolute EBITDA margins are better, I'm not too worried about gross margins.

rows.why: Dine-in transactions grew 63.5% YoY (68.6% in Barbeque Nation India) with no price increase taken, and 15 new restaurants are opening in Q2-Q3 FY27, though SSSG is set to moderate as comparables tighten.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The FY27 capex of ~INR140 crores was held, not raised, and no new capex plan was announced; expansion is funded from internal accruals with borrowings kept prudent, and net debt only rose to INR106 crores from INR102 crores.

rows.why: SSSG of 28.7% in Q1 (vs 14.4% in Q4 FY26) will moderate as Q3 and Q4 FY27 lap the strongest FY26 quarters, and management gave no numeric full-year SSSG guide, so reported growth is set to normalise.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Big Buffet format is being rolled out in Tier 2/3 markets with about 6 quarters of data, and the Barbeque Nation India store format was reduced to ~3,500 sq ft from 4,500 sq ft, but no specific new product or brand launch dates were given.

rows.label: Big Buffet Tier 2/3 expansion, India capacity view raised to ~600 restaurants
rows.why: Management raised its view of Barbeque Nation India's scale capacity to ~600 restaurants from 400-450, against 266 restaurants total at Q1 close, based on about 6 quarters of Big Buffet data in Tier 2/3 markets.

rows.label: Back-end cost leverage after normalised cost base
rows.why: Back-end cost fell to 6.5% of sales from 7.1% in Q4 FY26, and management says the cost base is now normalised after hires, with only April increments left to flow through.

rows.label: International gross margin pressure from Middle East inflation
rows.why: International gross margin fell about 3 pp on Middle East-linked inflation with some commodity prices up 30-40%; management expects a sequential taper but says some structural reversal may not occur.

543287|2026-03.headline: Lodha FY26 presales INR205bn (+16%) and PAT INR34.3bn (20% margin); FY27 presales guided to INR240bn, PAT growth ~20% medium term.
543287|2026-03.overview: Lodha delivered its best-ever quarter in Q4 FY26 with presales of about INR58.9bn (+23% YoY), and full-year presales of INR205bn (+16%) with every quarter a record. PAT grew 24% to INR34.3bn, with PAT margin touching 20% for the first time, while adjusted EBITDA grew 14% and the embedded development margin held near 33%. Management shifted its primary guidance metric to PAT, guiding FY27 presales of about INR240bn (mid-teens growth) and PAT growth of about 20% CAGR to over INR85bn by FY31. Business development was strong, with 12 projects and INR600bn GDV added, and net debt fell to 0.23x equity.

segments.commentary: Growing at 25%+ CAGR; branded developer share in the INR400bn+ market rose from about 30% to 40%. Sewri cited as emerging hotspot with 5x growth.

segments.name: Luxury (INR50cr+ / INR100cr+)
segments.commentary: Company holds 40% share of the INR100cr+ segment and leads South & Central by sales with about 30% CAGR since FY23; INR50cr+ projects realise 30% higher per sq ft price.

segments.name: Bengaluru
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR24bn presales in FY26, over 12% of total, three years after pilot entry in FY23.

segments.name: Palava / Extended Eastern suburbs
segments.commentary: Q4 Palava presales near INR800cr; extended eastern suburbs sales flat at INR20-25bn for four years; average Palava price about INR11,000/sq ft carpet vs INR20,000+ in Airoli and INR25,000+ in Mulund/Thane.

segments.name: Annuity / RentCo (retail, office, warehousing)
segments.commentary: Annuity income about INR3bn in FY26 from 3.8mn sq ft complete of 8.8mn sq ft pipeline; target about INR10bn annual rent by FY31 excluding data centres.

segments.name: Data centres (Palava green DC park)
segments.commentary: 400 acres shovel-ready; AWS and STT secured as anchors; plan about 1GW powered shell on 100 acres, incremental cost INR100-110bn, income expected from FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance of about INR240bn, with embedded EBITDA margin of 32-34%, including single-digit % land sales contribution.
FY27 launch pipeline of INR218bn GDV identified; NCR launches (2 JDA projects, Gurgaon, GDV about INR33bn) excluded and expected Q4 FY27 or early FY28.
First-half FY27 presales expected in low 40s % of full-year guidance; assumes Middle East situation normalises by end of Q1 FY27.

Medium-term PAT CAGR of about 20%, from INR34bn in FY26 to over INR85bn by FY31.

Average DevCo to become debt-free over next few years; total debt at end FY27 expected lower than FY26 despite annuity capex.

qa_highlights.question: Will FCF turn positive through lower capex and OCF growth, and why is there no OCF guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Business development investment to be muted over 2 years given visibility; OCF expected to grow about 20% p.a. from INR71bn in line with PAT, with other linked factors not separately guided.

qa_highlights.question: How ready is the FY27 INR218bn launch pipeline and what is the status of environmental clearances?
qa_highlights.answer: New launches were about one-third of FY26 sales and will be slightly lower in FY27; all projects have land acquired, designs done and approvals available or in process. Management said the environmental clearance issue (Supreme Court order August 2025) is behind the market, with clearances resuming from November 2025.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for data centre build-to-suit announcements and lease income?

Management said the quarter was flattered by roughly half of the year's planned land sales, including data centre park land sold to Digital Edge India at about INR 420 million per acre. Residential pre-sales were deliberately weak because about one-third of normal launches were postponed to Q2 on Middle East conflict concerns. Net debt fell by INR 4.5 billion to under INR 50 billion, with net debt to equity at about 0.2x.

segments.name: Land sales
segments.commentary: Data centre and other land pre-sales of about INR 12 billion, with PAT contribution of about INR 6 billion. Management guides land sales of INR 20-30 billion a year for the next several years.

Medium-term PAT growth of about 20% a year, taking PAT beyond INR 85 billion by FY31; ROE expected to move toward 20% from about 16% in FY26 but may not reach it.

Estimated capex for the power-shell infrastructure is INR 500-700 crore over time, per the CFO-level answer on infrastructure.
Power density is 11-15 MW per acre. Management does not yet plan chips or racks and sees turnkey shell at least two years away.
demand_pricing: Middle East NRI buyers are about 4-5% of sales. Management sees the impact as moderate and expects NRI and US-based buyers to shift some money toward Indian homes.

Conversion rate reportedly 8% or higher from July, with a long-run aim of 10%.
Sales from new cities (Pune, Bangalore, NCR, MMR) to reach 30-45% of pre-sales in the medium term.

Palava land sale price rose to about INR 420 million per acre from about INR 210 million in calendar 2025. Management puts fair market value at about INR 650 million per acre, reachable in about 18 months.
Competition described as rational. Branded share of MMR is about 30%, which management expects to reach 40-45% by the end of the decade.

On the Q4 steel EBITDA per tonne question, management attributed part of the gap to old low-priced carryover orders and part to import cost and rupee impact; no quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FY26 volume growth, and which capacities come online in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 0.5 million tonnes of DRI, the Galvalume line at Jamuria, doubling colour-coated volume, new captive power plants lowering grid power costs, and the aluminium foil plant.

qa_highlights.question: Is aluminium a pass-through business or does it earn higher margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Largely a pass-through in price terms; margin upside expected from backward integration into foil stock as the new foil plant is built.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 EBITDA exceed INR3,000 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the estimate was close, plus or minus about 5%, and pointed to about 30% growth in FY27 as achievable, with conservative guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise and payable days stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said inventory rose from 99 to 123 days due to positioning of raw materials for CRM, blast furnace coking coal and iron ore, to be liquidated in Q1-Q2 FY27. Payable days are about 130 and not a one-off.

qa_highlights.question: What are the returns and EBITDA per tonne expectations for the stainless steel capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects EBITDA of INR15,000-20,000 per tonne for stainless, about INR12,000-15,000 on an overall basis, and above INR18,000 for an integrated iron-to-steel route. Returns are said to be 20-30% better than carbon steel.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded and what is the balance-sheet stance?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly internal accruals with possible short-term debt. Management said net cash was about INR1,800-1,900 crores in FY26 and expected to exceed INR2,000 crores. Debt capped at 0.5x equity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ED matter and the CPCB non-compliance a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ED coal case is at the letter-reply stage and not a concern. On CPCB, it described a minor error found in inspection that it has rectified, with compliance expected within 3 months.

risks_watch: Inventory days rose to 123 from 99 and payable days are about 130; management expects liquidation in Q1-Q2 FY27, so working-capital reversal is a watch item.
Q4 steel EBITDA per tonne rose only about INR2,600 against a price increase of about INR5,100; cost drivers were not quantified.
Nickel price increases (about 20% since December per an analyst) and imported raw material costs affecting stainless margins.
Pending ED notice on coal and a CPCB non-compliance observation; management says both are manageable.
Execution of the INR2,700 crore capex by March 2029 and the aluminium foil ramp-up in H2 FY27.
Management has stated that Q4 realisations are unlikely to move higher from current levels.
543299|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volumes, margins and cash generation, with a stated conservative stance on guidance. Evasive on the Q4 cost-versus-price bridge and on the ED matter, where questions were deflected to a separate discussion.
key_quotes: This is a business firing on all cylinders.
Shyam Metalics will never depend on the realization side.
I think this year, we will be very comfortable with our growth close to 30% over this year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 operating EBITDA growth of about 30% over FY26's INR2,333 crores, with CRM EBITDA at INR10,000-11,000 per tonne and aluminium at INR35,000-40,000 per tonne; EBITDA margin was 14.4% in Q4 FY26 vs 13.8% a year earlier, but Q4 realisations are not expected to rise further and the Q4 steel EBITDA per tonne gap was not quantified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (Galvalume, aluminium) and Q3 FY27 (DRI)

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 volumes grew 26% to 4.94 million tonnes and Q4 volumes rose 22% YoY; colour-coated volume is expected to roughly double YoY once the Galvalume line starts, and aluminium exports are oversold with the company unable to meet international demand.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: already announced; further capex likely in FY28
rows.why: The Board approved INR2,700 crores of new capex (Kharagpur wire mill INR900 crores, Sambalpur stainless INR1,800 crores) on top of a total programme of about INR10,000 crores, with INR2,900 crores in FY27 and INR3,000 crores in FY28, and the 800,000-tonne steel plant is still to be announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA growth of about 30% and calls it conservative, and says FY27 EBITDA is within about 5% of INR3,000 crores, but it has also said Q4 realisations are unlikely to rise further from current levels.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Inventory days rose from 99 to 123 and payable days are about 130, with working-capital liquidation expected in Q1-Q2 FY27, while nickel-linked stainless costs (about 20% higher since December per an analyst) and imported raw material costs are pressuring margins.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Galvalume colour-coated line due end-May/early June 2026 and aluminium foil stock and foil plant in trials, with battery foil qualified with 2 to 3 customers.

rows.label: Aluminium foil ramp-up and export demand
rows.why: Aluminium realisation rose 16% YoY to INR4,07,461 per tonne, management says exports are oversold, and the foil plant impact is expected in H2 FY27 once battery foil is qualified with 2 to 3 customers.

rows.label: Inventory liquidation after CRM and coking coal build
rows.why: Inventory days rose from 99 to 123 on raw material positioning for CRM, blast furnace coal and iron ore, and management expects liquidation in Q1-Q2 FY27, which should support cash generation of about INR2,000 crores.

rows.label: CPCB non-compliance and ED coal case
rows.why: Management says CPCB compliance is expected within 3 months and the ED coal case is at the letter-reply stage, but both are unresolved and the company deflected questions on the ED matter.
