543299|2026-06.headline: Shyam Metalics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.3% YoY to INR5,455 crore and EBITDA rose 28.3% to INR812 crore, with margin at 14.9%.
543299|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR5,455 crore, up 23.3% YoY and 4.1% QoQ, while EBITDA was INR812 crore (14.9% margin, up from 14.3% a year ago). Operating EBITDA was INR765 crore at a 14% margin and PAT was INR351 crore (6.4% margin), up 20.6% YoY. The company declared an interim dividend of INR1.8 per share and said the aluminium foil plant in Odisha has begun commissioning, with the aluminium flat roll project on track for Q2. Management also took a 26% stake in Emerge Green Power, a renewable energy vehicle, and shifted its solar strategy from capex to a JV-based model.

financial_highlights.change: vs 14.3% in Q1 FY26 and 14.4% in Q4 FY26
+20.6% YoY, +12.6% QoQ; margin vs 6% in prior quarter

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Management attributed higher aluminium EBITDA per ton (up about 52% YoY per analyst) to LME prices and product mix. The Odisha aluminium foil plant has started commissioning; full operations expected to take 3-4 months, with real value expected from Q3.

segments.name: Flat products / colour-coated (CRM)
segments.commentary: Colour-coated plant commissioned in April 2026, lifting cold rolling capacity by 60% to 0.4 million tons. Management expects flat product numbers to more than double in FY27. CRM EBITDA was about INR8,500 per ton in the quarter, which management said may moderate.

segments.name: Stainless steel
segments.commentary: Current run rate of about INR130-140 crore revenue per quarter. Management expects INR600-700 crore once the new plant reaches 70-80% utilisation. Vision 2031 assumes about INR14,000 per ton EBITDA, with mix of roughly two-thirds 200/400 series and 35-40% 300 series.

segments.name: Specialty alloys
segments.commentary: Analyst computed Q1 FY27 specialty alloy EBITDA margin around 20.5%, versus the roughly 15% implied by the FY31 vision. Management said demand is strong and no major capacity expansion is declared, though it is under evaluation.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for 2031 EBITDA margin of about 14-15% (long-term aspiration) and 600-700 bps improvement in ROE and ROCE by 2031; also cited a 15-17% overall business margin in a later answer.

Management is guiding FY27 growth above 20% in terms of numbers, with EBITDA growth of more than 20-25%. Analyst math of 30-35% EBITDA growth was acknowledged as possibly conservative; the chairman said projections are more than 25%.
Remaining announced capex of about INR9,580 crore to be deployed over the next 3-4 years, primarily funded through internal accruals.
Iron-making facilities and power plants expected to be commissioned around end of Q2 / early Q3 FY27; Q3 and Q4 are described as important for value-added contribution.
Another downstream capex leg is under Board evaluation, with clarity expected by Q3.
Interim dividend of INR1.8 per share declared; INR4,500 crore fundraising approval described as an enabling resolution only.
capex_capacity: Colour-coated plant commissioned April 2026, cold rolling capacity up 60% to 0.4 million tons.
Aluminium foil facility in Odisha commissioning; aluminium flat roll project on track for Q2 FY27 commissioning.
HR coil plant to produce about 2 million tons; flat steel volume target of 1.7-1.8 million tons by 2031.
Specialty steel: auto steel plant and SBQ mill at Ramsarup, expected to be commissioned by end of next year.
Beneficiation plant commissioned to use low-grade iron ore.

Solar strategy shifted from capex to an opex/JV model, with 26% stake in Emerge Green Power Private Limited (a PE-backed venture fund, not a related party). Some power plants expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian steel demand grows 7-8% a year and rebar accounts for about 50-55% of steel consumption; the recent rebar price fall was described as a seasonal monsoon effect.
Export business of about INR2,000 crore provides natural hedge; management said most raw materials are sourced domestically.
Management said the company is moving toward B2C and value-added products, with competition in CRM described as intense.

qa_highlights.question: Is aluminium EBITDA per ton up about 52% YoY driven by LME or mix, and why is specialty alloy margin (~20.5%) far above the FY31 vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium gains came from LME prices and product mix. Management said the 2031 ~15-17% margin is a holistic group figure and conservative, and that past targets were beaten.

qa_highlights.question: Is the softness in rebar prices seasonal or a demand weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a regular monsoon and logistics effect. Demand is expected to keep growing, and the company is focused on the annual view rather than quarterly moves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for new capacity and value-added revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium stabilises 3-4 months after commissioning, with value from Q3. Iron-making by end of Q2/early Q3, and flat products expected to more than double in FY27. Stainless run rate could reach INR600-700 crore at 70-80% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance only 20%+ growth when Q1 was up 28-30% and capacity is coming on stream?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers conservative guidance. It said projections are more than 25% and the numbers could be fantastic, with growth above 100% expected year on year in some parts.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise an enabling INR4,500 crore fundraising resolution if capex is internally funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is only an enabling resolution with no fundraising currently on the table. It has no major opportunity under evaluation and is prepared for future opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Emerge Green Power structure and capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: The 26% stake is a JV-style solar model, with the investee run by a PE-backed fund. Management said it avoids heavy capex, with returns around 8-10% on a buy-back model.

risks_watch: Specialty alloy and stainless margins look high versus the FY31 vision. Sustainability of CRM EBITDA at about INR8,500 per ton is uncertain given competition.
Inventory: management said it targets 2-3 months of inventory; a sizeable working capital build (around INR1,000 crore inventory cited) is exposed to commodity and geopolitical swings.
Execution risk on commissioning of aluminium foil, aluminium flat roll (Q2), iron-making (end Q2/early Q3) and power plants. Volume growth target of 25% for FY27 was not clearly confirmed.
Monsoon-quarter seasonality (Q2) could weaken volumes and realisations.
Commodity exposure: nickel is not sourced domestically for 300-series stainless, requiring imports of nickel scrap or nickel pig iron.
543299|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and margins but conservative on forward targets, repeatedly saying guidance is prudent. Evasive on specific volume numbers, the purpose of the fundraising resolution and the specialty alloy expansion, which was described as under evaluation.
key_quotes: We are very sure that, we will maintain this growth trajectory, what we had been doing in the past, and will become more and more investor and stakeholders friendly in the time to come.
We rather believe to speak less and deliver more.

We remain confident of delivering a 600 to 700 basis point improvement in return on equity and return on capital by 2031, supported by higher utilization, richer value-added product portfolio and increasing contributions from our downstream businesses.
Enabling resolution. Just -- no, it's just enabling resolution. Nothing very serious on the table.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Total EBITDA margin rose to 14.9% from 14.3% a year ago, but management calls the 14-15% long-term aspiration conservative and CRM EBITDA of about INR8,500/ton is expected to moderate amid intense competition.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Colour-coated plant already commissioned in April 2026 (cold rolling capacity up 60% to 0.4 Mt), Odisha aluminium foil in commissioning, aluminium flat roll on track for Q2, and iron-making and power plants due around end Q2/early Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects flat product numbers to more than double in FY27 after the 60% CRM capacity increase, though the 25% FY27 volume target was not reaffirmed and Q2 is seasonally weak.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Another downstream capex leg is under Board evaluation with clarity expected by Q3, and the INR9,580 crore balance capex is being deployed over 3-4 years, but no new capacity has been declared and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance is above 20% revenue growth and 20-25%+ EBITDA growth, which management calls conservative, with the chairman saying projections are more than 25% against Q1 EBITDA up 28.3% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Commissioning risk on aluminium flat roll (Q2), iron-making (end Q2/early Q3), and power plants, plus monsoon seasonality in Q2 and CRM and specialty margins that look high versus the FY31 vision.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aluminium foil is in commissioning with full operations expected in 3-4 months and real value from Q3, and the aluminium flat roll project is on track for Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Stainless steel new plant ramp to INR600-700 crore quarterly revenue
rows.why: Current run rate is only INR130-140 crore per quarter and the target needs the new plant at 70-80% utilisation, which is not yet demonstrated and was described as end-next-year commissioning for auto steel and SBQ.

rows.label: Interim dividend of INR1.8 per share and Emerge Green Power 26% stake
rows.why: Interim dividend of INR1.8 per share is declared, and the 26% stake in Emerge Green Power moves solar to a JV/opex model with returns around 8-10% on a buy-back model.

rows.label: Working capital pressure from inventory build
rows.why: Management targets 2-3 months of inventory against a sizeable inventory build of around INR1,000 crore, exposed to commodity and geopolitical swings.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, CRM and aluminium ramp and called guidance conservative, but was evasive on volume numbers, the INR4,500 crore fundraising purpose and specialty alloy expansion; analysts pressed on high specialty and CRM margins versus the FY31 vision and the FY27 volume target.

543299|2026-09.headline: Shyam Metalics Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33.4% YoY to INR5,960 crore and operating EBITDA margin expanded 170 bps to 13.8%.
543299|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached INR5,960 crore (up 33.4% YoY, 9.3% QoQ) on a 26% rise in sales volume to 15.49 lakh tons. Reported EBITDA was INR857 crore (14.4% margin) and operating EBITDA was INR823 crore (13.8% margin), with PAT of INR511 crore helped by a lower depreciation charge after a switch from WDV to straight-line depreciation. Management announced a proposed 51% stake in Alom Solar Pvt Ltd, which won the Phutamura coal block (170 Mt reserves, production expected July 2027), and an MoU for a 9 MTPA Maharashtra steel complex that management said is a post-FY29/FY30 decision. Capex to date is INR9,921 crore (about 53% of INR18,785 crore plan), with INR8,864 crore still to be deployed over 2 to 3 years from internal accruals.

segments.name: Carbon steel flat products
segments.commentary: Sales volume more than doubled YoY to about 81,500 tons in Q2. The HR and flat mix is scaling up, with the 1.6 Mt HR mill at Jamuria targeted for 2028.

segments.name: Stainless steel
segments.commentary: Volume grew 20.7% YoY to about 29,850 tons and realisation rose 35.2% YoY. Management cites value-added products (specialty wires, pipes); the INR2,700 crore Odisha expansion targets March 2029, and management guided about INR1,100 crore EBITDA by FY31.

segments.name: Specialty alloy
segments.commentary: Volume rose 4.7% YoY and realisation rose 18.4% YoY.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Volume rose 3% YoY and realisation rose 27.7% YoY. The 18,000 tpa Sambalpur foil line was commissioned in July, taking foil capacity to about 42,000 tpa; a 60,000 tpa FRP plant is planned under the INR800 crore downstream programme.

segments.name: Carbon steel long products
segments.commentary: Volume grew modestly YoY and rose 6.8% QoQ. Mittal Corp is running at about 85% utilisation, with management citing EBITDA of about INR10,000 per ton.

guidance_outlook: Management expects value-added products to reach roughly 70-80% of mix within 2 years, with the basic-supplies share falling to about 20%.
Targets overall EBITDA margin of 14.5% or more (from the 11-12% range it has been running), with a long-term aim of 15-16%.
Stainless steel is expected to contribute about INR1,100 crore EBITDA and the SBQ business about INR1,000 crore EBITDA by FY31.
Alom Solar coal block is expected to add about INR400 crore incremental EBITDA by FY31 for an estimated INR360 crore capex (Shyam share about INR185 crore).
Maharashtra 9 MTPA project: land acquisition in 1 to 1.5 years, major execution after FY29/FY30; no major outflow expected in the next few quarters.
Targets RoE of 16% and RoCE of 24% by 2031; management says about INR3,000 crore of CWIP is not yet in returns.
capex_capacity: Capex since listing INR9,921 crore (about 53% of INR18,785 crore plan); INR6,671 crore already capitalised; balance INR8,864 crore over the next 2 to 3 years from internal accruals.
HR mill of 1.6 Mt at Jamuria, targeted for 2028; auto-steel specialty bar/combo mill of 0.8 Mt at Kharagpur (INR900 crore).
Stainless steel expansion of INR2,700 crore at Odisha with downstream processing and SBQ plant, targeted for commissioning by March 2029.
Aluminium foil capacity of 18,000 tpa commissioned in July at Sambalpur; a 1.5 Mt beneficiation plant at Sambalpur (INR150 crore) was also commissioned.
Solar plant of about 9 MW commissioned at Jamuria; NCLT approved merger of Shree Venkateshwara Electrosteel Castings into Shyam Sel Ltd (tax benefit over INR15 crore).
demand_pricing: World Steel Association projects flat global steel demand in 2026 and 1.7% growth in 2027; India demand expected to grow 7.9% in 2026 and 8% in 2027.
Management said there is a shortage of HR in India at present.
Aluminium pricing was supported by Middle East disruption that has shut some plants, along with stronger domestic and export demand for foil.
Management attributed higher raw material costs to a pass-through in steel prices as demand rose, rather than cheaper inputs, when asked about raw material cost falling to about 71% of revenue.
Management said it is not concerned about new coated-steel capacity from players such as BMW Industries, which it describes as a converter business.

qa_highlights.question: Which volume drivers are expected over the next 6 to 12 months, given the sponge iron and stainless steel plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the revenue-driving mix will not change much near term, but expects value-added products to reach about 70-80% of the mix within 2 years as HR, stainless steel, specialty alloy and SBQ capacity comes up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scale and timing of the 9 MTPA Maharashtra steel MoU (INR50,000 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is at an early stage. Land is expected in 1 to 1.5 years, engineering takes about 6 months, and the project will be built in phases of 4.5 to 5 Mt, with major execution after FY29/FY30. It will be 100% owned by Shyam Metalics.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins higher in stainless steel, specialty alloys and aluminium foil this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strong demand, a shift to value-added products (specialty wires and pipes in stainless), continuous improvement as the plant stabilises, and Middle East disruption supporting aluminium foil demand.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital allocation work between West Bengal and Maharashtra under the internal-accrual policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no current plans for a second Bengal phase until existing projects stabilise, and no major Maharashtra outflow in the next few quarters. It does not intend to add debt, and any shortfall of INR400-1,000 crore is manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment has the best margin and how is capital being prioritised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stainless steel earns about INR13,000-15,000 per ton EBITDA, carbon steel about INR6,000-7,000 per ton, and aluminium about INR40,000 per ton on a smaller base. It will not concentrate capital in one product.

qa_highlights.question: How is Mittal Corp performing since acquisition and what are its per-ton economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity utilisation is about 85%, with wire and bright bar exports started. Management estimates RoCE above 20-25%; the CFO corrected EBITDA per ton to about INR10,000. No major long-product expansion is planned there.

qa_highlights.question: Is new coated-steel competition from players such as BMW Industries a margin risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not worried. It views BMW as a converter, says the market is growing, and argued that full backward integration from ore to colours is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material cost fall to about 71% of revenue when peers reported increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material prices have risen and the increase has been passed through to customers, with demand also rising. It noted some advantage from input prices in the growing segments.

risks_watch: Execution risk on INR8,864 crore of remaining capex, including HR mill (2028), Odisha stainless (March 2029) and Alom Solar coal block (July 2027 target).
Stabilisation of newly commissioned stainless steel and aluminium foil capacity; management says the margin gains are not from one specific factor.
Competitive intensity in coated steel and HR as new capacity (including from West Bengal players) comes on stream.
Maharashtra project is at MoU stage with land and mining not yet secured; management says no major outflow in the next few quarters.
Sustainability of margin gains if raw material prices stay volatile; a 1 pp operating margin move is material against the 13.8% base.
Sustaining RoE/RoCE progress toward 16%/24% by 2031 as CWIP of about INR3,000 crore is commissioned.
543299|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on volumes, margins and balance sheet, with a strong focus on the capex programme. Management was evasive on specifics: it gave no capex timeline or cost breakdown for the Maharashtra project and offered only "nothing very specific" on the margin drivers, while routinely deferring to later periods.
key_quotes: Amit, we will not see a major change on the revenue-driving mechanism, what is going right now.
So the initial investment is going to be only for 4.5 million to 5 million tons.
We are not doing any major expansion in Mittal Corp. in the long product, because we feel like we have to invest more on the downstream rather than upstream.
We don't put everything in one basket at one time.
So presently, for next few quarters, I don't see any kind of major financials outflow coming out in Maharashtra project, because we are at a very initial stage.

543300|2026-03.headline: Sona Comstar Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% YoY to ₹1,272 crore, a record quarter, though EBITDA margin fell 2.7pp to 24.4%.
543300|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 posted record revenue (₹1,272 crore, +47% YoY), record EBITDA (₹311 crore, +32%) and record PAT (₹192 crore, +17%), with BEV revenue of ₹359 crore at a record 39% share. Margins compressed on commodity inflation with pass-through lag, product mix (lower-margin traction motors and railways) and a PLI income base effect. Management won four new driveline orders, including three from European OEMs in one quarter, and said Europe's EV order flow is returning. Full-year FY26 revenue grew 26% to ₹4,475 crore, with EBITDA margin at 24.7% and adjusted PAT up 11%.

segments.name: Automotive BEV
segments.commentary: Q4 BEV revenue ₹359 crore (39% share, record); FY26 BEV revenue ₹1,154 crore (-6%), weak Q1 drove the full-year decline. 67 EV programs across 35 customers, 37 in production and 30 pending.

segments.name: Traction and suspension motors
segments.commentary: Traction motors about 10% of revenue. Suspension motors expected to grow 3-4x in FY27 volumes, reaching single digit share of revenue in FY26 and possibly double digits in FY27.

segments.name: Differential gears and assemblies
segments.commentary: Legacy products kept growing alongside new products. Q4 saw 7 non-EV differential gear programs from existing customers worth about ₹3 billion.

segments.name: Railway (acquired)
segments.commentary: Lower-margin, high-return business, consolidated during FY26 and funded with about ₹1,800 crore. Q4 approvals for electric control panels (first batch supplied) and HVAC (supply to start this quarter).

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Eastern markets were 60% of Q4 revenue vs 40% a year earlier. India exceeded 50% of mix for full year FY26.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin band guided at 23-25% post railway acquisition, replacing the earlier 24-26% band for the core business.
Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, freight, packaging, energy) expected to keep pressuring margins in the foreseeable future, as pass-through lags.
Haryana minimum wage hike effective 1 April 2026 expected to add labour cost; to be offset via productivity, tighter headcount addition and workload management.
Novelic India SOP for one customer expected at end of calendar 2026; Europe in-cabin safety NCAP requirement moved to 2027.

Railway growth over 3-5 years framed through capacity/process improvement, white-space variants and new products (HVAC needs about 3 years for full rolling stock coverage; electric panels 12-15 months).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex ₹369 crore; additional land bought for about ₹110 crore.
Gas requirement cut by nearly 20% at company level via electric heating, gas-flow optimisation and process changes; no production loss so far.
Traction motor capacity of about 1 million electric motors, reusable across customers with tweaks.
Fixed asset turnover fell to 2.9 due to new capitalisation and land purchase; expected to improve as FY26 capex generates revenue in FY27.
ROCE dipped due to fresh equity raised in September 2024; expected to improve over medium term as railway capital is deployed.
demand_pricing: Q4 wins: 4 driveline orders, including 3 from European OEMs (highest ever in a quarter from Europe, first EV win from Europe in about 4 years) and 1 hybrid platform.
FY26: 31 new programs won and 3 new customers added; order book roughly flat YoY after a Q2 correction tied to one model.
Pricing: company says a large part of commodity inflation is passed through with a lag; the remainder hits margins.
Demand: management cites March 2026 BEV sales up about 45% in EU and India e-car and e-2W up 65% and 45%; April trending above 50% in India.
US: Section 232 tariffs (25%) unchanged; management says revenue and margins from US not materially affected.
China: one large Chinese EV customer supplied; management sees entry into China-for-China supply chain as hard for now.

qa_highlights.question: Opportunity from European peer bankruptcies and asset sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says some opportunities already flowing (recent wins); Europe still a good place to win business over the next 12 months, with no material change to the opportunity set.

qa_highlights.question: Novelic India progress and ramp?

543308|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 34.8% YoY to INR 1,075 crore, but EBITDA pre-Ind AS fell 33.5% to INR 131 crore as new hospitals dragged margins.
543308|2026-03.overview: KIMS reported Q4 FY26 total revenue of INR 1,084 crore (+35.3% YoY, +8.1% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 216 crore (+6.8% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 19.9% versus 25.3% a year ago. Management attributed the margin compression to roughly INR 32 crore of EBITDA erosion from newer units (in operation under one year), while mature units held about 28.5-29% margins. PAT fell to INR 33 crore from INR 106 crore a year ago. Management is raising about INR 1,500 crore via QIP to cut net debt, which it says has peaked at INR 3,000-plus crore, and targets net debt to EBITDA of 1-2x from about 1x-3x currently.

segments.name: Mature units
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 862 crore with EBITDA about INR 250 crore, a margin of roughly 28.5-29%. For FY26, mature units generated INR 3,335 crore revenue and about INR 956 crore EBITDA, about 29.5% margin.

segments.name: Newer units (under one year old)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 224 crore with EBITDA erosion of about INR 32 crore. For FY26, these units generated INR 597 crore revenue and about INR 128 crore EBITDA erosion.

segments.name: Mahadevapura (Bengaluru)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 49 crore and loss about INR 14 crore; management says it averages about INR 17 crore/month and targets INR 25-30 crore/month over 12 months.

segments.name: Electronic City / PES (Bengaluru)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 17 crore with loss about INR 25 crore; commissioned in December 2025. Management expects EBITDA-positive by end of FY27.

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 47 crore and loss about INR 5 crore. Management says Thane was EBITDA-neutral in March and April 2026, before adding doctors in May.

segments.name: Nashik
segments.commentary: Q4 loss about INR 1 crore. Still awaiting STAR, Medi Assist and GIPSA empanelment.

guidance_outlook: Telangana cluster EBITDA growth guided at about 10-12% in FY27, below historical rates due to Kondapur and Kompally.
Newer-unit combined losses in FY27 and FY28 expected to be less than half of the roughly INR 120-128 crore FY26 drag, subject to insurance empanelments.
Use about INR 1,000 crore of QIP proceeds to retire debt; remainder for losses and capex in existing facilities.

Palakkad (300-bed, acquired; consolidated) expected at INR 6.5-7 crore revenue in May 2026 with about 5% negative EBITDA, breakeven by June-July 2026, targeting INR 12-15 crore/month revenue over time.
Bangalore ARPOB to be modelled at INR 75,000 annually; Andhra ARPOB at about INR 26,000-27,000.
Bengaluru occupancy expected at 35-40% by end of FY27 on full bed capacity.
Kondapur move to new 800-bed facility from first week of June 2026; Phase 1 of 400-500 beds; INR 50-75 crore further capex deferred to FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: New Kondapur (Hyderabad) 800-bed hospital; shift from old facility starting first week of June 2026, with a one-month transition and old facility possibly running 2-3 months more.
Phase 1 of Kondapur to open at 400-500 beds; remaining 300 beds to be commissioned as occupancy rises.

Expansions in FY26: Kompally (Hyderabad), two in Guntur, Thane and Sangli (Maharashtra), Mahadevapura and Electronic City (Bengaluru), Kollam (Kerala), and fertility centres in Hyderabad and Guntur. KIMS Cuddles mother-and-child unit opened in Nellore; cancer block opened in Ongole.

Greenfield projects planned in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu (one hospital), with continued expansion in Andhra and Telangana; these take 3-5 years to commission. Secunderabad expansion expected within 18 months.
Project funding norm: about 40% equity and 65% debt. Doctor participation typically 3-5% of equity; the model remains open.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per operating bed rose 13.7% YoY and 1.7% QoQ in Q4; average revenue per patient up 14% YoY and 3.5% QoQ.
IP volumes up 17.9% YoY and 4% QoQ; OP volumes up 30.1% YoY and 4.1% QoQ in Q4. FY26 IP volumes +15.4%, OP +25.4%.
Maharashtra Q4 occupancy at 60.5% (FY26 about 52.1%), which management calls the new base.
Hyderabad is the most competitive market; 4-5 hospitals commissioned in the last year. Management reports losing only one or two doctors, with no material attrition.
Insurance empanelment delays (new GIC common empanelment process and volume of new hospitals) are the main ramp-up constraint for new units.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise a INR 1,500 crore QIP after saying debt had peaked, and are new expansion plans firm?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is near INR 3,000-plus crore and the QIP will retire debt, with cash flow then funding 3-5 year greenfield projects. Expansion plans are still being explored; 400-500 beds of small acquisitions may come in the next two quarters, all in home markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on insurance empanelment for the new hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Nashik still needs STAR, Medi Assist and GIPSA. Thane has GIPSA, with Medi Assist and STAR nearly done, covering about 70% of insurance volume. Bangalore needs 3-4 more months. Confusion from the new GIC common-empanelment process caused the delays.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ARPOB and occupancy run-rates for Bangalore and Andhra Pradesh for modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Bangalore ARPOB of about INR 85,000 for FY26 but management says to model INR 75,000. Andhra at about INR 26,000-27,000 in Q3 and Q4. Bengaluru occupancy expected 35-40% by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kondapur capex and phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: The 800-bed Kondapur facility is almost fully capex-complete, with INR 50-75 crore left for two additional floors in FY28-FY29. Phase 1 covers 400-500 beds. Transition cost is expected to be about INR 15-25 crore, based on the Sunshine move precedent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt outlook for FY27 after the QIP?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,000 crore of debt to be retired from QIP proceeds. The balance covers losses at new hospitals and capex in existing facilities.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA growth is expected for the Telangana cluster in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Telangana cluster EBITDA growth of about 10-12% in FY27, below historical levels because of the Kondapur and Kompally commissioning.

risks_watch: Insurance empanelment delays at Nashik, Thane and Bangalore hospitals, which management says limit ramp-up.
Margin dilution from new units: cluster-level margins, not company-level, are the guided metric; Q4 company margin was 19.9%.
Leverage: management targets net debt/EBITDA of 1-2x; the call says the current ratio is about 1x-3x (ambiguous). The QIP is about INR 1,500 crore.
Q4 PAT of INR 33 crore and EPS decline of 37.2% in FY26, with management acknowledging ROE and ROCE have fallen.
Geopolitical and macro risk: management cited the Gulf war and a government austerity appeal.
Competition for doctors in Hyderabad; possible common-empanelment initiative by IRDAI/GIC, which management declined to comment on.
Inconsistencies in disclosures: bed-addition plan changed without a timeline; management said the update would come next quarter.
543308|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and cluster-level margin trajectory, but cautious on near-term profitability, acknowledging that new-unit losses and insurance empanelment delays will persist. Management was evasive on forward-looking growth numbers and on the common-empanelment policy.

Right now, the only challenge I see is the insurance empanelment.

543308|2026-06.headline: KIMS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 1,180 crore, with EBITDA pre-Ind AS at INR 222 crore and debt cut to INR 2,570 crore.
543308|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total revenue of INR 1,196 crore (+36.1% YoY, +10.3% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 240 crore at a 20.1% margin, with PAT of INR 37 crore versus INR 85 crore a year earlier. Growth was driven by IP volumes (+26.6% YoY) and OP volumes (+28.5% YoY), with the Kondapur hospital commissioned in June and Palakkad (Kerala) opened. The QIP raised INR 1,500 crore, of which INR 1,100-1,125 crore repaid debt, and a INR 600 crore promoter preferential allotment is partly pending. Management guided Telangana to 30-35% margins over time, Kerala to 20-22% in two to three years, and Bengaluru to break-even for the full year, while several new units are still ramping up.

financial_highlights.change: +20.1% YoY, +10.9% QoQ; margin vs 20.27% in Q1 FY26

segments.commentary: Management said revenue and EBITDA grew strongly YoY in Telangana and Andhra; Kondapur did INR 45 crore in July (first full month) against INR 32-33 crore monthly previously. Telangana occupancy is about 61% on the adjusted bed base excluding Kondapur and 200 Secunderabad beds under renovation.

segments.name: Bengaluru cluster (Mahadevapura, Electronic City)
segments.commentary: Mahadevapura reached EBITDA break-even in June and did about INR 20 crore revenue in July; Electronic City expected to break even in about one to two quarters. Management aims for zero EBITDA for the cluster for FY27. Census-bed occupancy at Mahadevapura is about 40%.

segments.name: Maharashtra (Thane, Nashik, Nagpur)
segments.commentary: Thane averaged about INR 16 crore monthly revenue in Q1 and did INR 21 crore in July at about 10% EBITDA margin. Nashik reached EBITDA break-even in Q1; Nagpur did INR 30 crore revenue in July. Empanelment delays of four to five months weighed on Q1.

segments.name: Kerala
segments.commentary: Kerala margins are in the single digits currently, with management expecting mid-teens in FY28 and 20-22% over two to three years after a 4-5% entry-cost drag. Palakkad opened, taking Kerala to three units; one more hospital (Thrissur) is due in three to four months.

segments.name: Andhra Pradesh
segments.commentary: Management said AP remains strong. Q1 ARPOB growth slowed from prior quarters (Q4 FY26 about INR 27,000), which management attributed to seasonal case mix. Cancer services were added to most AP hospitals in the last two to three months.

guidance_outlook: Telangana EBITDA margin expected to return to 30-35% over time as new Kondapur and Secunderabad beds ramp up; management said 30% is achievable by FY30 without new beds, and 70% occupancy is targeted in three to four years.
Bengaluru cluster targeted at zero EBITDA for full FY27; Bengaluru ARPOB expected to settle at INR 80,000-85,000 once empanelments complete, versus about INR 90,000+ recently.
Kondapur full potential of about INR 100 crore revenue per month (about INR 1,200 crore a year) within four to five years; model margin around 30%, with 30-32% suggested for the next two years.
ARPOB growth guidance of 4-5% per year; management called 15-16% historical growth too aggressive to model.
Maintenance capex about INR 100 crore per year for three to four years; about INR 100-125 crore growth capex over the next nine months, including Rajahmundry construction (INR 60-75 crore in FY27).
Debt-equity intended to be kept around 2.5:1; surplus cash to go to greenfield and brownfield growth in core states. Minority interest about 10.5% currently, 10-15% longer term.
Empanelment with the remaining 50% of insurers, covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets, expected by end-August to mid-September 2026.
capex_capacity: Kondapur hospital commissioned in June 2026 (first patient 20 June); about 450-500 operational beds added in the last 10 days of Q1, and the old Kondapur hospital will run for about six more months with rent of about INR 90 lakh per month plus GST and INR 3-4 crore a year of operating cost.

Palakkad (Kerala) opened in Q1; Thrissur to commence in three to four months; Electronic City and other Bengaluru beds added at Mahadevapura (operational beds up from about 170 to 210, total cluster 280 to 340).
Secunderabad: old 250-bed facility demolished; replacement facility expected by end of next year.

Two O&M agreements (Golden Lan Solutions, Sarvottam Healthcare) approved in draft: a 300-bed Telangana hospital near Kondapur with INR 90-95 crore monthly revenue potential, and a Kakinada hospital currently at INR 7-8 crore a month, targeting INR 15-20 crore. O&M means no losses borne by KIMS.
Future pipeline: greenfield in Karnataka (300-350 beds, expandable by about 100) and acquisitions in Maharashtra, Kerala, Telangana and Andhra; timing and bed count not committed.

qa_highlights.question: Kerala cost increase and steady-state margin, plus whether the Q1 ARPOB jump is structural or seasonal.
qa_highlights.answer: Kerala is in growth phase; single-digit EBITDA margin now, mid-teens next financial year, and 20-22% over two to three years after a 4-5% entry-cost drag. Management said ARPP is the better metric; ARPOB moves with seasonal case mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why Telangana occupancy sits around 50-52% and whether it can rise further.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bed count includes 250 demolished Secunderabad beds not yet operational; ex-Kondapur and ex-200 renovating beds occupancy is about 61%. 70% is achievable in three to four years without new beds.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost impact after the INR 1,100 crore debt repayment.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said QIP proceeds arrived around 24 June and debt was repaid on 27-28 June, so the interest saving was not in Q1 and will show from Q2. Debt was INR 2,570 crore at 30 June, about INR 2,400 crore after early July repayments.

qa_highlights.question: Kondapur losses, pre-operative costs and status of the old hospital.
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-operative costs about INR 1.5-2 crore a month; Q1 losses marginal. Old hospital runs about six more months at about INR 90 lakh a month rent plus GST and INR 3-4 crore a year operating cost.

qa_highlights.question: Thane ramp-up lagging peers and when it turns breakeven.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 weakness to a four-to-five-month empanelment delay and seasonality. Thane averaged about INR 16 crore monthly in Q1 and did INR 21 crore in July at about 10% margin; a healthy margin is expected if the trend holds.

qa_highlights.question: Telangana margin: why 30% guidance versus historical 35% peaks.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 30-35% over time, citing FY25-26 margins of about 31%, Secunderabad at 34-35% and Q4 FY26 Telangana at 38-39%. Return to 30%-plus will take time as new beds ramp.

demand_pricing: IP volumes 72,493 (+26.6% YoY, +14% QoQ); OP volumes 6,58,617 (+28.5% YoY, +8% QoQ); management cited FY25-based annual growth of 15.4% for IP and 25.4% for OP.
Average revenue per operating bed +9.7% YoY and +0.1% QoQ; ARPP +6.8% YoY and -3.8% QoQ. Management said ARPP is the better indicator, as ARPOB moves with ALOS and seasonal case mix.

Kondapur commissioned with first patient on 20 June 2026; July (first full month) revenue about INR 45 crore versus INR 32-33 crore monthly previously. Management said Kondapur full potential is about INR 100 crore per month within four to five years.

Bengaluru ARPOB running at INR 90,000+ for two quarters; management guided INR 80,000-85,000 once empanelments complete, with ARPP said to be similar to Telangana. Mahadevapura census-bed occupancy about 40%.

Telangana occupancy about 61% excluding Kondapur and 200 Secunderabad beds under renovation; management targets 70% in three to four years without new beds, and said about 65% on a prior adjusted basis was also cited. ARPOB growth guided at 4-5% a year; management called 15-16% too aggressive.

Insurance empanelment: about 50% of insurers done; remaining 50% covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets expected by end-August to mid-September 2026. Maharashtra Q1 hit by four-to-five-month empanelment delay; Thane July revenue INR 21 crore at about 10% EBITDA margin.
risks_watch: Empanelment: remaining 50% of insurers, covering Thane, Nashik and two Bengaluru assets, due by end-August to mid-September 2026; the Joint Insurance Committee common-empanelment process is unresolved.
Ramp-up of new units: Electronic City breakeven guided in one to two quarters; Thane margin and Kerala single-digit margins still weak.
Bengaluru ARPOB may fall from INR 90,000+ toward INR 80,000-85,000 as empanelments complete.
Telangana occupancy about 61% on the adjusted base; Secunderabad 250-bed replacement not due until end of next year, and the 200 renovating beds are excluded from the base.
Government receivables improving but not fully on time; management said loss funding dropped only a little in Q1.
Acquisitions and greenfield timing not committed; management declined to quantify bed additions for FY28-29 and said the O&M deals (Golden Lan, Sarvottam) are draft-stage.
key_quotes: The first month has been very promising. We grew by almost 40% in less than a month.
As far as Telangana is concerned, we do not see any reason why we cannot ramp up to 70%, in spite of the new Kondapur hospital and the new Secunderabad hospital over the next three to four years.
I think it is too aggressive. Four to five is a good number.
Most likely it will get invested for greenfield and brownfield growth.

543311|2026-03.headline: India Pesticides FY26 revenue rose 27.9% to INR 1,078 crore and PAT 45.8% to INR 120 crore; Q4 domestic sales up over 50% to INR 183 crore.
543311|2026-03.overview: FY26 crossed INR 1,000 crore revenue for the first time, with EBITDA up 44.7% to INR 194 crore at an 18% margin. Q4 growth was driven by domestic herbicides and intermediates (domestic INR 183 crore vs INR 118 crore), while Q4 exports fell to INR 84 crore from INR 89 crore on geopolitical disruption and pricing pressure. Management said raw material and freight inflation is being partly passed to customers, with sulphur-based inputs seeing the largest increases. Management reiterated the INR 3,000 crore revenue target for March 2031 and guided FY27 revenue growth of 15-20% with EBITDA margin of 18-20%. Dividend was held at INR 0.75, which drew pushback from an individual investor.

543317|2026-06.headline: G R Infra Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 32.71% YoY to ~INR2,423 crores, but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 11.02% from 12.65%.
543317|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 32.71% YoY to about INR2,423 crores, while consolidated revenue rose 40% to INR2,784 crores. Margins compressed on higher construction and material costs, with standalone EBITDA margin at 11.02% versus 12.65% a year earlier and group EBITDA margin at 16.8% versus 20%. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance at 15-20% despite the 30%+ first-quarter run-rate, citing appointed-date timing for new projects. Order book stands at about INR25,300 crores as of 1 July 2026, with about INR32,000 crores of bids yet to be opened.

segments.name: BharatNet
segments.commentary: FY27 expected revenue about INR400 crores, of which about INR300 crores is capex (cabling, starting second half) and the balance O&M. Order book about INR1,000 crores.

Order inflow to date has lagged government pipeline claims for about two years, per management.

543318|2026-03.headline: Clean Science Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR193 crore with 46% EBITDA margin; FY26 standalone revenue fell 12% to about INR796 crore.
543318|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to about INR193 crore on volume recovery, with EBITDA of INR88 crore (46% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (40%), but revenue fell 19% YoY. For FY26, standalone revenue declined 12% from INR900 crore to INR796 crore, attributed to loss of an FMCG key account (4-MAP), lower offtake and pricing pressure. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 14% to about INR246 crore, led by HALS (Clean Fino-Chem), with EBITDA of INR96 crore (33%) and PAT of INR58 crore. Management said Clean Fino-Chem reached its first positive EBITDA (INR7 crore) and that the Hydroquinone/Catechol plant is still stabilising at about 10-15% utilisation.

segments.name: Performance chemicals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 72% of FY26 standalone revenue. Management cited a rebound in flagship product volumes and a gross margin (RMC 33%) about 2 points better than prior quarters.

segments.name: Pharma-Agro (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 19% of FY26 standalone revenue. The pharma intermediate plant was refurbished for HALS intermediates, and the older pharma intermediate was dropped.

segments.name: FMCG (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed the balance 9% of FY26 standalone revenue. A key FMCG account (4-MAP) was lost during the year.

segments.name: HALS (Clean Fino-Chem subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q4 FY26, at over 1,000 tonnes per quarter versus about 350-360 tonnes eight quarters earlier. Blended realisation was about INR460/kg versus INR420-430/kg in Q3; exports rose to about 50% of sales in select products from about 20%. Subsidiary EBITDA margin was about 15% in Q4 versus about 1% in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Performance Chemical 2 (water treatment-related capex) expected to commercialise by September 2026; validation in Q3, initial commercial production in Q4, and a pickup in FY28.
Hydroquinone/Catechol plant expected to reach optimal operations in 1-2 quarters; captive HQ/catechol now replaces imports for TBHQ and Veratrole.
Capex budget for FY27 of about INR80-100 crore; Clean Fino-Chem projects under an INR200 crore enabling Board resolution, with investment likely in the second half of FY27.
Management aspires to a HALS blended realisation of USD7-7.5/kg but did not give FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance, calling FY27 a 'very tricky' year dependent on macro and crude oil.
Management said it is not pencilling in any price hikes; it expects to benefit in an inflationary environment, as it did in FY23.
capex_capacity: Clean Fino-Chem Hydroquinone/Catechol plant commissioned in December 2025; still in initial stabilisation, with utilisation about 10-15% and March 2026 HALS exit utilisation about 40%.
Performance Chemical 2 commercialisation timeline moved due to scarce manpower linked to labour movement from higher gas prices; now targeted by September 2026.
Plans to debottleneck HALS lines and add a dedicated HALS 2020 line (in-house technology, validated with European customers) and to backward-integrate further key intermediates with minimal capex.
Pharma plant refurbished in the next couple of months to produce HALS intermediates, replacing Chinese sourcing.
Subsidiary capital infusion of about INR200 crore in FY26 takes total investment in subsidiary to INR750 crore.
demand_pricing: MEHQ: management is maintaining market share by calibrating prices against Chinese hydroquinone producers, who are less affected by raw material costs. Phenol and acetone prices rose sharply, and long-term contracts (half-yearly or yearly) could not pass on increases; these will be renegotiated on expiry.

HALS demand: export share rose to about 50% in select products (Europe, Middle East, US), with Southeast Asia and LatAm being explored. Distribution partners are adding safety stock, and inbound customer interest is rising.
Anisole: management said it is the largest producer and consumer globally and India; competition from China does not affect its sales, as anisole is mainly used captively.
Base chemical prices reportedly rose about 2x in some commodities, but management said these are not transactional benchmarks. Management said China has a pricing advantage over other geographies.
Management declined to share product-wise revenue, geographic split, or product-level volumes, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HALS revenue jump sharply, and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer validation and trials delayed the response by several quarters. Exports rose to about 50% of sales in select products from about 20%, with over 1,000 tonnes sold in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company passing on higher raw material costs (phenol, acetone, ammonia)?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were passed on partly, not fully; long-term contracts could not be repriced, and these are to be renegotiated as they expire. Q4 subsidiary EBITDA was INR8 crore despite March price spikes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Performance Chemical 1 (HQ/catechol) utilisation and breakeven outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 10-15%. Management expects two more quarters to optimise norms and yields before ramping utilisation further.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a volume or gross margin explanation for MEHQ, given the share-defence pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sequential growth of 7-8% was volume-led, led by flagship products. Standalone gross margin improved on product mix, with no one-off gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and the performance bonus reversal amount?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex could be INR80-100 crore, with Clean Fino-Chem investments likely in the second half. The bonus reversal was about INR11 crore.

543318|2026-06.headline: Clean Science Q1 FY27 consolidated sales hit a record INR264 crore (+10% YoY, +7% QoQ), with standalone EBITDA at INR87 crore (43% margin).
543318|2026-06.overview: Management reported record consolidated sales of about INR264 crore, up 7% QoQ and 10% YoY, driven by HALS scale-up. Standalone revenue rose 5% QoQ to INR203 crore on realisation gains, while standalone sales fell 6% YoY on volume loss from raw-material and shipping disruptions, including about two weeks of production stoppage. HALS is now 22% of sales and legacy top-4 products fell to 60% of sales from 85% in Q4 FY23. Management announced a Geneus Chem (Swiss) collaboration for advanced NOR HALS and a 5-year Kemin supply contract, and said CFCL became operationally self-sustaining.

qa_highlights.question: What drove HALS volume and pricing, and is the INR250-300 crore annual run-rate comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume about 1,000 tonnes in Q1; average price rose from about INR440 to INR550/kg on mix shift (HALS 770 share fell from about 50% to 35%). Management said the INR250-300 crore annualised run-rate is comfortable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 43-45% HALS gross margin sustainable, or helped by cheap acetone?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Geneus Chem transaction and its revenue potential?

qa_highlights.question: What was the cause of the YoY decline in legacy volumes, and will volumes recover in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Propylene shortage at a primary Indian supplier forced about two weeks of shutdown. Management said volumes are not an issue now; raw material pricing and shipping availability remain challenges.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Kemin 5-year contract add volume and need capacity?

qa_highlights.question: Will the Kemin and Geneus deals preempt new entrants?

543318|2026-09.headline: Clean Science Q2 FY27: standalone revenue up 11% QoQ to INR226 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 36% as raw material costs rose to 41% of sales.
543318|2026-09.overview: Management reported a record-high quarterly revenue, with standalone sales of INR226 crore (up 11% QoQ, 10% YoY) and consolidated sales of INR295 crore (up 23% YoY). Standalone EBITDA was INR82 crore (36% margin) and PAT INR55 crore (24%), with margin compression driven by phenol, acetone and methanol costs that were 50-100% higher YoY and could not be passed on to customers. HALS revenue roughly doubled YoY, with around 22% of quarterly sales (about INR66 crore per analyst's calculation, confirmed as "more or less" right) from HALS. Consolidated PAT turned positive in the quarter, helped by a turnaround at CFCL.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 2x YoY on strong volume growth; H1 FY27 volumes were 67% of total FY26 volumes. Around 22% of Q2 sales; capacity utilisation about 30-35% (up to 40% cited).

segments.name: Hydroquinone / catechol (CFCL)
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 30-35%; output mainly captive, with small sales picking up in Europe and India.

qa_highlights.answer: Management will keep testing price increases and will stop when customers push back. It expects competitors to raise prices eventually but does not want to move first.

qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes so but said the outcome is uncertain.

qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is about 11,500 tons, rising to about 12,500 tons with added advanced grades. Advanced grade is about 40% of the portfolio, up from a lower share earlier, and the ratio is expected to keep shifting.

543320|2026-03.headline: Eternal's Q4FY26 call: management gave a three-year outlook of 60% quick commerce NOV CAGR and a ~$1bn EBITDA ambition, with no FY27 growth number and no quarterly financials in the transcript.
543320|2026-03.overview: The call was a Q&A-only session with CEO Albinder Dhindsa, CFO Akshant Goyal and Kunal Swarup, with no prepared remarks in the transcript. Management reiterated a 60% NOV CAGR for quick commerce over three years and a roughly 5-6% steady-state contribution/EBITDA margin for Blinkit, and said it is not guiding FY27 growth to 100%. Competitive intensity was described as unchanged, with management choosing to keep marketing spend high to capture cheap new customers. Management declined to disclose store-level, geographic-split, warehouse-capacity and ad-mix data, and said it will keep reinvesting incremental food delivery margin into growth.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst math implies quick commerce margin of roughly 3-3.5% in the medium term; management said the math is broadly in line
Analyst cited ~3% in one question; management referenced 5-6% as the level it will reach at some point
Referred to as overall billion-dollar profit target by FY29; management said it includes Hyperpure and all current businesses
Monthly active delivery partners up ~30% YoY
Down from ~3.6 over the last couple of quarters; management attributed this mainly to new customer additions
Management attributed it to multiple sequential factors, not mainly AOV

financial_highlights.change: Management did not split it by business

segments.name: Quick commerce (Blinkit)
segments.commentary: Management targets 60% NOV CAGR over three years, and fixed costs were flat QoQ while marketing spend stayed high to acquire customers at low CAC. Steady-state margin of 5-6% was cited, and NCR contribution was said to be roughly 8-9%, which management did not confirm.

segments.name: Food delivery
segments.commentary: Growth is near 20% and margin is about 5.5%, per the analyst. Management is reinvesting incremental margin into growth, with a lower MOV of about INR 99 and platform fee increases used to fund targeted discounts.

segments.commentary: Management said event cancellations from artist visa issues would not change the overall outlook. It has no plans to add categories and does not treat travel as a focus area.

segments.name: Hyperpure
segments.commentary: Management said it is the smallest business but is included in the ~$1bn profit ambition, and was described as meaningful and relevant.

segments.name: Bistro
segments.commentary: Management described it as a small early experiment, not a big bet, and it is being watched against competitors.

guidance_outlook: Quick commerce NOV growth of 60% CAGR over the next three years; management said it is not guiding a specific FY27 figure and the 100% FY27 growth expectation no longer holds.
Dark store count of about 3,000 by March 2026 is on track; management declined to guide store additions beyond that.
Blinkit steady-state contribution margin of 5-6% at some point, with no unlocks assumed beyond current execution to reach roughly 3% in the analyst's math.
June quarter QoQ growth expected to accelerate, driven by reversal of AOV decline, more days versus March quarter and seasonality (summer categories).
Group EBITDA ambition of about $1bn by FY29 was referenced; management said it is not formal guidance and numbers may move.
capex_capacity: Warehousing capacity of 17 million (per analyst) is not disclosed quarter-on-quarter or year-on-year.
Store expansion: the company will not guide beyond 3,000 dark stores; the urban/tier-2 mix is shifting over time, with no numbers given.
Automation is increasing across all warehouses over the next few years; the pace depends on an ROCE framework, with no capex figure given.
Store format: larger or smaller stores are chosen hyperlocally, with no single rule for size.
demand_pricing: Competitive intensity described as high everywhere, with aggressive players in different markets; management said it has not changed meaningfully since the last call.
Management said it will keep pricing discipline, with lower MOV and free delivery in some micro-markets; it will react based on customer retention and frequency, not market share.
Customer retention has not been materially hurt, per management; declining order frequency is driven by new customer additions.
Platform fee increased across customers, while discounts are targeted at price-sensitive cohorts in select geographies.
Management expects advertising to keep rising as a percentage of NOV but gave no ceiling or target.

qa_highlights.question: Does 60% QC growth imply quick commerce margin of around 3-3.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said the math is broadly fine but there is no specific guidance, and the numbers could move.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin of safety in the 60% CAGR if competition worsens?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal said the CAGR is built on assortment, geographic expansion and densification, and that competitive intensity is not expected to last beyond three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be 70-80% given the 3,000 store target?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal confirmed FY27 will not be 100% but gave no number, citing flexibility and possible acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: Is Swiggy's Toing model something Eternal will follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal said there are no plans for Toing; Bistro is a small early experiment that will be watched.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of the drop in orders per customer from ~3.6 to ~3.35?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal said it is largely due to a surge in new customer addition over the last couple of quarters, with little retention impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the number of food delivery partners growing faster than orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Albinder Dhindsa said more part-time riders are joining, which raises active partner counts and lowers orders per rider per shift.

qa_highlights.question: Will food delivery margin upside from the platform fee be reinvested or kept?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal said the company will reinvest incremental margin into growth where ROI is good, and will let margin rise if that stops working.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ad revenue ceiling as a share of GMV affect steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Goyal said the company does not operate with a cap in mind and has no target for ad share of NOV in quick commerce.

Food delivery order per rider has fallen 10-15% over a year, and the rise in part-time riders could affect unit economics.
Customer frequency is falling (per analyst, about 3.6 to 3.35), and management expects it to stabilise as new customer growth normalises.
Higher fuel prices would raise last-mile costs; management expects to pass costs on unless the increase is drastic.
Event cancellations due to artist visa issues could affect District, though management said there is no impact on the outlook.

543320|2026-06.headline: Eternal's Blinkit quick commerce guides long-term EBIT margin to top of range, now 6%, with Q1 flagged as peak competitive intensity.
543320|2026-06.overview: Management spoke almost entirely to Blinkit (quick commerce), with questions also covering food delivery, Bistro, District, Nugget and payables. Management said competition is high but more predictable because it is now mostly subsidies on products and delivery fees, and that discount-led growth is unsustainable. Blinkit net order value (NOV) growth was described as robust, with NAOV expected to stay flat year on year. Management declined to guide Q2 volume growth, and said current EBIT margin is negative, so there is no ROCE yet. The call did not give reported quarterly financial figures beyond those cited in questions.

financial_highlights.change: Moved to higher end of prior range

financial_highlights.value: About 1.8% of NOV, largely perishables; netted in gross profit
financial_highlights.change: Described as asymptotic, not expected to fall materially
Expected to stay in same range; seasonal Q3 uptick possible

financial_highlights.value: 2,100-2,200 orders per store per day cited for new-format stores

segments.commentary: Adding about 10 kitchens per quarter and expanding cautiously. Older kitchens are improving on throughput, menu pricing and operations. Bistro is in a separate entity, with no overlap in food delivery NOV or profit.

segments.commentary: Dining-out and movies are the largest categories, with retail stores and events the more promising newer ones. Customer base is smaller than food delivery or quick commerce, with fewer cities and higher NAOV.

Shifting to larger stores; new-format stores are cited at 2,100-2,200 orders per day, and existing stores are being upgraded to larger properties.

Management said NOV per store per day rose about 60% against the earlier assumption, versus about 150% for capex per store.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise the quick commerce long-term margin guidance to 6% amid competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said capex per store and efficiency gains, plus larger store sizes, give higher margin visibility, so the company expects to finish at the higher end of the earlier range.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 the peak of competitive intensity, and what does predictability mean?
qa_highlights.answer: Albinder Singh Dhindsa said Q1 was the peak seen to date because more players were aggressive. Competition now mainly takes the form of product and delivery-fee subsidies, which he said cannot go much deeper without large losses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Blinkit AOV fall for two quarters, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop is in line with last year and mostly reflects category mix and price matching. NAOV is an outcome, flat YoY, and not expected to grow meaningfully. Q3 may rise on seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Blinkit contribution margin not rise with take rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher minimum wages in several states and larger new stores with lower early contribution. Q1 last-mile costs are seasonally high, and YoY gross profit gains have largely flowed to contribution.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Blinkit capex around INR 700 crore for 200 stores when the stated capex per store is INR 2.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said warehouse capex is lumpy, so the per-store figure should be read over 6-9 months or longer. Over those periods capex per store is below INR 2.5 crore, and management expects that to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the net working capital reduction to 14 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said lower inventory days, from better replenishment and throughput, drove the cut from 18 to 14 days, with a steady-state target of 12 days. Kunal Swarup said the Q1 OCF lift came from a one-off tax refund on higher advance tax.

543320|2026-09.headline: Eternal's Q2FY27 call was Q&A-only: management kept FY29 $1B Adjusted EBITDA guidance and flagged food margins flat for 1-2 years while reinvesting in growth.
543320|2026-09.overview: The call covered only the Q&A session, with no prepared remarks or reported financial figures in the transcript. Management said competitive intensity in food delivery rose in Q2 and that Eternal is investing more in customer acquisition and frequency, with margins expected to stay broadly flat over the next 1-2 years. In quick commerce, management said the 12-month competitive spike is over, which gives it confidence to re-accelerate store expansion, mainly in smaller cities, starting October-December quarter. Management also discussed dark.ai, a privacy-focused AI application for power users, which is unmonetised and carried in the Others segment.

financial_highlights.value: about INR 9 lakh (steady-state target about INR 11 lakh)

blended across tiers; tier 2/3 expected to cost less, no separate figure given
growth expected to pick up YoY from the October-December quarter

segments.commentary: Management plans to accelerate store additions from the October-December quarter, mostly in smaller cities, and expects no short-term margin hit. NOV per store per day is about INR 9 lakh versus a steady-state target of about INR 11 lakh. Blinkit's 1P share is at a steady state of about 90-95% of SKUs. Store capex guidance of INR 2.5 crore is a blended figure.

segments.name: Others (dark.ai and enterprise AI)
segments.commentary: dark.ai has been in development for about a year, is unmonetised and is carried in Others, with costs described as not yet meaningful. Management said the base case is a high gross margin business, but hardware and compute may be needed if demand is strong. Launch is a few months away.

guidance_outlook: Management maintains the FY29 $1 billion Adjusted EBITDA guidance, but said it is too early to comment on it further.
Food delivery margins are expected to remain broadly flattish over the next 1-2 years, with investment in growth prioritised over margin optimisation.
Quick commerce store additions are to accelerate from the October-December quarter, with NOV growth expected to pick up on a YoY basis in that quarter.
Management expects the bulk of new quick commerce stores to be in smaller cities, and expects Blinkit's NOV per store per day to rise over time, though not linearly.
dark.ai launch is a few months away; monetisation and capex decisions will be taken closer to launch.
capex_capacity: Blinkit blended capex per new store is about INR 2.5 crore, and tier 2 and tier 3 stores are expected to cost less, but management did not confirm a separate figure.
Store additions are set to nearly double over the next 6-7 quarters, with the bulk in smaller cities.
NOV per store per day is about INR 9 lakh today versus a steady-state target of about INR 11 lakh; management said growth in store numbers may be lumpy.
dark.ai capex is not expected to be meaningful unless the product gets a very strong response, in which case GPUs and infrastructure may be needed.
Quick commerce SKU mix is at a steady state of 90-95% 1P, so no further incremental working capital build is expected from that.
demand_pricing: Food delivery competitive intensity was higher in Q2, and Eternal is raising investment in new customer acquisition and frequency.
Quick commerce competition rose over the past 12 months with 5-7 players; management says it now has better visibility on competitor strategies.
Blinkit NOV growth is expected to pick up YoY from the October-December quarter. Blinkit's MTU in mature cities is multiple times Zomato's MTU, with no plateau seen yet.

Mature cities (operating more than 2-3 years) account for over 70% of NOV that is EBITDA positive; the share of NOV from top 8 cities is declining directionally, and management did not disclose the figure.
New cities have NAOV about 10-15% lower; assortment expansion in tier 1 cities offsets this. Gourmet stores have expanded to Bengaluru and Mumbai but are not a material share of orders.

qa_highlights.question: Has food delivery discounting intensified in Q2, and have margins peaked?
qa_highlights.answer: Competitive intensity was higher than in prior quarters, partly driven by Zomato. Management expects margins to stay broadly flattish over 1-2 years and to reinvest surplus in growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why accelerate quick commerce store additions in FY28, and where?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition is now more predictable after the 12-month spike. Most new stores will be in smaller cities, where payback is described as strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Blinkit contribution margin trend despite NOV per store rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed flat contribution to investment in new stores. NOV per store does not translate linearly into contribution because store size and gross profit mix also vary.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY29 $1B Adjusted EBITDA guidance more comfortable given better competition visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment beyond maintaining the guidance, noting that only two quarters of the three-year plan have passed.

qa_highlights.question: What is dark.ai, what is its capex and monetisation, and is it within Eternal?
qa_highlights.answer: dark.ai is inside Eternal and unmonetised, with costs carried in Others. It is an application layer on open-source models, with the base case being a high gross margin, self-funding business. Hosting may need GPUs if demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will tier 2 and tier 3 store capex be below INR 2.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 2.5 crore figure is blended across tiers, set with the expectation that most expansion would be in tier 2 cities.

risks_watch: Food delivery competition could keep discounting elevated, which would pressure margins despite the flat-margin stance.
Blinkit store expansion could weigh on contribution margins in the short term and on NOV per store if new-store ramp is slower.
Blinkit's 79% growth reference point and the October-December NOV pickup need to be checked in the next quarterly update.
dark.ai launch timing, monetisation model and possible GPU capex are undefined; commitment to return on capital will be tested.
Share of NOV from top 8 cities is declining; management did not disclose the figure, so the mix shift is hard to track.
Exchange-rate exposure on dollar-priced tech server costs below contribution could raise indirect costs as the business scales.

Management frequently declined to share specific figures, such as the top-8 city NOV share and the 2H food delivery growth assumption.
key_quotes: Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards.
Doing this last year would have been fraught with risk because we didn't know how some of these things would have panned out, and payback on investments are very important for us.
If it works, it will become really big; it's more like a zero-to-one bet at this point.

rows.why: Management is raising spend on new customer acquisition and frequency and will reinvest surplus rather than expand margins, with food delivery margins guided broadly flattish.

543321|2026-03.headline: Tatva Chintan Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,341 million, with EBITDA of INR281 million (about 21% margin); FY27 guidance held at ~25% growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin.
543321|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was INR1,341 million, up 24% YoY and 2% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR281 million, up 214% YoY and 10% QoQ, which management attributed to better product mix and operating leverage. Electrolyte Salts was the standout segment, at INR131 million (up 1,378% YoY), while PTC fell 20% YoY and PASC fell 24% QoQ on dispatch delays after the new Dahej block was commissioned. Management maintained FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin despite raw-material and freight cost inflation linked to the geopolitical conflict, which is being partly passed on to customers. The Jolva greenfield project is set to break ground within about 60 days, with commercial production targeted for early 2028.

qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 25% revenue growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin; cost increases are only partly absorbed by customers, but the guidance was not changed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 ESS run-rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is sustainable at around the same level each quarter; on an annual basis, FY27 ESS revenue could be about 4x Q4, from one application, with the hybrid battery application adding from late 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PASC decline QoQ?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jolva timeline and investment?

543321|2026-06.headline: Tatva Chintan Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 43% YoY to INR1,671 million, with EBITDA up 86% YoY to INR323 million.
543321|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR1,671 million grew 43% YoY and 25% QoQ, and EBITDA of INR323 million rose 86% YoY and 15% QoQ. Growth was led by volume rather than price, with price pass-on only starting about 40-50 days before the call. Electrolyte Salts was the weak spot, down 52% QoQ to INR63 million after raw material shortages linked to the Middle East crisis halted production for several weeks. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 25-30% growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin, and announced a greenfield facility of about INR200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is 60% gross margin sustainable, and how much of the improvement is process versus launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited launches and operational efficiency as the two drivers; launch margins will not drop off sharply, and second-gen processes and ongoing efficiency gains should hold margins near 60% barring a quarter here or there.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide EBITDA margin only 30-32% when Q1 was 36.6%?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ankleshwar and Dahej are on track, Solapur is slightly delayed due to labour slowdown, and existing capacity suffices as Solapur Phase 1 and 1.1 will be loaded with captive intermediates and ROW business.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company looking at acquisitions, and what are the criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is not a constraint and it would not spend on facilities; it is looking at synergistic pipeline-led acquisitions from different platforms that add value to the API plus strategy.

H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,322 crores (+11.1% YoY) with H1 EBITDA margin of 39.3%. rows.label: Pizza Hut revival relaunch and Analyst Day

rows.label: International growth (Nepal, Thailand)
