543330|2026-06.headline: Devyani Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore, with record Operating EBITDA of INR 151 crore (9.6% margin).
543330|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore and Operating EBITDA rose about 38% YoY to INR 151 crore, the company's highest ever, at a 9.6% margin. KFC returned to positive SSSG (3.3%) with dine-in salience improving to 57%, while Pizza Hut remained loss-making at brand contribution level with SSSG of -2.2%. Management flagged LPG, wage and commodity inflation, a weak monsoon outlook and volatile macro, and said Sapphire merger approvals from NSE and BSE were received in June with completion targeted by end FY27.

segments.name: KFC India
segments.commentary: SSSG +3.3%, revenue INR 684 crore (~+12% YoY), gross margin 69.4%, brand contribution INR 115 crore; offline saliency 57%, up over 3 pp YoY. Management targets 59-60% dine-in share and ADS of 105k-110k for 20%+ brand contribution margin.

segments.name: Pizza Hut
segments.commentary: SSSG -2.2% (improving sequentially), ADS up to ~INR 32,400 per store per day, revenue INR 184 crore, gross margin 76.3%, brand contribution loss INR 4 crore; 626 stores at quarter end.

segments.name: Own brands (BBK, Vaango)
segments.commentary: Biryani By Kilo SSSG +7.2%, Vaango +7.1%; combined revenue INR 98 crore, gross margin 65.9%, brand contribution ~INR 10 crore (10.2%). 218 stores including 23 BBK Express; BBK target INR 1,000 crore brand in next few years.

segments.name: Franchise brands (incl. Costa)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew ~6% YoY; gross margin fell to 74.6% on input costs; brand contribution margin 15.1%, up YoY on cost management.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 523 crore, growth above 20% YoY for another quarter; brand contribution margin 18.2%, up 1.5 pp YoY.

guidance_outlook: KFC SSSG expected around 5-6% over the medium term per management; Percy Panthaki's follow-up framed 105k-110k ADS as roughly 1.5-2 years away on that basis.
Brand contribution margin for KFC to cross 20% once ADS passes 105k-110k; management said this is conditional on the current cost environment.
Store opening plan unchanged from earlier guidance; 11 net new KFC and 3 net new BBK stores in India in Q1; 1,855 stores in India and 2,255 globally at June 30, 2026.
Merger with Sapphire Foods expected to complete by end FY27; management said Pizza Hut's full focus would come after the merger, which Vivek Maheshwari confirmed as FY28.
Early Q2 trends: July showed positive trend per management, but Shravan timing creates a drag; Q2 is too early to call.
capex_capacity: Store opening pace in line with prior guidance; 11 net new KFC and 3 net new BBK stores in India in Q1.
Management said there is spare capacity in existing KFC stores, so the dine-in shift needs no additional capex; future formats will stay as currently sized.
BBK Express small-box format (23 stores) being tested in food courts; BBK dine-in and airport formats being piloted.
Technology platform build: core team in-house with outsourcing to Cognizant; tech rollout targeted before merger approval.
demand_pricing: KFC SSSG +3.3%; management reports demand 'stable' and July trends positive, but macro (LPG, rupee, crude) remains a constraint.
Slight price increases taken at KFC and Pizza Hut to offset LPG and commodity costs; KFC gross margin restored to 69.4% through judicious discounting.
KFC marketing rebalanced from deep online discounting toward dine-in visits.
Pizza Hut ADS is low versus peers; management says innovation and price laddering across price points are needed, with product work ongoing.
Franchise brands gross margin fell to 74.6% on higher input costs, offset by better cost management.

qa_highlights.question: What drivers beyond SSSG could lift KFC margins from ~17% and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the key lever is ADS; crossing 105k-110k ADS should take KFC brand contribution above 20%. Other levers are dine-in promotion, operating leverage and technology adoption, which will only deliver a few quarters after the merger.

qa_highlights.question: Can KFC dine-in salience return to 60-65%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65% is not achievable near term given convenience preference, especially in the North; the target is 59-60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SSSG not guided higher after 13 quarters of negative trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited tough macro (rupee, oil, LPG availability) and said a bullish view needs a stable environment that it does not yet see.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Pizza Hut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 3-way structure with Sapphire and Yum! held back decisions and innovation; product, ingredient and price-ladder work is underway, with full push after the merger.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mandate and leadership build-out?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters are supportive on investment; new COO, CTO and CMO have been hired, with joinings ranging from 2 weeks to 2 months; the whole leadership team is now in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Sapphire integration be straightforward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IT stacks and processes are largely similar because technology was run by Yum!, so integration should not be a major challenge.

risks_watch: Inflation in LPG, wages, food commodities and packaging could offset the KFC margin path; management said the ADS target may move if costs rise.
Below-normal monsoon forecast and El Niño risk could weigh on demand.
Pizza Hut remains loss-making at brand contribution level with ADS well below peers.
Merger completion by end FY27 and the technology build-out being ready before merger approval.
Aggregator dynamics and delivery cannibalising dine-in sales; management is shifting marketing toward dine-in.
543330|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on profitability and KFC momentum, but cautious on macro, SSSG outlook and Pizza Hut; management repeatedly said it is too early to call Q2 and that a bullish view requires macro stability.
key_quotes: The business has improved profitability and posted its highest ever EBITDA of INR 255 crore at 16.1% of the revenues.

So the key lever for ADS, as you know, is a combination of SSSG in the existing stores, as well as the quality of new stores that we are opening, so that we are able to start the new stores at a higher ADS number.

So, Vivek, this hypothesis used to play when delivery was new, and I am talking about, let us say, post-COVID period, because that was giving us net addition in terms of top line, and on an incremental basis, it made sense .
Today, we have excess capacity available in our stores, whereby we can easily make the shift without incurring additional capex.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: KFC brand contribution rose about 22% with margin up 1.4 pp, consolidated Operating EBITDA hit a record INR 151 crore (9.6% margin, +38% YoY), and KFC brand contribution is guided above 20% once ADS reaches 105k-110k, roughly 1.5-2 years away, conditional on costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Store additions continue at pace: 11 net new KFC and 3 net new BBK stores in Q1 FY27, taking India stores to 1,855 and global to 2,255, though management said future formats stay as currently sized with no major new capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: KFC SSSG of +3.3% with July trends positive, store additions of 11 KFC and 3 BBK in Q1, and International revenue growing above 20% YoY to INR 523 crore; Pizza Hut ADS is still low at about INR 32,400 per store per day.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said capex is not changing and spare capacity exists in existing KFC stores, so the dine-in shift needs no additional capex; no utilisation figure was disclosed to support a new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management refused to guide SSSG above the 5-6% medium-term range and said a bullish view needs a stable macro it does not yet see; KFC SSSG was +3.3% in Q1 after 13 quarters of negative trends.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged LPG, wage and commodity inflation, a below-normal monsoon and El Nino risk, and said the ADS target may move if costs rise; Q2 is too early to call and Shravan timing is a drag.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pizza Hut product, ingredient and price-ladder work is underway with full push after the merger (FY28), and BBK Express, dine-in and airport formats are in trials with 23 BBK Express stores; no firm launch dates were given.

rows.label: Sapphire Foods merger completion
rows.why: NSE and BSE approvals received in June and management continues to expect completion by end of FY27; Pizza Hut's full focus is set for FY28 after the merger.

rows.label: BBK brand scale-up to INR 1,000 crore
rows.why: Own brands revenue is INR 98 crore in Q1 with BBK SSSG +7.2% and 218 stores; the INR 1,000 crore ambition is a multi-year objective with no interim timeline.

rows.label: Dine-in shift and marketing rebalancing at KFC
rows.why: KFC dine-in salience rose to 57% (up over 3 pp YoY) with a 59-60% target, and marketing is moving away from deep online discounting, supporting KFC brand contribution margin.

tone.note: Management was confident on record EBITDA, KFC's return to positive SSSG and the merger timeline, but cautious on macro, the 5-6% SSSG path and Pizza Hut, and analysts pushed on SSSG and ADS timing.

543330|2026-09.headline: Devyani Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10.4% YoY to INR 1,519 crore and operating EBITDA rose about 34% to INR 125 crore (pre-Ind AS).
543330|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 10.4% YoY to INR 1,519 crore, with KFC and international driving growth and Pizza Hut still declining. Operating EBITDA (pre-Ind AS) rose about 34% to INR 125 crore, margin 8.2% versus 6.8%, and the company posted Q2 PBT of INR 5.7 crore against a loss last year. Management flagged strong raw material, LPG and state minimum wage inflation, with only a small 1-2% YTD price increase so far. The Sapphire Foods merger received CCI approval; SEBI no-objection and NCLT approval remain pending, with closing targeted by fiscal year-end.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA (as stated in Chairman's remarks, likely Ind AS basis)

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR 24 crore last year
brand contribution INR 91 crore, margin 17.9%, +1.2 pp YoY

segments.name: KFC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 642 crore (+12.3% YoY); SSSG 4.4%; gross margin 68.2% (flat); brand contribution margin 13.9% (flat); 50 net adds taking network to 844 stores; on-premise saliency 56%.

segments.name: Pizza Hut
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 184 crore (nearly flat YoY); SSSG -1.4% (decline narrowed QoQ); ADS INR 32,000 per store per day; gross margin 76.7%; brand contribution margin -1.8% (loss INR 3.3 crore); 632 stores after 6 net adds.

segments.name: Own Brands (Biryani By Kilo, Vaango)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 95 crore (+~11% YoY); BBK SSSG 8.1%, Vaango SSSG 6.9%; gross margin 65.4% vs 62.6%; brand contribution INR 9 crore (9.4%); 225 stores including 26 BBK Express.

segments.name: Franchisee brands (Costa)
segments.commentary: Franchise portfolio revenue grew about 7% YoY; Costa SSSG 9.9%, gross margin 74.2% (vs 73.6%), brand contribution margin 15.5%; 202 stores.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 509 crore with brand contribution INR 91 crore (17.9%); Thailand flooding in September disrupted business and fuel costs weighed on consumers.

guidance_outlook: Full-year net new store additions guided at 200-220; company says it is on track.
KFC standalone store additions guided at 100-110 for FY27; management says it will deliver.
Merged-entity guidance to be revisited after CCI approval; management will engage and come back.
Merger with Sapphire Foods targeted to close by end of current fiscal year (FY27), pending SEBI no-objection and NCLT approval.
Q3 SSSG targeted to be slightly better than Q2; Q2 SSSG levels described as sustainable.
Biryani By Kilo brand contribution target of about 14-15% in short to medium term.
capex_capacity: Store footprint at 1,923 in India and 2,325 globally as of September 30, 2026; 70 net adds in Q2 (68 in India).
Revamped business development structure now in place; management says it is firing and phasing of openings has been shifted between quarters without changing full-year numbers.
Pizza Hut to add stores selectively, replacing underperforming closures.
Own Brands network at 225 stores; BBK Express format being tested at food courts.
demand_pricing: SSSG across India brands ranged 4% to 9% (excluding Pizza Hut), with growth described as transaction-led and on-premise led.
Price hikes limited to 1-2% YTD, staggered to protect muted consumer sentiment; management says price increases still on the agenda.
KFC value architecture: INR 99 and INR 149 meal combos, Wednesday value offer, BOGO offers in select markets.

Q2 seasonality: Navratri moved into October (north and west skew) while Durga Puja shifted into the next quarter (south and east skew, where KFC is strong); management expects Q2+Q3 combined to be similar to peers.
North region KFC SSSG reported at +20%; management says on a regional basis it is in line with or slightly ahead of peers.
Competition and macro: food and fuel inflation, job losses from AI adoption cited as pressures on household budgets.

qa_highlights.question: Why has KFC lagged some peers sequentially, and what is October trending like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed part of the gap to Navratri shifting into Q2 for peers, while Durga Puja (a KFC tailwind in south and east) shifted into Q3; expects Q2+Q3 to be similar to peers and targets Q3 SSSG slightly above Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is Pizza Hut moving to a value-focused, transaction-led strategy post-merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus is innovation pipeline, entry-level price laddering and dine-in; value offers are tied to multiple price points, with rollout of similar BOGO-type offers over the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is inflation fully in the P&L or are there further headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw materials (chicken, oil, paper) are stabilising but not fully passed on; minimum wage hikes are fully baked in, with possible small additional state hikes; gas prices doubled YoY and are stable, with pricing the only variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will KFC gross margin fall further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current price increases are baked in and it does not expect gross margin to deteriorate further, though further price increases remain on the agenda and promotions are a lever.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Biryani By Kilo's turnaround and can it reach 20%+ margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is brand contribution of about 14-15% in the short to medium term, driven by procurement scale, store labour efficiency and supervisory layer efficiency, plus positive SSSG leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Can KFC SSSG for Q2+Q3 be 8-9% as Sapphire indicated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on Sapphire; said Q2 SSSG is sustainable and Q3 is targeted slightly better. North KFC SSSG was +20% to illustrate seasonality impact.

qa_highlights.question: Will KFC store additions slow given near-term headwinds and the merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no reason to slow KFC expansion given under-penetration vs pizza and chicken demand; KFC guidance of 100-110 stores is unchanged, and phasing is being shifted ahead of post-merger reset.

qa_highlights.question: Will Pizza Hut's strategic plan be shared soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet; management will share more colour once the merger is consummated, after understanding Sapphire's Pizza Hut granular performance.

risks_watch: Sustained raw material (chicken, oil, paper), LPG (nearly double YoY) and state minimum wage inflation versus the limited 1-2% price increase taken so far.
Pizza Hut SSSG still negative at -1.4% with negative brand contribution (-1.8%); turnaround plan not yet detailed.
Merger execution: pending SEBI no-objection and NCLT approval; management expects post-merger management reset and possible slowdown in store openings.
Heightened food-authority inspections disrupting store operations; consistency of enforcement uncertain.
Thailand flooding and higher fuel costs weighing on international demand; merged-entity guidance still to be issued.
Macro: management expects discretionary spending to stay under pressure as interest rates begin to rise.
543330|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operating execution and store expansion, but cautious on consumer demand and the near-term cost outlook. Management was evasive on peer comparisons and Sapphire's numbers and deferred Pizza Hut strategy and merged guidance to later.
key_quotes: This is one of the best Q2 operating EBITDA numbers that we have seen and the same helped us post profit before taxes of INR 5.7 crore for the quarter against a loss last year.
We are building the business for the future, we are not building for near term.
Pricing is the only variable.

rows.why: Operating EBITDA margin rose to 8.2% from 6.8% and gross margin is up 70 bps to 68.5%, but raw material, LPG and minimum wage inflation is only partly passed on with 1-2% YTD price hikes, and management sees no further gross margin deterioration yet.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Net new store additions of 200-220 for FY27 are reaffirmed as on track after 70 net adds in Q2 (68 in India), and KFC is guided to 100-110 standalone additions with 50 done in Q2 and 844 stores now.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: SSSG across India brands runs 4% to 9% (ex Pizza Hut), KFC Q2 SSSG 4.4% is called sustainable, and Q3 SSSG is targeted slightly better than Q2, though Pizza Hut SSSG is still -1.4%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed store guidance but gave no revenue or margin upgrade, and merged-entity guidance is still to be revisited after CCI approval with discretionary spend under pressure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects a post-merger management reset that could slow store openings, and Pizza Hut SSSG is -1.4% with brand contribution at -1.8%, while merged-entity guidance is still pending.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BBK Express food-court format is being tested across 26 stores, and Pizza Hut plans BOGO-type value offers over the next couple of quarters, though no firm launch dates were given.

rows.label: Sapphire Foods merger closing
rows.why: CCI approval is received and management is optimistic about closing by fiscal year-end, but SEBI no-objection and NCLT approval are still pending.

rows.label: Biryani By Kilo margin to 14-15%
rows.why: BBK SSSG is 8.1% and brand contribution is 9.4% today against a 14-15% target, driven by procurement scale, store labour efficiency and positive SSSG leverage.

rows.label: Further price increases
rows.why: Only 1-2% YTD price hikes have been taken against raw material, LPG and minimum wage inflation, and management says further price increases remain on the agenda but are staggered to protect demand.

tone.note: Management was confident on store expansion (200-220 net adds reaffirmed) and Q2 SSSG sustainability, but cautious on consumer demand and cost pressure, and it was evasive on Sapphire's numbers and peer comparisons, deferring Pizza Hut strategy and merged guidance.

543331|2026-03.headline: Meghmani Organics FY26 standalone revenue rose 4% to INR 2,091 crore and EBITDA 27% to INR 228.7 crore, but Q4 standalone EBITDA was only INR 26.2 crore.
543331|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: US tariffs, a weaker export environment and the US-Iran war pushed raw material costs up while realisations stayed broadly flat. Standalone EBITDA recovered 27% for the full year, but Q4 remained thin, with Crop Protection margin near 9% and Pigments near 3%. Management suspended TiO2 operations as unviable after the anti-dumping duty was withdrawn and sulphuric acid prices spiked. Management guided to Crop Protection margins of 15-17% in FY27, double-digit Crop Protection top-line growth, and a Nano fertiliser ramp-up, and announced an amalgamation of two subsidiaries and a Brazil subsidiary.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA up 24% YoY; margin vs 6.9% prior year

segments.name: Crop Protection (FY26)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,631 crore (about 78% of standalone revenue), EBITDA INR 244 crore, margin 15%; production about 40,371 MT at about 72% utilisation. Q4 revenue INR 348.6 crore, EBITDA INR 31.3 crore, margin about 9%.

segments.name: Pigments (FY26)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 461 crore (about 22% of revenue), EBITDA INR 15 crore, margin 3.3%; production about 13,191 MT at 40% utilisation. Q4 revenue INR 108 crore, EBITDA INR 3.2 crore, margin about 3%.

segments.name: Crop Nutrition
segments.commentary: Nano fertiliser products (Nano DAP, Nano NPK, Nano Zinc) received Ministry of Agriculture approval, to be made at Sanand, Gujarat with no additional capex. Commercial production expected in the Kharif season; Nano Urea is the key product, with about 7-8 products in the basket. No segment financials disclosed.

segments.name: Titanium Dioxide (Kilburn)
segments.commentary: Operations temporarily suspended as commercially unviable after the anti-dumping duty withdrawal, higher sulphuric acid and utility costs. Anti-dumping matter is under DGTR review.

guidance_outlook: Crop Protection: management expects EBITDA margin within 15-17% in FY27, and double-digit top-line growth with better profitability than Q4.
Pigments: top line of about INR 500-600 crore; FY27 profitability expected to be better than FY26's 3.3% margin, though not dramatically so.
Crop Nutrition: significant growth in top line and bottom line over the next 2-5 years; management declined to give quarter-wise timing and said FY27 as a whole will show growth.
Capex: no significant capex in FY27; routine capex of INR 35-40 crore. Working capital to improve through inventory and receivable-day reduction.
Dividend: management said it will try to provide a reasonably good dividend in FY27, subject to Board approval.
Renewable energy: 3.3 MW wind-solar hybrid power agreement, taking renewable share of energy use above 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pay a dividend, given no dividend in recent years?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend was declared for FY26; management said it will try to provide a reasonably good dividend in FY27, subject to Board approval, based on better revenue and profitability.

qa_highlights.question: When will the TiO2 anti-dumping duty be restored and when will sulphuric acid prices stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a DGTR announcement on TiO2 anti-dumping duty within 1-2 months, but could not predict sulphuric acid price normalisation and hoped the war and Strait of Hormuz disruption end soon.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Protection margins reach the long-term range in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 15-17% Crop Protection EBITDA margin range for FY27, saying Q4 was hit by inability to pass on price increases that is now gradually easing.

qa_highlights.question: What are the quantified synergies from the amalgamation of Kilburn and Meghmani Crop Nutrition?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantified synergies were given; benefits cited were reduced compliance across entities, combined customer-facing teams, resource optimisation and utilisation of cash held in the subsidiaries. The Court has directed a vote on June 6.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and capex plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant capex; routine capex of INR 35-40 crore. Working capital to improve through inventory rationalisation and lower receivable days.

qa_highlights.question: When will Nano Urea and other Nano products show revenue impact, and are orders in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined quarter-wise guidance, saying some orders will come in Q1 and Q2 and the full year will show significant growth; it confirmed existing orders and expects more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nano Urea sell-out rate and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give sell-out data. It said IFFCO has the upper hand due to conventional urea presence, and Meghmani's Nano product basket is being expanded.

No significant capex planned in FY27; routine capex of INR 35-40 crore.
Nano fertiliser products (Nano DAP, Nano NPK, Nano Zinc) to be made at the existing Sanand, Gujarat facility with no additional capex; Nano Urea made in the same plant.

TiO2 operations suspended; minimal operating cost retained and no capex planned for the unit.

Management attributed the consumer group's slowdown (revenue +4%) mainly to a base effect from the September 2025 GST cut and a festive season that shifted into October and November, and guided Q3 to be the best quarter in company history.

financial_highlights.value: Consumer/OLX other income INR 4.41 crore in OLX vs INR 13.51 crore last year
financial_highlights.change: Down; total other income down about 19% YoY in Q2 per management

76 million average (as stated) and 43 million monthly unique traffic (as asked by analyst)

segments.name: Consumer group (New Auto: CarWale, BikeWale)
segments.commentary: Revenue from operations +4% YoY, EBITDA +5%, margin 41%, PAT +13%; H1 revenue +10% and EBITDA +16%. Management attributed the slowdown to the high base of Q2 last year (37% growth in the quarter).

segments.name: Remarketing (SAMIL / Shriram Automall)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12% in the quarter and +13% half-yearly; EBITDA margin about 30% and PAT +47% in the quarter, driven by retail online auctions with the highest margins. Management said listed vehicles were about 1.56 million and auctioned about 2.35 lakh (annualised for Q2).

segments.name: OLX
segments.commentary: Revenue +26% YoY in the quarter and +28% half-yearly; EBITDA +36% with margin 32%; PAT declined on lower other income and 58% higher tax. Management guided growth to exceed 26% and reach 30-35% in coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 expected to be the best quarter in company history across most businesses, with highest-ever revenue; management declined to give a sequential growth rate for Q3.
Group EBITDA expected to grow sequentially at a similar rate (about 20%) from Q2 to Q3; management pointed to a path toward 40% group EBITDA margin.
OLX growth expected to exceed 26% and reach 30-35% in coming quarters, driven by existing products plus Elite Buyer, Elite Seller and e-commerce.
VAYA Live expected to roll out for OEMs/dealers and consumers sometime in the current quarter, becoming a flagship product over the next one to three quarters.
Long-term goal of about INR 1,000 crore PAT in four to five years, which management said is directionally on track.

No buyback or dividend possible this year under current regulation because the standalone tax benefit continues for one or two more years; cash to be used for M&A if found, otherwise distributions later.
capex_capacity: Management said the business is asset-light: no material capex and no meaningful working capital requirement, with most profits converting to cash.
VAYA tech costs described as largely fixed; no material change expected from VAYA rollout, with token and compute costs being optimised.
Landmark partnership for OLX car commerce: management is still working out whether CarTrade should invest part of working capital, depending on margin sharing.
Commerce platform with escrow and logistics for non-auto categories (mobiles, white goods) in product development; no date given beyond coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Management said there was no change in OEM vs dealer mix (about 65-70% OEM per earlier comment; CFO later said about 74% of consumer revenue from OEMs, up 3-4 points partly due to last year's timing).
Consumer revenue growth attributed to volume and conversion, not price escalation; lead generation is the largest revenue component.
Industry growth was concentrated in the September 2025 GST-cut period; management cited FADA data showing Navratri 2026 sales below last year's.

Traffic decline attributed to GST-related enthusiasm last year and the festive season shifting about 10 days into October; management said AI is not affecting genuine users and leads and organic share is 96%.
Management said online share of OEM spends is rising, with classifieds at about 18-20% of total OEM spend and a long runway vs 40-60% in developed markets.
OLX Elite Buyer launched about 30 days before the call with a 'massive uptake'; management declined to give an updated buyer count. Elite Seller is now a significant part of seller revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the consumer revenue slowdown is base effect or seasonality versus broader OEM ad-spend pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a complete base effect from the September 2025 GST cut, when Q2 last year grew 37%. It said OEM behaviour has not changed and that October 2026 would be the best month in New Auto history.

qa_highlights.question: Will OLX revenue growth accelerate, given product cadence?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said growth will exceed 26% and be stronger in the coming two quarters, driven mainly by existing products, with Elite Buyer, Elite Seller, Landmark car partnership and e-commerce adding later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise at OLX (about 15-16% QoQ) but fall about 12% in consumer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs were shifted: more investment in used cars at OLX and lower CarWale used-car management costs, since both businesses are common. It said the overall cost level is stable.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the standalone or consumer revenue is lead generation and what drives growth, volume or price?
qa_highlights.answer: Lead generation is the largest component. Growth comes from volume and conversion improvements, not rate escalations.

qa_highlights.question: Can cash be returned via buyback, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distribution is currently not permitted by regulation because the standalone tax benefit continues for one or two more years, so no buyback or dividend this year. Cash may go to M&A if a target is found.

qa_highlights.question: Will VAYA Live add material cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost is not material: it is built on AI code and proprietary data, avoiding LLM data costs, and the tech cost base is fixed.

VAYA Live and commerce product launches are promised within the quarter or in coming quarters; delivery is unproven.

543334|2026-03.headline: Nuvoco posted record FY26 volume of 20.4 Mt and Q4 EBITDA of INR590 crore, but guided Q1 fuel cost to INR1.51-1.55/mn kcal and ~INR200/t cost inflation.
543334|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 volume of 20.4 million tons and EBITDA of INR1,881 crore, with Q4 the first 6 Mt quarter and a record quarterly EBITDA of INR590 crore. Price hikes of INR8-12/bag (trade) and INR10-15/bag (non-trade) were taken in April to offset fuel, packaging and gypsum inflation. Management said the hikes only just cover current cost inflation, leaving a gap of roughly INR200/t against the full cost increase. Net debt rose to INR4,445 crore at FY26-end, driven by the Vadraj acquisition, CCD and VEGL investments.

financial_highlights.change: first time a quarter crossed 6 Mt
vs INR3,640 crore at start of FY26; Dec-25 INR4,817 crore

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Plants running near 95% utilisation; petcoke share cut from 55-60% to about 50%, with a target of 45% using domestic coal. Vadraj capacity expected to ease shortfalls once commissioned.

segments.commentary: Clinker and grinding units to be commissioned in phases between Q3 FY27 and Q1 FY28; capex INR627 crore in FY27 and INR728 crore in FY28 (per management, largely Vadraj refurbishment).

April packaging bag cost up ~INR100/t (granule price moved from INR99/kg in February to INR155/kg); May-June outlook uncertain.
Mineral gypsum import costs seen rising ~INR20/t.
Total cost inflation estimated at ~INR200/t; April price hikes do not fully cover it.

qa_highlights.answer: Jojobera and Panagarh hardware complete, awaiting CTO; Jajpur in 2-3 months and Arasmeta by end-2026; all expected online by end-FY27 once CTO is received.

qa_highlights.question: Current kcal cost and Q1/Q2 fuel outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 blended fuel INR1.44/mn kcal (coal INR1.27, petcoke INR1.84, AFR INR0.9). Q1 guided INR1.51-1.55 as petcoke moves to INR2.01; Q2 to rise further as later-booked shipments arrive.

qa_highlights.question: Packaging cost impact in March and April, and petcoke flexibility?
qa_highlights.answer: March impact ~INR20/t; April ~INR100/t across bags, granules and conversion. Petcoke share to fall 300-500 bps in East and 200-300 bps in North, with FGD gypsum replacing mineral gypsum.

qa_highlights.question: Are April price hikes sustainable through monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is fairly confident hikes will hold near term if cost inflation stops; further inflation would be passed on, and it is not 1-to-1 pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt rose in Q4 and FY26 — why?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: FY26 net debt rose INR900 crore to INR4,445 crore due to Vadraj (INR1,800 crore) and VEGL (INR200 crore) investments, offset by INR900 crore CCD. Chairman-level comment: like-for-like debt fell ~INR300 crore from operations.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex and debt guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex INR900 crore in FY27 and INR960 crore in FY28; leverage to 2x-2.5x EBITDA target within FY27, with debt elevated for a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth 7-9%; Nuvoco aims to match it, with North at ~95% utilisation and possible cement shortfall in North for some months after Vadraj until commissioning.

543334|2026-06.headline: Nuvoco Q1 FY27: volume up 5% YoY to 5.3 mt and EBITDA up 7% to INR572 crore, highest-ever Q1 for both.
543334|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volume rose 5% YoY to 5.3 million tons and EBITDA rose 7% YoY to INR572 crore, the company's highest-ever first-quarter volume and EBITDA. Realisation rose about INR320 per ton QoQ, largely offset by about INR230 per ton of cost inflation (power and fuel, raw material, packing bags, freight, fixed-cost deleverage), leaving a net EBITDA gain of about INR90 per ton. Management said the Surat grinding unit (2 mtpa) was inaugurated on 11 July 2026, ahead of schedule, and Kutch clinker and grinding remain on track for phased start from Q3 FY27. Management guided Q2 cost increase of about INR100 per ton, with power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton and packing and freight easing.

financial_highlights.value: Up about INR320 per ton QoQ (Q1 vs Q4)
financial_highlights.change: Cost inflation about INR230 per ton; net EBITDA impact about INR90 per ton
vs INR5,274 crore a year earlier (about INR600 crore lower)
FY27 capex guidance INR900 crore unchanged

segments.commentary: Risda petcoke share cut from about 37% to about 25% and Arasmeta at zero petcoke, using Sonepur Bazari coal and sweetener. Jojobera and Panagarh CTOs are nearly done; Jajpur awaits NIPL certificate; Arasmeta targeted for end FY27.

segments.commentary: Surat 2 mtpa grinding inaugurated 11 July 2026; sales in Gujarat currently about 1.3-1.4 mt, targeted near 2 mtpa annualised by Q4 FY27. Kutch clinker and grinding phased from Q3 FY27; Sachana bulk terminal targeted Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 total cost expected to rise about INR100 per ton QoQ (give or take INR20-30); power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton due to kiln and mill shutdowns, with packing bag costs seen cooling INR20-25 per ton and freight easing with the lean-season discount from 1 August.
Fuel cost expected to stay broadly flat in Q2 (1.52 could move to 1.55); petcoke inventory adequate for the quarter at similar cost; Q3 may carry higher-cost inventory.
FY27 volume growth target of about 7-8%, in line with market demand expectations of 7-8% over the next three quarters.

Sachana bulk cement terminal with dedicated railway siding: work commenced, targeted operational by Q2 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Given Surat is online, what volume is expected this year and what is the clinker source before Kutch starts?
qa_highlights.answer: Gujarat sales of about 1.3-1.4 mt now; target about 2 mtpa annualised by Q4 FY27. Clinker for the incremental volume comes from the Chhattisgarh cluster and bartering; Kutch clinker expected to supply Surat from start of FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of East debottlenecking (CTOs for Jojobera, Panagarh, Jajpur, Arasmeta)?
qa_highlights.answer: Jojobera and Panagarh CTOs almost done; Jajpur awaits NIPL certificate; Arasmeta technical design done and ball mill procurement underway. All four to be ready by end FY27 and needed for FY28; no delay per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 realisation gain was price versus trade mix and geo-mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Three drivers: price increases (biggest), premium mix with Concreto, Duraguard Microfiber and Uno (about 5 mt premium and super-premium), and geo-mix shift toward high-realisation states (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Western MP). Trade mix unchanged at 75%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook for Q2 and fuel and packing trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Total cost up about INR100 per ton QoQ (plus or minus INR20-30). Petcoke inventory covers Q2 at similar cost; packing bags to ease INR20-25 per ton; rake availability improving to about 4 per day; power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton from shutdowns.

qa_highlights.question: Will Gujarat (Surat and Kutch) EBITDA per ton converge with the company average, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Year 1 EBITDA per ton will be lower due to high costs and aggressive volume push, with no dilution of price intended; modelling shows Gujarat EBITDA per ton equal to rest-of-North in years 2-3. Kutch, Sachana and Surat form a hub-and-spoke network.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any change to FY27 capex and what is the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex unchanged at INR900 crore with about INR370 crore spent in Q1; FY28 capex INR950-1,000 crore including Vadraj, Sachana terminal and routine spend.

543334|2026-09.headline: Nuvoco Q2 FY27: volume up 9% YoY and revenue up ~14%, but energy cost rose ~INR90/ton QoQ; Q3 fuel guided to INR1.8/mn kcal from INR1.59.
543334|2026-09.overview: Management described a challenging quarter driven by a renewed Middle East escalation, petcoke and domestic coal price spikes, and monsoon disruption in the East. Volume grew 9% YoY, revenue about 14% and EBITDA about 11%, supported by premiumization at a record 45% and trade mix of 75%. Fuel cost rose from INR1.52 to INR1.59 per million kcal in Q2, and management guided Q3 to INR1.8 with about INR100-120/ton net cost inflation QoQ, offset by an October price hike of about INR20/ton. Vadraj's Surat grinding unit (2 MTPA) was commissioned in late September, and net debt rose above INR5,000 crore on working capital and capex, with a guided return to 2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA in the next 4-6 quarters.

segments.name: Gujarat (Vadraj / Surat & Kutch)
segments.commentary: Surat 2 MTPA grinding unit commissioned in late September; running at ~1.5 MTPA annualised, targeting 2 MTPA in Q4 FY27 with 50-60% utilisation in Q4 and 70-75% in FY28. Kutch clinker line expected in Q4 FY27, with jetty operational by first week of December.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Strong volume growth in Q2 per management. Around 1 million tons of cement capacity to be released from Rajasthan from Q4 for North sales, as Surat supplies Gujarat.

segments.name: East
segments.commentary: Erratic monsoon weighed on demand in Q2; East expansion deferred from Q3-Q4 FY27 to Q1-Q2 FY28. Price hike of about INR20/ton in trade and non-trade taken in October.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 fuel cost guided at INR1.8 per million kcal vs INR1.59 in Q2, adding ~INR70-80/ton energy cost QoQ; Q4 could add a further INR70-80/ton in a worst case.
Q3 FY27 net cost inflation guided at INR100-120/ton QoQ (energy ~INR70-80, packing bags ~INR20, busy-season surcharge waiver ~INR10), offset by ~INR20/ton price increase taken in October.
Industry demand expected at ~8% growth in H2 FY27; company guides 8-9% blended volume growth across North, West and East.
FY27 capex ~INR1,200 crore (INR780 crore spent in H1, ~INR420 crore in H2); FY28 capex INR800-900 crore.
Net debt expected to return to around March 2026 levels by end FY27; 2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA in the next 4-6 quarters, and below 2x once Vadraj volumes scale.
Surat incremental costs of ~INR30-40 crore expected in Q3 (interest and depreciation), partly above and below EBITDA.
Vadraj/Gujarat EBITDA per ton expected to match Nuvoco's all-India EBITDA per ton around FY29 (possibly FY28 Q4 to Q1 FY29).
Company targets 35 MTPA cement capacity by FY28.
capex_capacity: Surat (Vadraj) 2 MTPA grinding unit at Limla, Surat commissioned late September 2026; ~3,500-3,600 tons/day peak output against ~5,500 tons/day capacity.
Kutch clinker/grinding project on track: phased operations from Q3 FY27, clinker line December, Kutch clinker to Surat via barge once jetty is operational.
Viramgam (Sachana) bulk cement terminal with railway siding under construction; INR50 crore spend planned in H2 FY27.
East debottlenecking delayed from Q3-Q4 FY27 to Q1-Q2 FY28 to prioritise Vadraj cash flow and management bandwidth.
CleanMax agreement for 46.4 MW wind-solar hybrid project in Rajasthan, expected ~100 million units/year.
demand_pricing: Industry demand grew in Q2 but varied regionally; monsoon disrupted the East while low-rainfall regions performed better. Prices did not improve as expected in Q2.

Price action: non-trade up ~INR20-25/ton in North after 15 September, trade cut INR5-7/ton in North in late September, then ~INR20/ton increases in non-trade (North and East) and trade (East) in October.
Premium product mix at 45%; Duraguard Microfiber and Concreto Uno each crossed 1 million ton volumes, with Concreto Uno reaching it in under 18 months.
Management expects post-Diwali demand pickup and believes price increases will hold through the balance of the year.
Management sees 5% demand impact only if back-to-back adverse monsoon or drought years occur; assumes this does not happen in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What was average fuel cost in Q2 and what is the spot impact at petcoke near $187?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel cost rose from INR1.52 to INR1.59 per million kcal (energy ~INR1,080/ton vs INR1,005 in Q1). Q3 is guided at INR1.8, adding ~INR70-80/ton, with petcoke covered for Q3 and Q4 through mid-February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the overall Q3 vs Q2 cost outlook and how will it be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cost inflation of INR100-120/ton: energy +INR70-80, packing +INR20, raw materials ~+INR10, offset by ~INR20/ton price increase plus fixed-cost leverage from higher volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat's utilisation and run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Running at ~1.5 MTPA annualised; target 2 MTPA in Q4 FY27 with 50-60% utilisation in Q4 and 70-75% in FY28, as Kutch grinding is not available in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex ~INR1,200 crore (INR780 crore in H1, ~INR420 crore in H2, of which INR1,000 crore for Vadraj); FY28 INR800-900 crore. East expansion delayed 6-8 months to FY28 H1.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt evolve and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt crossed INR5,000 crore (INR200 crore working capital build plus capex). Expected to return to March 2026 levels by end FY27, and to hover at 2-2.5x EBITDA over 4-6 quarters, with the long-term target below 2x.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest expense fall and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing costs for Surat were capitalised until commercial operations started in late September; interest and depreciation will rise QoQ from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 reported tax rate 41.6% because MAT credit is unavailable under the old regime; the company will decide on regime transition within 3-4 months and share the implications.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Vadraj EBITDA per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gujarat and Western Maharashtra EBITDA per ton expected to match Nuvoco's all-India level in year 3 (FY29, possibly FY28 Q4 to Q1 FY29), subject to cost inflation being offset by prices.

risks_watch: Petcoke prices near $190 with potential to exceed $200/ton; full impact of high-cost petcoke expected from March 2027 onwards.
Domestic coal auction premiums and rake shortages; linkage coal supply expected to ease from early November.
Price hikes must hold post-Diwali; any reversal would erode the expected Q3 benefit.
Surat clinker is currently sourced from Chhattisgarh and Chittor at high cost until Kutch clinker starts; the Q3 to Q4 margin dent was not quantified on the call.
Net debt at above INR5,000 crore vs the INR3,500-4,000 crore comfort range; deleveraging depends on H2 working capital release.
Tax regime transition decision pending; affects tax rate from FY28.
Geopolitical developments (Middle East) remain a watch item.
543334|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operational execution and pricing actions, and candid about the cost shock. Management was evasive on specifics where variables were still moving: Q4 fuel cost, Surat clinker delta and regional growth splits were deferred to follow-up.
key_quotes: Overall, we are looking at as a company, from the current run rate of 1.5 annualized tons per annualized volume, we'll go to 2 million tons in Q4 this year.
And once the monsoon ends and the festival ends, I think construction activity will pick up speed going forward.
So, the average INR20 price increase should totally defray the cost increase, and we'll have a delta benefit in realization in Q3 versus Q2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Surat 2 MTPA grinding unit commissioned late September, running ~1.5 MTPA annualised with target 2 MTPA in Q4 FY27 at 50-60% Q4 utilisation; Kutch clinker line due December and ~1 MT released from Rajasthan from Q4.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management holds 8-9% blended volume growth for H2 FY27 vs industry ~8%, with Q2 volume up 9% YoY and Surat/Kutch adding capacity; East growth weak with monsoon disruption.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex raised to ~INR1,200 crore (INR780 crore spent in H1 vs original INR450-460 crore plan) and FY28 guided at INR800-900 crore, with Viramgam terminal (INR50 crore) under construction; capex is front-ended rather than newly announced.

rows.why: Prices did not improve as expected in Q2 and fuel cost is rising INR1.52 to INR1.59 to INR1.8, so upside to margin or revenue guidance looks limited.

rows.why: Net debt rose above INR5,000 crore vs INR4,500-odd crore in March 2026 and guidance is 2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA within 4-6 quarters, dependent on H2 working capital release.

rows.why: Management expects Gujarat EBITDA/ton to converge with all-India around year 3 (FY29), subject to cost inflation being offset by prices, with Surat utilisation at 70-75% only in FY28.

543336|2026-03.headline: Chemplast Q4 FY26 net loss of INR45 crores on INR898 crore CCVL impairment; consolidated EBITDA rose to INR194 crores from INR37 crores.
543336|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to INR1,256 crores and EBITDA jumped to INR194 crores from INR37 crores, but the company posted a net loss of INR45 crores. The quarter absorbed an INR898 crore non-cash impairment on the investment in CCVL (suspension PVC) and a INR150 crore exceptional charge at CCVL for onerous contracts and raw material write-down. Management said suspension PVC spreads are at roughly breakeven on a replacement-cost basis because of Chinese carbide PVC imports, while specialty chemicals grew 13%. The Board also formed a committee of three independent directors to review strategic priorities, reorganisation and M&A.

financial_highlights.value: INR898 crores vs book value INR1,556 crores

financial_highlights.metric: CCVL exceptional charge (onerous contracts, RM write-down)

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (Paste PVC, CMC, refrigerant gases)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR475 crores, up 13% YoY, with volumes up 17% YoY mainly from paste PVC; Cuddalore paste PVC ran at 100% of capacity through the year. Revenue share was 38% of Q4 total.

segments.name: Value-added Chemicals (caustic soda, chloromethanes, hydrogen peroxide)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR120 crores vs INR169 crores a year earlier (about 29% decline), with 9% share of Q4 revenue. Caustic volumes fell YoY due to membrane change at Mettur, though they improved sequentially from Karaikal.

segments.name: Suspension PVC (CCVL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR661 crores, up 18% YoY from INR560 crores, 53% of Q4 revenue. Spreads are near breakeven on replacement cost; Chinese carbide PVC at about $820/t CFR India is pressuring prices.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the commodity business including CCVL to face a volatile near-term environment in FY27, while expecting stronger performance in specialty.
Management hopes the 7.5% customs duty on PVC returns at end-June 2026; it said this could add about $60-70 per tonne to realisations.
Anti-dumping duty on paste PVC imports from EU and Japan is expected to be implemented in H1 FY27, pending notification by the Finance Ministry.
R32 capacity expected to reach 14 kt by end of calendar 2026, with commissioning in phases through the year after the 2 kt Mettur swing plant started commercial production.
Custom manufacturing revenue target of about INR1,000 crores now expected next financial year, roughly 12 months behind plan according to Dr. Rangachari.
Management said the CCVL INR150 crore inventory write-down is expected to reverse in the current financial year.
capex_capacity: R32 refrigerant gas: 2 kt swing plant at Mettur has started commercial production; expansion to 14 kt targeted by end of calendar 2026, with design provisions for further debottlenecking.
Paste PVC at Cuddalore operated at 100% of capacity in FY26; paste PVC capacity was expanded last year.
MPB 3 Phase III expansion in custom manufacturing is progressing as planned; 45-plus molecules in the pipeline, of which 17 are commercial.
R32 quota: management said the allocation is expected by 2027, with the baseline survey running to end-2026. It is not yet confirmed.

demand_pricing: Domestic suspension PVC demand fell about 1% in FY26 from roughly 4.3 million tonnes; management expects stable to marginally higher demand and a recovery one to two quarters after geopolitical stabilisation.
Chinese carbide PVC is priced around $820/t CFR India, while FOB Japan VCM lands at about $755-760/t, leaving SPVC margins at variable cost.
Paste PVC demand held steady from footwear, with healthy automotive and upholstery traction. Imports from EU declined after ADD findings.
Agrochemical slowdown led to deferred custom manufacturing sales; management says innovator demand has not been hit by generic pricing but new molecule launches are ramping more slowly.
Caustic soda prices spiked after the war began and are now normalising; chloromethane and hydrogen peroxide volumes were constrained by lower caustic output.

qa_highlights.question: Are SPVC spreads still weak and could FY27 remain stressful for CCVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said spreads are at neutral replacement cost, with VCM prices softening slightly. It acknowledged a couple more onerous contracts hit production in May-June and called FY27 a pessimistic-case risk, while Chinese producers are also under cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the impairment taken and what cash-flow outlook underpins it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impairment reflects the current view with no regulatory support. At today's prices, margins are only covering variable costs; the impairment would be reviewed periodically if conditions improve.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR150 crore exceptional item and how will Q1 be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: It is the gap between actual cost and net realisable value at 31 March, expected to reverse in Q1 FY27. One or two more consignments could carry small contribution differences, and the business is roughly breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: Is the government likely to restore the 7.5% duty, and what other measures are in play?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry bodies are pushing for the duty to return at end-June. They are also seeking minimum import prices and QCO reinstatement; ADD is seen as the only long-term WTO-compliant solution.

qa_highlights.question: Has an ADD application on Chinese PVC been filed?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet. Data is being compiled and filing is expected in the near future.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R32 export strategy and quota status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is working with partners on export sales; domestic and export are both planned. It expects a quota allocation by 2027 and said the baseline survey runs to end-2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the custom manufacturing and LOI-backed revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify total LOI value. Six LOIs have been signed out of 17 commercial molecules, and the INR1,000 crore target is retained for next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mandate of the independent director committee?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a broad review of portfolio reorganisation and M&A opportunities. Specialty capital allocation remains the priority, and no outcome has been predetermined.

543336|2026-06.headline: Chemplast Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA loss of INR115 crores on INR1,125 crores revenue; net loss INR176 crores on VCM high-cost inventory.
543336|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose to INR1,125 crores from INR1,100 crores a year earlier, but input cost spikes from the Middle East disruption drove an EBITDA loss of INR115 crores and a net loss of INR176 crores. Management attributed the loss mainly to high-priced VCM inventory booked around March-April, which it says will be consumed by July-August. Specialty chemicals (CMCD) volumes grew 21% YoY and the segment is described as recovering, while Suspension PVC and caustic/chloromethane remained under price pressure. Management expects spreads near $160/t from September onward, with the Karaikal PVC plant offline after a 17 July fire.

segments.name: Suspension PVC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR569 crores vs INR608 crores YoY; prices fell in April after duty exemption let Chinese imports surge, and demand softened seasonally. Management guides spread to ~$160/t (India, replacement basis) from September.

segments.name: Paste PVC
segments.commentary: Realisations about $200/t above Suspension PVC per management; Cuddalore 7,000 t debottlenecking on track for October 2026 commissioning.

segments.name: Specialty / CMCD
segments.commentary: Volumes up 21% YoY on revenue of INR427 crores; 14 molecules commercial out of ~50 in pipeline; INR1,000 crore revenue target reiterated as on track. MPB-3 Phase 3 and pilot Phase 3 commissioned; utilisation ex-new assets ~60-70%.

segments.name: Refrigerant gas (R32)
segments.commentary: Commercial production started May 2026 from swing plant; full 14,000 t capacity expected online by end of FY27 per management, with ramp-up in Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Value-added chemicals (caustic, chloromethane, H2O2)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR129 crores vs INR138 crores; lower output due to planned caustic membrane changeover; caustic pricing under pressure from weak demand and excess supply.

R32: 14,000 t capacity targeted online by end of FY27; swing plant commercial production from May 2026.
Caustic soda capacity 120,000 t, operating range 100-120k t given electrolyser ageing.

Agchem market subdued with generic competition from China; management says demand on commercialised molecules remains healthy but some ramp-ups delayed by a quarter.
Caustic soda and chloromethane prices under pressure from weak regional demand and excess supply; hydrogen peroxide volumes up sequentially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VCM sourcing situation and would the company partially shut the plant given negative economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement VCM ~$700/t delivered vs PVC ~$900+/t, a $150-160 spread; management is evaluating alternate VCM sources and expects VCM prices to soften further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 PVC-VCM spread and what spread is needed for EBITDA and PBT breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 spread was negative (VCM ~$1,000+/t landed vs realisation ~$700-750/t). EBITDA neutral needs ~$120-130/t; PBT positive needs another $20-30/t.

543401|2026-06.headline: Go Fashion Q1 FY27: EBITDA before exceptionals down 2% to INR67.4 crores on marketing spend, while EBO SSSG turned positive at 0.6%.
543401|2026-06.overview: Revenue was flat YoY at about INR223 crores with gross margin of 62.9%, and EBITDA before exceptional items was INR67.4 crores (30.3% margin), down 2%. Management attributed the EBITDA moderation mainly to higher marketing spend, including the brand ambassador partnership. A one-off exceptional charge of INR6.5 crores was booked for write-off of capex on 66 closed stores, and PAT was about INR16 crores. Management presented the quarter as early progress against five FY27 priorities but repeatedly cautioned that one quarter does not make a trend.

segments.name: EBO (company-operated stores)
segments.commentary: SSSG +0.6% and same cluster sales growth +1.2%; footfall up about 1-1.5% YoY per bill cuts. Stores above 700 sq ft delivered SSSG of roughly 2.5%-3%, over 130 such stores.

segments.name: LFS (large format stores, Reliance Trends channel)
segments.commentary: Grew 2% YoY to INR50 crores after a difficult FY26; management says supply-chain disruption with a key LFS partner in Q3-Q4 FY26 has largely normalised.

segments.name: Everyday wear (daily wear concept)
segments.commentary: 15 stores live; 12-13 stated as profitable, with about 12 double-digit EBITDA positive. Sales around INR1,000 per sq ft per month. Target of 25-30 stores by end FY27. Size requirement 1,500-2,000 sq ft.

guidance_outlook: Store footprint: square feet to rise about 8%-10% on a year-through basis in FY27, back-ended; closures expected to be much lower than in recent quarters, though no store-count guidance given.
Advertising spend to stay within 2%-3% of revenue in FY27.
Everyday wear stores targeted at 25-30 by end FY27, from 15 today; 10-12 new product refreshes planned for FY27.
Company-level inventory days expected at 90-100 by year-end, including daily wear; working capital days have room to improve by a few days.
Capex to be funded through internal accruals; new large stores assumed 15-20 month payback and 45-60 days inventory on sales.
Fabric costs up 7%-10%; management is not taking price hikes now and expects gross margin pressure in coming quarters, magnitude not quantified.
capex_capacity: Store network: 66 stores closed in Q1, reducing retail space by 7,000 sq ft; further larger-format stores to be added in catchments where small stores are closed.
Plan to expand footprint over five years with potential to double square feet deployed, across Tier 1, 2 and 3 cities.
New store unit economics: payback 15-20 months, inventory turns 45-60 days on sales for larger stores.
Exceptional INR6.5 crores capex write-off linked to store closures in Q1.
Lingerie and ladies innerwear under evaluation as an addition to the daily wear concept.
demand_pricing: EBO SSSG +0.6% in Q1; management attributes it to possibly a weak base, transfer of sales from closed stores, and better Q1 footfalls, and says it is too early to call a trend.
Full price sales 94%; ASP about INR863.
Fabric cost inflation of 7%-10% linked to Middle East disruption; no price hikes taken yet.
Brand ambassador Shraddha Kapoor onboarded from July 2026 to target a younger audience.
Management said malls and high streets show no real outlier in SSSG, and older 700+ sq ft stores show a similar trend.

qa_highlights.question: What net retail area growth is expected in FY27, and is it back-ended?
qa_highlights.answer: Square feet deployed to rise about 8%-10% on a 12-month basis; the quarter alone saw a 7,000 sq ft reduction, and the increase will come over the year.

qa_highlights.question: What would SSSG look like excluding closed or to-be-closed stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported SSSG excludes stores closed in Q1 but not future closures. 700+ sq ft stores grew about 2.5%-3%; management could not give a clean ex-closures figure and attributed the 0.6% to base effects, transfers and footfall.

qa_highlights.question: How many more store closures in FY27 and how far through is the process?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance; closures depend on large-store opportunities but are expected to be much lower than in recent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much have raw material costs risen?
qa_highlights.answer: Fabric costs up 7%-10%; no price hike currently, and gross margin impact is hard to quantify given older inventory, though it is expected to hit coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are SSSG trends by store vintage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no clean vintage correlation; some FY18 stores grew about 10% while some FY24 stores declined. Detailed bucket data to be sent later through SGA.

qa_highlights.question: How are everyday wear stores performing?
qa_highlights.answer: 15 stores live; about 12-13 profitable and 12 double-digit EBITDA positive; INR1,000 per sq ft monthly sales; actual size requirement 1,500-2,000 sq ft.

Inventory of INR245 crores and 139 working capital days; target to reduce inventory days to 90-100.

543401|2026-09.headline: Go Fashion Q2 FY27 revenue fell 3% YoY to Rs 218 crore; gross margin 60.8% and SSSG roughly flat amid festive shift and RM inflation.
543401|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue declined 3% YoY to Rs 218 crore as the festive season shifted into October, with LFS dispatches moving out of September. Gross margin fell to 60.8% as higher-cost fabric inventory flowed through; management estimates a 200 bps hit in Q2 and 100-200 bps again in Q3. EBITDA before exceptionals was Rs 56 crore (25.8% margin) and PAT was Rs 9 crore. Store network consolidation continued: 23 closures and 9 openings in Q2, taking the EBO count to 737 with total retail area up to about 4.4 lakh sq ft. Management guided to lower closures and price hikes from post-festive, but gave no formal guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Q2 impact of about 200 bps from RM inflation (management estimate)
Store-closure capex write-offs; H1 FY26 was Rs 1.73 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow pre-Ind AS 116 (H1 FY27)

segments.name: EBO (company-operated stores)
segments.commentary: Same-store sales growth broadly flat in Q2 after +0.6% in Q1; 737 EBOs across 196 cities. Stores above 750 sq ft reportedly at +2-3% SSSG while smaller stores are negative; average EBO size about 608 sq ft.

segments.name: LFS (large format stores)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue hit by festive timing, with dispatches moved from September to October. LFS was about 23% of H1 FY27 sales; management says supply chain is normalised.

segments.name: Dailywear concept
segments.commentary: 21 operational stores vs 15 in Q1, with a target of 25-30 by end FY27 (8-9 more planned). Management cites about Rs 1,000 sales per sq ft per month as a benchmark.

segments.name: Online / quick commerce / Amazon
segments.commentary: Online receivables rose after quick commerce and Amazon SOR tie-ups began from March; receivables rose from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore.

guidance_outlook: SSSG target: positive for FY27 as a whole; management says it is 'keeping fingers crossed' and Q3 'should deliver a good number'.
Gross margin: 100-200 bps impact expected in Q3 FY27; margins expected to stabilise over the next 2 quarters as calibrated price hikes offset RM costs.
Store closures: Q3 closures visibility at 15-20 stores, sharply lower than Q1 (58-59) and Q2 (23); management says closures will 'considerably' decline in H2.
Dailywear: target of 25-30 stores by end FY27.
Inventory days to remain within the 90-100 day range guided earlier in the year.
Long term: about 2x square footage over the next 5 years, COCO model retained; bottomwear stores to move to 700-900 sq ft.
capex_capacity: Retail area about 4.4 lakh sq ft at 30 Sep 2026, up from 4.34 lakh at 31 Mar 2026 (about 14,220 sq ft added in H1 despite net closures).
H1 FY27 openings 24 and closures 89; Q2 openings 9 and closures 23.
Store renovations undertaken in H1 (a couple of stores), included in other expenses; value not disclosed.
Men's and women's topwear pilot: 21 stores above 1,500 sq ft; plan to add 8-9 more to test the topwear format.
demand_pricing: Festive timing shifted; management says a portion of pre-festive demand moved from September to October. Festive season started decently; 49 days to festive used as the leading indicator.
Price hikes taken on certain articles recently, with more planned post-festive; ASP for EBOs Rs 827 (H1). Management says ASP rise of 6% is mainly product mix, not price.
Fabric/yarn costs up 8-10% blended, after the geopolitical situation; management had expected cooling in Jul-Aug but prices stayed high.
Full-price sales ratio 93% in H1 FY27.
Value-added non-leggings portfolio now 70% of revenue; new bottomwear products in the Rs 800-900 price band.
Shraddha Kapoor brand campaign went live in Q2 (ambassador from July); effect to be assessed after the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Why have costs not fallen after closing about 75 net stores YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost was flat at about Rs 46.3 crore in Q2 vs Rs 45.75 crore a year ago, after April increments. Rent was about Rs 37 crore vs Rs 36 crore. Advertising rose to Rs 12.63 crore in H1 from Rs 7.85 crore, and exceptional write-offs rose to Rs 9.87 crore from Rs 1.73 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company taking price hikes to offset cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Some hikes have been taken and more are planned post-festive. Management expects margin offset to take a couple of quarters, with stabilisation in the next 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will closures slow down, and will H2 be better than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said closures will be considerably lower from Q3 (15-20 stores visible), and Q3 should deliver a good YoY number. On whether FY27 SSSG turns positive, management said it was 'keeping fingers crossed'.

qa_highlights.question: How much new-cost inventory is flowing through, given the inventory and COGS figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is hard to isolate because products sell at different rates and price hikes are happening. It estimated a 200 bps GM hit in Q2 and 100-200 bps in Q3, and acknowledged older inventory at old prices.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables rose from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore despite lower LFS revenue; why?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase is mainly non-LFS: online receivables from quick commerce and Amazon SOR since March, plus some export receivables for the Dubai store.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the LFS discount jumped to Rs 61 crore in FY26 from Rs 44.5 crore in FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LFS credits are margin-linked (about 5-6% of LFS sales, reconciled in Q4) rather than discounts. It did not confirm the Rs 61 crore figure and promised a clarification note; FY26 LFS decline was due to Q3 supply chain disruption at a large partner.

risks_watch: Gross margin: management expects 100-200 bps pressure in Q3 and says the 200 bps Q2 hit is not a precise figure; the timing of price-hike pass-through is uncertain.

SSSG: Q2 was flat with a festive shift; Q3 needs to be strong for FY27 SSSG to turn positive. Smaller stores (<300 sq ft, roughly 120-150 units) remain negative and 20-30% of the network is seen as problematic.
Competition and store format: management attributes slowdown to store size, not merchandise or competition (Zudio, Westside), but this is not independently verified.
Clarifications pending: store-count split by size (to be shared via SGA), LFS discount quantum (Rs 61 crore vs Rs 44.5 crore), and receivables rise from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore.
Topwear and menswear pilot (21 stores) is unproven; a 8-9 store test is still to come.

543411|2026-03.headline: Hi-Tech Pipes Q4 FY26 volume rose 27% to 1.47 lakh tons and revenue rose 102% to INR1,480 crores, while FY27 volume guidance is 6.5-7 lakh tons.
543411|2026-03.overview: Management reported strong Q4 FY26 volume growth of 27% YoY to 1.47 lakh tons and revenue of INR1,480 crores, up 102% YoY. FY26 volume rose to 5.32 lakh tons from 4.85 lakh tons, and EBITDA grew 8% to INR174 crores. Total comprehensive income in Q4 was INR18 crores against INR17.5 crores a year earlier. Management reiterated a 2 million ton capacity roadmap with 1 million tons to be added by FY29, and the call drew heavy questions on a large stock-in-trade cost line that analysts saw as depressing per-ton margins.

financial_highlights.change: +27% YoY vs 1.16 lakh tons in Q4 FY25
+37% as stated by management (base quoted as INR367 crores, likely a transcription error)
+33% YoY vs INR35 crores (management compared against 'Q4 FY26' in error)
vs INR17.5 crores in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Contribution reached 39% of business mix in FY26; management expects around 50% by end of FY27 as DFT and Hindupur capacity ramp. 300x300 hollow sections were launched during FY26.

segments.name: Stock-in-trade (trading)
segments.commentary: Trading cost was about INR21 crores in Q3 and about INR300 crores in Q4, around INR700 crores across two quarters per the CFO. Management described margins on this as very nominal and said it will decline as the newly operational plants ramp up.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of 6.5-7 lakh tons.
FY28 volume estimate around 8.5 lakh tons, based on 1.4 million tons capacity at 62-65% utilisation (70% peak).
EBITDA per ton of INR3,500-4,000 for FY27 and FY28, assuming no volatility and balanced demand-supply.
Capacity target of around 1.4 million tons by end FY27 and 1.7 million tons exit in FY28; 2 million tons is the longer-term goal, with INR300 crores of capex still needed (INR75-100 crores in FY27).
Value-added share expected to reach around 50% by FY27 end.
capex_capacity: Sanand Unit 2 Phase 3 DFT facility expected operational by Q3 FY27; Sanand APA pipes facility readiness by Q3 FY27 per Q&A (Q4 FY27 per prepared remarks). Oil and gas entry to start with water applications.
Greenfield Hindupur (Andhra Pradesh) facility, about 1.5 lakh tons coated/pre-galvanised/galvanised tubes for solar, expected operational by Q4 FY27; fully integrated for ERW pipes and solar tubes.
Chennai (Sri City) facility on track, expected commissioning in FY27 with full-year benefit in FY28.
FY28 capacity additions: Sanand 1.5 lakh tons, Hindupur 2 lakh tons, Sri City Chennai 1.5 lakh tons, UP plant about 2 lakh tons.
Incremental 1 million ton capex: around INR100 crores already in CWIP; another INR300 crores needed to reach 2 million tons.
Solar capacity 16.5 MW installed, about 35% of power needs; green hydrogen trial started at Secunderabad Unit 1.
demand_pricing: Management cited robust demand across segments including data centres, railways, solar, infrastructure and power projects.
Q4 headwinds: gas price volatility, intermittent gas availability, and elevated ocean freight, creating temporary pressure on input costs and export realisations industry-wide.
Rupee depreciation cited as making Indian exports more competitive; international certifications secured for Europe, America and Middle East.
Management said the stock-in-trade purchases were partly due to geopolitical import cargo and supplier commitment volumes; discounts and rebates would be hit if volumes were not lifted.

qa_highlights.question: Purpose and pricing of the INR90 crore preferential issue to promoters (individual investor).
qa_highlights.answer: Anish Bansal said the INR90 crore issue is by promoters and funds the working capital needs of the 1 million to 2 million ton expansion. No issue price was given in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What products Hindupur will make and the FY27 volume guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Hindupur is a coated steel tube facility of about 1.5 lakh tons, making coated, pre-galvanised and galvanised tubes mainly for solar. FY27 volume target is 6.5-7 lakh tons.

qa_highlights.question: Greenfield vs brownfield split of the extra 1 million tons.
qa_highlights.answer: Sanand is brownfield and Hindupur greenfield, a 50:50 split; capacity reaches about 1.4 million tons by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and approvals for oil and gas (API) pipes.
qa_highlights.answer: Full readiness of the Sanand API unit expected by Q3 FY27 after 1.5 years of equipment installation and testing. Start with water applications, then migrate to oil and gas, with export potential.

qa_highlights.question: Stock-in-trade cost jump and its margins; whether trading continues.
qa_highlights.answer: Stock-in-trade cost was about INR700 crores across Q3 and Q4 per the CFO, covering HRC, CR and galvanised products, with very nominal margins. Management said trading will fall as three newly operational plants (Secunderabad, Gujarat, Jammu) ramp up, and that stock was sold in March to avoid price-volatility losses.

qa_highlights.question: Capex breakdown and FY28 capacity and volume.
qa_highlights.answer: About INR100 crores is in CWIP and INR300 crores more is needed; INR75-100 crores targeted for FY27. FY28 capacity exit about 1.7 million tons, volume around 8.5 lakh tons, EBITDA per ton INR3,500-4,000.

risks_watch: Stock-in-trade purchases (about INR700 crores across Q3-Q4) depress gross margin and per-ton profitability; the company says this will fall as new plants ramp up.
Q4 EBITDA margin per ton (INR3,150) is well below the FY28 guidance of INR3,500-4,000, which assumes stable markets.
Execution risk on Hindupur (Q4 FY27), Chennai (FY27 commissioning), DFT (Q3 FY27) and API readiness (Q3 FY27), with the 2 million ton target spread into FY29.
Energy input costs, gas availability and ocean freight remain volatile.
Transcript inconsistencies (FY26 revenue base, Q4 EBITDA comparison, APA timeline Q3 vs Q4 FY27) should be checked against the filed results.
