543412|2026-03.headline: Star Health Q4 FY26 underwriting profit rose to Rs 186 crore on a 95.7% combined ratio, but reported Q4 PAT was a Rs 55 crore loss on a Rs 558 crore MTM hit.
543412|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 GWP rose 17% YoY (N basis) to Rs 6,259 crore, with fresh retail growing 38% and the loss ratio improving to 65.2% from 69.2%. Full-year GWP crossed Rs 20,000 crore (Rs 20,369 crore, up 16%) and FY26 underwriting profit turned positive at Rs 206 crore versus a Rs 165 crore loss in FY25. Reported Q4 PAT was a Rs 55 crore loss against a Rs 271 crore profit a year earlier, driven by the equity-market MTM loss. Management introduced a normalised investment yield of 8%, under which FY26 PAT was Rs 1,222 crore (up 45%) and ROE 13.1%.

segments.name: Retail Health
segments.commentary: Fresh retail grew 38% YoY in Q4 and 37% for FY26 (N basis); retail policies grew 11% in Q4 and 8% for FY26. Market share was 31.3% in FY26; retail loss ratio 64.8% in Q4 and 68.2% for FY26.

segments.name: Group Health / SME
segments.commentary: Management said SME was 78% of group business in FY26 versus 58% in FY25, with a recalibrated strategy that drove the group loss ratio improvement. No explicit group GWP figure was given.

guidance_outlook: Management targets sustainable high-teen growth and mid-to-high-teen ROE.
Annual price increases will continue across all products; management said no change beyond normal pricing is foreseen, and about 80% of the book is to be repriced from Q4 FY26 through Q1 FY27.
Reporting moves to 1/n basis for business and growth from FY27.
NEP growth is expected to lag GWP growth because of long-term policy sales, with catch-up expected in coming quarters.
Management expects the long-term share of NEP to keep rising next year.
Agent network to reach 1 million in two years, adding about 1 lakh agents a year.
capex_capacity: Home Healthcare, telemedicine and condition management usage rose 4-5x over the year, with Q4 consumption up about 9x. FY26 included over 90,000 telemedicine calls and over 40,000 pure telemedicine calls.
Claims platform migration to the Medi Assist platform is nearly complete, with the last product set to shift by Q1 FY27 end.
Customer app has over 14 million downloads and more than 1.5 million monthly active users; 95% of fresh premium is collected digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail Health premiums grew 30.2% YoY in H2 FY26 versus 11.2% for non-life. For full FY26, retail health grew close to 20% and non-life 9.3%.
New-to-insurance share of fresh premium was 94% in Q4 (90% a year earlier) and 93% for FY26 (89% in FY25).
Volume retention improved 1-1.5% YoY; the company cited about 86-87% volume retention and a renewal ratio of 99%. GWP-based renewal retention rose 300 bps and NOP-based 100 bps.
Agent productivity rose about 37% on fresh and 18% on total business. Over 90% of retail comes from agency and D2C channels.
Senior citizens are about 20% of the portfolio; the senior citizen commission reduction took effect April 2024 (FY25) and drove part of the commission ratio gain.
Long-term vs annual NEP split is about 80:20, moving 100-150 bps toward long-term on premium basis.

qa_highlights.question: How will the retail loss ratio (about 68%) get back to 65-66% levels seen in FY23-24, and how will seasonal vector-borne claims be handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said frequency and severity were managed in the high-single digits for FY26 and that Q4 benefited from lower frequency. It cited telemedicine and home healthcare usage growth and repricing of about 80% of the book from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27, but gave no numerical target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail growth lagging the industry, and how should the gap evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritises quality and profitable geographies over market share. Its market share was 31.3% in FY26, growth on N basis was 39% for FY26, and the company is not chasing share at the cost of profit.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the loss ratio improvement: renewal book, new business, severity or fraud controls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gain is a sum of parts: renewal repricing, sourcing quality, geography selection, and fraud, waste and abuse controls. Q4 frequency improvement cut across the whole book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the retention ratio uptick linked to long-term policies?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the Q3/Q4 retention noise to renewals pulled into September after the GST cut, with some spillover into Q1. Volume retention improved 1-1.5% for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for a major repricing in FY27, and is the current price rise enough for the target combined ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no need for above-normal increases. It expects the current annual pricing strategy to be sufficient to hit the target combined ratio.

qa_highlights.question: How is Bima Sugam expected to affect sourcing and renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bima Sugam is a consumer platform for affordable plans, that it will not be zero-cost, and that Star Health is a shareholder and supportive of it.

qa_highlights.question: Did the GST cut lift renewals and sum insured?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Walia said GWP-based renewal retention rose 300 bps, with customers opting for higher sum insured and riders, and that distributor income had risen over 50% since the GST announcement.

qa_highlights.question: Management did not answer on the EoM regulation's treatment of non-compliant companies and declined to comment on it, saying IRDAI guidance on EoM is awaited.

risks_watch: Retail loss ratio is still about 68% for FY26 versus the 65-66% seen in FY23-24; sustainability of the Q4 frequency improvement across a full cycle is unproven.

NEP growth lagging GWP growth due to long-term policy sales; deferred revenue quantum was not disclosed and will be shared offline.

Group Health volume is being deliberately reduced; the SME mix is rising.

543412|2026-06.headline: Star Health Q1 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 111 crore from Rs 16 crore, with CISR improving to 97% and normalised PAT up 44% to Rs 386 crore.
543412|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed a fourth successive quarter of improving core underwriting profitability, with underwriting result at Rs 111 crore versus Rs 16 crore a year earlier. Reported PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 550 crore, while normalised PAT (8% investment yield basis) rose 44% to Rs 386 crore, giving annualised ROE of 15.6% versus 12.2%. Fresh retail GWP grew 37% YoY to Rs 730 crore on a 1/N basis, but retail market share slipped to 29% from 31%, which management attributed to long-term policy accounting and deliberate avoidance of riskier pools. Management guided insurance revenue growth to rise towards 15-16% and expense ratio to fall 30-40 bps a year, while declining to give loss ratio guidance.

segments.commentary: Group share of GWP is now roughly 2.5%, down from about 5% a year earlier; management said group contributed part of the loss ratio improvement but retail also improved.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C fresh business grew 142% YoY, with 98% of customers new to insurance; D2C is 74% of digital fresh business.

guidance_outlook: Insurance revenue growth is expected to rise from 13.4% towards 15-16% as the quarters progress, and to increase further in FY28.
Expense ratio expected to improve 30-40 bps consistently each year from technology and productivity investments.

Reinsurance cost expected to fall: the voluntary quota share treaty (2023-24 and 2024-25, three-year) is fading out, and obligatory treaty renegotiation with GICRE may bring benefits; FY28 net reinsurance benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%.
Q2 is seasonally higher for loss ratio; management expects the same trend this year. No loss ratio guidance given.

demand_pricing: Fresh growth is partly driven by the GST waiver; majority of fresh business comes from first-time buyers. Management expects moderation of optical growth rates.

Pricing is annual and product-by-product on a calendar; most pricing actions have been taken in Q4 over the last couple of years, with earned impact flowing through subsequent quarters. Management described upcoming pricing as maintenance-level rather than step-up, with some discounts for non-claimants.
Retail claim settlement ratio 91%; over 9.5 lakh claims settled in the quarter, over 80% cashless.
Senior citizens are under 5% of the book; focus remains on younger cohorts.
Management is watching dengue, malaria and fever outbreaks; telemedicine and home healthcare used to manage these cases.

qa_highlights.answer: Insurance revenue grew 13.4%; management expects 15-16% through the year as long-term policy earnings build, and higher growth in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers for loss ratio improvement and how many claims are settled via telemedicine?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combined approach: repricing, portfolio selection, claims fraud control, network management, wellness and teleconsultation. No telemedicine claim count was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the expense ratio improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects 30-40 bps annual expense ratio improvement from tech, digitisation and productivity.

qa_highlights.question: What share of acquisition cost is employee expense and how is it split?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is split three ways: claims-related in claims, sales-related in acquisition cost, and support costs in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reinsurance impact on the expense ratio and what is the full-year benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Reinsurance cost is falling as the quota share treaty fades; FY28 benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%, though management said this was hard to pin down.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth slow in H2 as the GST-driven base builds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that H2 FY27 and early FY28 growth could be lower on the high base, and said it will not chase growth for its own sake.

543412|2026-09.headline: Star Health Q2 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 99 crore from a Rs 40 crore loss, with PAT up over threefold to Rs 265 crore.
543412|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 marked the fifth successive quarter of improving loss ratios and underwriting results, with CISR improving 2.9 points to 98%. Gross written premium on a reported 1/n basis grew 19% YoY to Rs 5,275 crore in Q2 and Rs 9,562 crore in H1, while fresh retail health GWP grew 35% in the quarter. 543415|2026-06.headline: Anand Rathi Wealth Q1 FY27 underlying PAT rose 24% YoY to INR116 crore, with AUM up 21% to INR1,06,300 crore.
543415|2026-06.overview: Management reported its 19th consecutive quarter of profit growth, with underlying consolidated revenue (excluding fair value gains, ESOP and related tax) up 18% YoY to INR336 crore and PAT up 24% to INR116 crore, a 34.4% margin. Reported revenue and PAT including fair value gains were INR430 crore and INR163 crore, with INR96 crore of the other income being mark-to-market gain on the Anand Rathi Global Finance (ARGFL) holding. Net flows were INR2,743 crore in the quarter, and client attrition was 0.09% of AUM with zero RM attrition. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,415 crore revenue and INR460 crore PAT, with Q1 delivering 24% and 25% of these respectively. The call also covered a Board approval to apply for an AMC licence, a UK subsidiary, and a GIFT City licence in progress.

segments.commentary: AUM INR1,06,300 crore, 13,941 client families after net addition of 1,600+ in last 12 months; client AUM attrition 0.09% in Q1 and zero RM attrition. AUM per RM described as rising, with 33 clients per RM.

qa_highlights.answer: Platinum families are about 230 vs 211 earlier, from 40-45 at launch about 2.5 years ago; upgrade rate estimated at 10-20% a quarter; management expects four-digit client counts in a few years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cap on AUM per RM?
qa_highlights.answer: No cap; management says AUM per RM should keep rising while client attrition stays low (0.09%), and some RMs have reached INR500-1,500 crore. The figure was INR100 crore at listing.

qa_highlights.question: How is asset allocation managed in volatile markets and why not recommend gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the highest portfolio beta is 0.6-0.65 and it sells products it buys; it does not recommend gold given household gold holdings of about 28% of savings. Overall mix is about INR55,000 crore equity and INR4,500 crore debt plus structured products.

qa_highlights.answer: INR96 crore is mark-to-market gain on ARGFL holding, revalued semi-annually by a third-party investment banker; the rest is interest on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is there yield pressure from TER changes in mutual funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through is limited to 1-3 bps of its roughly 1.09% post-GST yield, and scale gives bargaining power; it has no plans to recommend stocks, PMS or long-only AIFs currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will ARWL enter investment banking or other capital market businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will pursue only an AMC licence and no investment banking, focusing on intergenerational wealth rather than transaction-driven capital management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM growth plan and how is it sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% AUM growth from embedded client returns, capacity in existing RMs, new RMs and penetration, citing 90-95% confidence; the 4% Category II target implies 22-23% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI bank guarantee circular on derivatives volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views the circular as positive, expecting reduced high-frequency trading volumes, and sees negligible or positive impact on ARWL.

543419|2026-03.headline: Shriram Properties FY26 revenue rose 39% to INR1,357 crores and net profit crossed INR100 crores for the first time, with FY27 guidance of INR3,300-3,500 crores sales value.
543419|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,357 crores (+39% YoY) and net profit rose 30% to INR101 crores, driven by a strong Q4 handover push in Bangalore, Chennai and Kolkata. Full-year sales value was flat at INR2,354 crores, with Q4 sales of INR663 crores, as several launches slipped due to approval delays, mainly in Bangalore. Management guided FY27 to be stronger than FY26, with sales value of INR3,300-3,500 crores, collections of INR2,100-2,200 crores and handovers of 3,750-3,800 units. Analysts pressed on margins, the rising other-expense line, the cash flow trend, and the funding of new land acquisitions; management said these would be funded from completed-project cash flows and possibly intermittent debt.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: Core market; Songs of the Earth launch sold over 85% in launch year. Management says the growth strategy is centred on Bangalore and Pune, with North Bangalore flagged for higher pricing upside.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Maiden launch at Undri (Spectrum) sold over 300 units in under a year, against roughly 850 units absorbed annually by the micro-market over the last three years. Pune revenue is recognised under percentage-of-completion.

segments.name: Kolkata
segments.commentary: Land settlement with the Government of West Bengal done; 314 acres originally, 42 acres surrendered, 100+ acres still available. Skyblooms Villas over 50% sold and Signature Square about 40% sold at launch. Approval exists for 2.3 million sq ft of apartments, with plotted development planned.

segments.name: Chennai
segments.commentary: Contributed to Q4 revenue recognition from completed projects; a launch is expected within about a week of the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume guidance of 5-5.5 million sq ft and sales value of INR3,300-3,500 crores.
FY27 collections of INR2,100-2,200 crores and handovers of 3,750-3,800 units.
FY27 pipeline addition of 7-8 million sq ft and GDV addition of INR5,000-6,000 crores; land-related capital commitment of INR350-400 crores.
FY27 project completions of about 3.8 million sq ft, with revenue recognition potential of about INR1,740 crores.
Mission FY28 targets: sales of INR5,000 crores, revenue of INR2,500 crores and PBT of INR250 crores; management reiterated PBT margin of 10-11%.
Management expects 8-9% PAT margin on a normalised 3-year basis, with the effective tax rate below 25% due to carried-forward losses.
Construction capital spend of INR900-1,000 crores expected in FY27, versus roughly INR90-95 crores per quarter recently.
Finance costs may decline slightly, but gross debt of about INR600 crores will continue; the company may take intermittent bridge debt.
capex_capacity: Ongoing projects: 16.7 million sq ft, 85% sold; 2.6 million sq ft unsold in ongoing projects, plus 18.6 million sq ft upcoming pipeline; total unsold potential over 21 million sq ft, GDV about INR13,950 crores.
Seven projects acquired during FY26; approvals under way; over 7 million sq ft expected to enter the launch pipeline in the next 3-6 months. Target to double the upcoming pipeline in 18-24 months.
FY26 completed and delivered 8 projects, about 4 million sq ft. FY27 target of about 6 million sq ft launches across Bangalore, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata.

New business development investment of INR372 crores in FY26, one of the highest annual outlays; about 80% of cumulative operating cash of over INR900 crores over four years was reinvested into new projects.
Liquidity of over INR520 crores: cash of INR172 crores plus undrawn funding lines of INR358 crores. Equity about INR1,460 crores; cost of debt 11.2%; CRISIL A-/Positive.
demand_pricing: FY26 sales value INR2,354 crores (marginal increase); sales volume 4.15 million sq ft; Q4 sales INR663 crores. Management said a couple of Q4 launches slipped into Q1 FY27.

Pricing: management expects organic price growth of no more than 5-6% a year, against 8-10% construction cost inflation; margin protection rather than expansion is the aim. Tiles, paints and PVC windows face 5-10% price pressure.
Management flagged IT employment trends, interest rate affordability and longer sales cycles as sector risks; focus is on mid and upper-mid housing.
Kolkata: management said the new state government is positive. Long-term outlook strong, but near-term recovery expected to be slower than Bangalore or Pune.
Competition: management said the market favours branded and organised developers.

qa_highlights.question: Will rising operating cash outflows and higher new-project investment lead to a cash crunch or more debt?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said FY26 free cash flow fell slightly due to construction spend ahead of finishing stages; no additional debt is needed for construction, as liquidity is sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR126 crores to INR172 crores, and will they rise further in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said higher accelerated revenue recognition (about INR1,200 crores vs about INR800 crores) brought about INR25 crores of brokerage charges, with INR7 crores impairment on Bengal land and INR10 crores of provisions; he said other expenses should not rise in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What PBT and PAT margins should be assumed?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said PBT margin of 10-11% is the target; PAT margin is expected to be 8-9% on a normalised 3-year basis, because the effective tax rate may be below 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 presales slightly below the INR2,600 crore guidance, and why are there few Kolkata launches?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said a couple of projects slipped into Q1 FY27, with one launched that week and another in Chennai in about a week. Kolkata plotted development is being tested before the remaining 100+ acres are monetised; 2.3 million sq ft of apartment approval is already in hand.

qa_highlights.question: When will construction spend ramp up, and how much new project investment is planned in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said construction capital spend is expected at INR900-1,000 crores in FY27. The 8 million sq ft pipeline addition implies INR350-400 crores of land commitment, to be funded from completed-project cash flows and possibly bridge debt.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR4,000 crore revenue recognition potential over three years conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said ongoing projects alone can deliver about INR4,400 crores, to be unlocked in 2-3 years. Upside exists from Kolkata and the pipeline, but management preferred conservative guidance.

risks_watch: Approval delays (approvals, e-Khata, OCs, Kaveri portal) that caused FY26 launch slippage and could affect FY27 launches of about 6 million sq ft.
Other expenses (INR172 crores) and provisions, including the INR10 crore recoverable from a landowner; management said these should not rise in FY27.
Operating cash flow fell YoY, and construction capex is set to rise to INR900-1,000 crores in FY27; monitor collections against the INR2,100-2,200 crore guidance.
Rising material costs (tiles, paints, PVC) and limited ability to pass on price increases beyond 5-6%.
Finance costs and net debt; management said gross debt of about INR600 crores will stay and bridge debt may be taken.
Q1 FY27 launch execution: Chennai project and Kolkata plotted development.
543419|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 recovery and FY27 visibility, but deliberately conservative on guidance because of geopolitical, consumer confidence and IT employment uncertainty. Management said upside exists if conditions improve, and it declined to commit to exact numbers beyond the stated FY27 KPI ranges.
key_quotes: Therefore, while we remain cautious in the near term in terms of our guidance to the market on FY '27 KPIs, we are fully geared to seize the opportunities in the market and sustain our growth momentum in FY '27 and beyond.

Margin protection is real. Margin enhancement happens only through new project -- new micro portfolio upgrades where you enter better micro markets or launch projects in new micro market, which have a higher pricing potential.
But for now, I think it will be better to be conservative than saying something which is very big and then pulling back.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management aims for margin protection rather than expansion, with organic price growth capped at 5-6% against 8-10% construction cost inflation and tiles, paints and PVC facing 5-10% price pressure; FY26 EBITDA was flat at INR177 crore despite revenue up 39%, and other expenses rose from INR126 crore to INR172 crore.

rows.why: Seven projects acquired in FY26 with over 7 million sq ft expected to enter launch pipeline in 3-6 months, and FY27 target of about 6 million sq ft launches across Bangalore, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata; approvals still under way and FY26 launches slipped on approval delays.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 sales volume guided at 5-5.5 million sq ft versus 4.15 million sq ft in FY26, about 20-33% higher, and handovers of 3,750-3,800 units backed by 3.8 million sq ft of completions.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management guided INR350-400 crore land-related capital commitment for FY27 and INR372 crore new business development investment in FY26, with construction capital spend rising to INR900-1,000 crore versus about INR90-95 crore per quarter recently; utilisation is not a metric for a developer, so the call rests on the land pipeline.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management was deliberately conservative, with ongoing projects alone able to deliver about INR4,400 crore of revenue recognition potential over 2-3 years versus the INR4,000 crore three-year figure, and said upside exists if conditions improve.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Launches already slipped in FY26 (Q4 presales INR663 crore below INR2,600 crore-run-rate expectation, couple of launches moved to Q1 FY27) and approvals remain a gating item for about 6 million sq ft of FY27 launches; management flagged geopolitical, consumer confidence and IT hiring risks.

rows.why: Chennai launch expected within a week of the call and FY27 target of about 6 million sq ft of launches across Bangalore, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata, including Kolkata plotted development being tested.

rows.label: FY27 sales value guidance INR3,300-3,500 crore
rows.why: Versus INR2,354 crore in FY26 (about 40-49% higher), backed by 85% sold in ongoing projects and 2.6 million sq ft unsold, though sales value was flat in FY26 and launches slipped.

rows.why: Management said gross debt of about INR600 crore continues and intermittent bridge debt may be taken to fund INR900-1,000 crore construction spend and INR350-400 crore land commitments; net debt INR438 crore, D/E 0.3x, liquidity over INR520 crore.

rows.label: Collections guidance INR2,100-2,200 crore
rows.why: Versus INR1,661 crore collected in FY26 (+12% YoY, all-time high), about 26-32% higher, while FY26 operating cash flow of INR271 crore declined YoY.
